confirmed.title: Wholesale `state.entities = allAlive` discards entities appended to state.entities during the tick (trade-caravan carrier)
confirmed.evidence: gameTick.ts:105 `const aliveEntities = state.entities.filter((e) => e.alive);` then 206-212 build `allAlive` from that pre-tick snapshot plus `newEntities`, and 234 `state.entities = allAlive;`. `spawnCaravan` (called from the systems layer via tickLayerSystems.ts:142 -> tickTradeCaravans -> spawnCaravan) instead does tradeCaravans.ts:246 `state.entities.push(carrier);` (plus `indexLivingEntity`), which is in neither list. gameTick.ts:224-226 documents the contract: 'Daily systems may append authoritative entities through ctx.newEntities'.
confirmed.impact: `state.entities = allAlive` silently deletes the carrier at the end of the departure tick, so `hasActiveCarrier` (tradeCaravans.ts:256-259, `state.entities.some(...)`) is false on the very next systems pulse; because `spawnCaravan` returned true, `route.nextDepartureTick` was cleared (tradeCaravans.ts:275-277), so the route re-schedules a fresh departure ~8 days later (`scheduleTradeRouteDeparture`, EVENT_INTERVAL.tradeRoute). Every departure first calls `deductExports(state, route)` (tradeCaravans.ts:231) after `canAffordExports`, so the colony loses the route's wood/stone/food/gold every 8 days forever: no carrier ever walks, `applyImports` (tradeCaravans.ts:336) never runs, `caravansCompleted`/`tradeCaravansCompleted`/`goldFromTradeRoutes` never increase, and no refund is possible. `getCaravanMoveTarget`/`tryAdvanceCaravanLeg` (humanTick.ts:445) are dead code as a result.
confirmed.fix: Spawn the carrier through the documented tick-layer contract: give `tickTradeCaravans(state, ctx)` and `spawnCaravan(state, ctx, route)` the TickContext and replace `state.entities.push(carrier); indexLivingEntity(state, carrier);` with `pushNewEntity(state, ctx, carrier);` (simulationEntities.ts:17-27 already registers entityById/grids; keep `indexLivingEntity` if the persistent index is still needed). Alternatively, make gameTick preserve untracked in-tick spawns, but the ctx.newEntities path is the one every other spawner uses (simulationEntities.ts:26, dailyPopulation.ts:112-114, tickLayerSystems.ts:133).
confirmed.verification: Reproduced by driving real gameTick() ticks with an active route: on the systems tick spawnCaravan ran (wood 500→499) but `state.entities.filter(e => e.faction === 'trade_caravan')` was empty at the end of that same tick, and on the next systems tick hasActiveCarrier (tradeCaravans.ts:236) was false so the route reset with nextDepartureTick +576 — exports burned, applyImports (line 314) unreachable. gameTick.ts:234 replaces state.entities with `allAlive`, built only from the line-105 pre-systems snapshot plus ctx.newEntities; spawnCaravan pushes straight into state.entities, unlike dailyPopulation.ts:102-114, which pushes into state.entities, allAlive AND ctx.newEntities. Minimal fix: pass ctx into spawnCaravan and create the carrier through pushNewEntity(state, ctx, carrier) (matching the migration.ts BUG-12 comment), or merge in-tick appends into allAlive before line 234.

confirmed.title: YearlyStats.deaths subtracts a per-year count from a cumulative dead-entity count
confirmed.evidence:
stats.ts:104 `humans: entities.filter(e => e.type === ET.Human && !e.alive && e.age > 0).length - (prevYearStats?.deaths.humans || 0),`
stats.ts:107 `).length - (prevYearStats?.deaths.animals || 0),`
stats.ts:132 `s.totalHumansDied = state.entities.filter(e => e.type === ET.Human && !e.alive).length;`
gameTick.ts:206-208 `const allAlive: Entity[] = [];` / `for (const e of aliveEntities) {` / `if (e.alive) allAlive.push(e);` then gameTick.ts:234 `state.entities = allAlive;`
confirmed.impact: gameTick rebuilds `state.entities` from alive entities only, so by the time `recordYearlyStats` runs at the year-rollover tick (gameTick.ts:83) the world array contains no `!alive` entity. `YearlyStats.deaths.humans`/`deaths.animals` are therefore always 0 and `lifetimeStats.totalHumansDied` is always 0, which is what StatisticsPanel.tsx:43 renders as "Humans Died" — the lifetime records panel reports 0 deaths forever. (Line 104 also subtracts the previous year's *delta* from a cumulative-looking count; both sides are 0 today, so the unit mismatch is currently masked.) The same alive-only snapshot makes `births.humans` (line 70) miss any child who died in its birth year.
confirmed.fix: Record deaths where they happen: increment a persistent counter at the death owner (e.g. in killHuman / the animal death helper) and derive both the per-year value and `totalHumansDied` from that counter (deltas), instead of scanning `state.entities` for `!e.alive`; e.g. in `updateLifetimeStats` replace line 132 with `s.totalHumansDied += latestYear?.deaths.humans ?? 0;` once the yearly value comes from the counter.
confirmed.verification: The cited formula is exactly as reported, and the left operand is structurally always 0 because state.entities only ever holds living entities when recordYearlyStats runs: gameTick.ts:234 assigns allAlive, simDelta.ts:498 assigns aliveEntities, and saveLoad.ts:400 forces `alive: true` on load, so `deaths.humans` is 0 - previous = 0 in every year (inductively always 0). The impact narrative is overstated, though: a repo-wide grep finds no reader of YearlyStats.deaths (not even the UI), so the defect is a stored, always-zero stat rather than a visible wrong outcome — hence low. Minimal fix: own a cumulative death counter where deaths are recorded (killHuman/finalizeHumanDeath) and compute the per-year delta from it.

confirmed.title: tryGraduateHumanChild is unreachable: the daily age sync clears isJuvenile before the graduation check, so no child ever graduates
confirmed.evidence: dayCycle.ts:135 `if (!entity.isJuvenile || entity.age < HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS) return false;` — but dayCycle.ts:246 in the sync that runs first sets `entity.isJuvenile = entity.age < HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS;`, and humanTick.ts runs the sync at line 300 (`syncHumanAgeFromCalendar(entity, state, {...})`) before the check at line 360 (`tryGraduateHumanChild(entity, config.size, config.speed, (e) => { if (isPlayerHuman(e)) applyEducationGraduation(state, e); });`).
confirmed.impact: `computeHumanAgeYears` returns 12 exactly when daysLived reaches juvenileSpan, and line 246 immediately sets isJuvenile=false, so on the only tick where age>=HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS the guard's `!entity.isJuvenile` clause is already true and the body never runs. No human is ever incremented out of juvenile by this function (only setHumanBirthFromAge/syncHumanAgeFromCalendar ever write isJuvenile — verified by grep; tickLayerSystems.ts:227 only handles WILDLIFE_TICK_TYPES, which excludes Human). Consequence: `applyEducationGraduation` (only other reference is its definition, education.ts:125) is never called, so `entity.educated` is never set — schoolDays accumulated as a juvenile never convert to skill/energy bonuses, no 'Graduation' notification/event ever fires, and `getEducationResearchMultiplier` (education.ts:155) can never count an educated settler. `entity.size` also stays at the juvenile 0.5x value set in entityFactory.ts:110 (today the renderer derives human scale from isJuvenile, so this is latent rather than visible).
confirmed.fix: Let the graduation transition own the flag: in `syncHumanAgeFromCalendar` (dayCycle.ts:246) stop clearing `isJuvenile` and instead pass the new age to the promotion owner — e.g. make the sync return `wasJuvenile && !isNowJuvenile`, or delete line 246 and have `tryGraduateHumanChild` (called every tick from humanTick.ts:360) clear `isJuvenile` together with size/speed and the `onGraduate` callback. Do not simply drop the `!entity.isJuvenile` clause, or every adult would re-run the callback each tick.
confirmed.verification: Verified by running gameTick on a settler born 359.7 days earlier with schoolDays=20: at the day boundary age became 12 and isJuvenile false (syncHumanAgeFromCalendar via humanTick.ts:300 → dayCycle.ts:245-246) while `educated` stayed undefined, and a later direct tryGraduateHumanChild call returned false. The two guard clauses are mutually exclusive because entity.age only reaches HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS through that same sync (grep: isJuvenile is written only by setHumanBirthFromAge, syncHumanAgeFromCalendar, tryGraduate, finalizeSettlerAge and migrateHumanAges), so applyEducationGraduation (education.ts:125) is dead and `educated` is never set. Minimal fix: let the graduation transition own the flag — remove the isJuvenile write at dayCycle.ts:246 (have the sync report the transition) and let tryGraduateHumanChild, called every tick from humanTick.ts:360, clear isJuvenile/size/speed with the callback exactly once.

confirmed.title: Construction-builder picker omits alive/pregnant and ignores addToConstructionCrew's rejection
confirmed.evidence:
(entity) =>
      isPlayerHuman(entity)
      && !entity.isJuvenile
      && !hasWorkAssignment(entity)      // lines 88-91 — no `entity.alive`, no `!entity.pregnant`
      && !isImprisoned(entity)
confirmed.impact: isPlayerHuman (playerHuman.ts:12-17) is a type/faction predicate and does not test `alive` or `pregnant`. Every other crew/job path excludes pregnancy — workforce.isEligibleIdleWorker (workforce.ts:58-68), assignWorkerTransition (workforce.ts:202) and assignBuilderInPlace (workforce.ts:399-409) — and addToConstructionCrew itself does not check pregnancy (workforce.ts:234-242), so the manual 'assign builder' command (assignBuilderToBuilding -> _applyBuilderAssignmentMut) can put a pregnant settler on a construction crew where auto-staffing never would. The same filter gap can select a dead settler: addToConstructionCrew returns false silently (workforce.ts:236) while lines 103-109 still announce 'Builder Assigned'.
confirmed.fix: Match the sibling filters: add `&& entity.alive && !entity.pregnant` to the pickAdultSettler predicate at lines 88-95 (or enforce both inside addToConstructionCrew and return a status the caller checks before notifying).
confirmed.verification: The predicate at L88-94 indeed lacks `entity.alive` and `!entity.pregnant`, which isEligibleIdleWorker (L58-68), canAssignWorkerToBuilding's incomplete branch (L322-330) and assignBuilderInPlace (workforce.ts:399-409) all have, and addToConstructionCrew (workforce.ts:234-242) does not check pregnancy either — so a pregnant settler selected by pickAdultSettler really is pushed into building.occupants. It is reachable from the UI: for an incomplete building listAssignableWorkersForBuilding returns [] (L302), so SelectedBuildingPanel.tsx:673-676 shows '+ Fill builders' → commands.ts:328-330 fillBuildingWorkers → _applyBuilderAssignmentMut, where the first matching entity is taken regardless of which settler satisfied canAssignWorker. The corpse half of the claim is not reachable in normal play (dead entities are GC'd from state.entities each tick and saves force alive:true), but the unconditional '✓ Builder' text at L103 is still a defect; minimal fix: add `&& entity.alive && !entity.pregnant` to the predicate and gate the success text on addToConstructionCrew's return value.

confirmed.title: buildings.ts exports a second, unused getBuildingConfig with a different contract

FALLBACK_BUILDING_CONFIG`, and a repo-wide grep shows every consumer (GameBuildRail, SelectedBuildingPanel, SelectedEntityPanel) imports the buildingConfig version — nothing imports the buildings.ts one, nor isDecorBuilding (693), isResidentialBuilding/isResidenceBuilding (699-709, distinct from the widely used residencyOccupancy.ts:7) or isUniqueBuilding (712). confirmed.title: connectionsAt's 'lone crossing' repair guard can never fire
confirmed.evidence: lines 166-174: `north: north || (!south && !north), south, east: east || (!west && !east), west,` … `if (countConnections(conn) < 2) { return { north: true, east: true, south: false, west: false }; }`.
confirmed.impact: `north || (!south && !north)` is true whenever `south` is false, so N+S >= 1; identically E+W >= 1, so `countConnections(conn) >= 2` always. The fallback return is unreachable, which means the comment's stated purpose ('a lone crossing reads as zero connections and skips corners') is not achieved by this branch — a lone crossing is instead forced to `{north:true, east:true}` by the line-167/169 coercions, i.e. it is classified as a `straight`/`elbow` rather than through any fallback. Any future reader relying on the guard will not get the documented behavior.
confirmed.fix: Delete the unreachable `if (countConnections(conn) < 2)` block and state the actual coercion contract in the comment, or replace the coercions with the intended explicit check (`if (!north && !south && !east && !west) return { north: true, east: true, south: false, west: false };`).
confirmed.verification: Reading connectionsAt (144-179) with countConnections (40-42): `north || (!south && !north)` is false only when north===false and south===true (and symmetrically east===false implies west===true), so the synthesized object always has at least two true arms and the `if (countConnections(conn) < 2)` block at 172-174 is unreachable. Nothing changes in play today, so this is a low-severity dead guard that reads as an active repair; minimal fix: delete the block (or return the synthesized object directly and document that a coincident H/V snap centre always reads as at least a corner).

confirmed.title: Big News ids are re-minted from 1 after a save load while persisted dismissal ids keep the old bn_N — every new card is silently hidden
confirmed.evidence: simEffects.ts:93 `nextBigNewsId = maxSeq + 1;` driven only by simEffects.ts:86-87 `for (const item of state.bigNews) { const match = /^bn_(\d+)$/.exec(item.id) ...`; simEffects.ts:102-104 `const seq = nextBigNewsId++; state.bigNews.push({ id: \`bn_${seq}\`, ...`. The load path empties that array first: saveLoad.ts:367 `bigNews: [],` then saveLoad.ts:446 `syncBigNewsIdFromState(world);` — while the dismissal ids ARE persisted (saveSchema.ts:22 `'villageForge', 'tutorialSeen', 'dismissedBigNewsIds', ...`) and re-applied as a display filter (useTransientGameFeedback.ts:304-311 `const dismissedIds = new Set(loadedWorld.dismissedBigNewsIds ?? []); ... setHiddenBigNewsIds(dismissedIds);` and :319-321 `.filter((news) => !news.dismissed && !hiddenBigNewsIds.has(news.id))`).
confirmed.impact: Every big-news card a player dismisses (manually or by the 8s auto-dismiss timer, useTransientGameFeedback.ts:241-244 -> dismissBigNewsItem -> dismissedBigNewsIds) leaves a `bn_N` id in the save. After reloading that save, `syncBigNewsIdFromState` sees an empty bigNews list, so the counter restarts at 1 (and the worker thread, which never syncs at all, also starts at 1) and re-issues ids that are already in the persisted dismissed set. `activeBigNews` filters on id, so the first N announcements after a load — festival starts, full-moon Howler warnings, raid-incoming banners — are never shown, where N is the number of announcements dismissed in the previous session (hundreds after a long game). No test covers this (grep of tests for `bigNews`/`dismissedBigNews` returns nothing).
confirmed.fix: Make ids collision-proof across sessions: change `syncBigNewsIdFromState` to take `Pick<WorldState,'bigNews'|'dismissedBigNewsIds'>` and also scan `state.dismissedBigNewsIds` for `/^bn_(\d+)$/` when computing `maxSeq`, and call it from the worker's session/import path (`src/game/simWorker/gameWorker.ts` `resetWorkerSession`/`importSave` handler) as well as from `loadGameFromParsed`; alternatively mint tick-scoped ids (`bn_${state.tick}_${seq}`) and update both regexes in syncBigNewsIdFromState.
confirmed.verification: syncBigNewsIdFromState (simEffects.ts:84-94) derives maxSeq only from state.bigNews, and the load path empties that array (saveLoad.ts:367 `bigNews: []`) before calling it at :446, so the module counter restarts at 1 — in the worker too, since gameWorker.ts never calls it (grep finds it only in saveLoad/gameEngine) — while dismissedBigNewsIds is a persisted allow-listed field (saveSchema.ts:22) reused both as a display filter (useTransientGameFeedback.ts:304-311, 319-321) and as a delta filter (simDelta.ts:20-25). Re-issued bn_N ids already in that set are therefore dropped for the first N announcements after a load. Fix: also scan state.dismissedBigNewsIds for /^bn_(\d+)$/ in syncBigNewsIdFromState and call it from the worker import path, or mint tick-scoped ids; severity medium because it silently hides UI cards but corrupts no state and self-heals once the counter passes the old maximum.

confirmed.lines: 407-427 (caller gate 412) vs src/game/simulation/humanSocial.ts:64 and src/game/adaptiveSpatialQuery.ts:205 | 407-427 (caller gate), vs src/game/simulation/humanSocial.ts:64 and src/game/adaptiveSpatialQuery.ts:205
confirmed.title: Ambient-dialogue stagger in humanTick (mod 3) is misaligned with the neighbour-scan stagger (SOCIAL_STAGGER = 6), so half of all ambient rolls get an empty candidate list and can only produce a solo line
confirmed.evidence: humanTick.ts:412 `(state.tick + entity.id) % 3 === 0` gates the call `tryAmbientRandomDialogue(entity, ambientChatNeighbors(entity), state.tick, 0.036 * PER_TICK_RATE_SCALE, ...)`. The candidate provider is `simAmbientChatNeighbors` (humanTick.ts:282-283), and humanSocial.ts:64 begins `if ((tick + self.id) % SOCIAL_STAGGER !== 0) { return []; }` with adaptiveSpatialQuery.ts:205 `export const SOCIAL_STAGGER = 6;`. Multiples of 3 are not all multiples of 6.
confirmed.impact: For every tick where (tick+id) % 6 === 3 (exactly half of the ticks the caller admits), ambientChatNeighbors() returns an empty array, so `tryAmbientRandomDialogue` can never pair the speaker with a nearby settler and always emits a solo remark. Paired ambient conversation therefore fires at roughly half the rate the code intends, which is precisely the monologue regression documented in tests/humanChat.ambientPairing.test.ts (BUG 2026-08-21-ambient-dialogue-often-becomes-leader-monologue) — that test calls tryAmbientRandomDialogue directly and so cannot see the caller-side gate.
confirmed.fix: Replace the caller's `(state.tick + entity.id) % 3 === 0` with the same stagger the callee uses: `(state.tick + entity.id) % SOCIAL_STAGGER === 0` (SOCIAL_STAGGER is already imported in humanTick.ts line 113). This keeps the expensive-neighbour-query short-circuit while guaranteeing every admitted roll actually receives candidates.
confirmed.verification: humanTick.ts:412 admits a roll only when `(state.tick + entity.id) % 3 === 0`, while simAmbientChatNeighbors returns [] unless the same expression is divisible by SOCIAL_STAGGER = 6 (humanSocial.ts:61-66, adaptiveSpatialQuery.ts:205); on the residue-3 half of those ticks tryAmbientRandomDialogue (humanChat.ts:467-481) finds no partner and startDialogueTreeChat is called solo, and the BUG 2026-08-21 test (tests/humanChat.ambientPairing.test.ts) calls tryAmbientRandomDialogue directly so it cannot see this gate. The mechanism is confirmed, but only flavour dialogue is affected, so I correct the severity to low; minimal fix: change the caller gate to `% SOCIAL_STAGGER === 0` (SOCIAL_STAGGER is already imported at humanTick.ts:113).

confirmed.title: Affair exposure reason ignores its inputs and always rolls a flat 22% 'caught', which jails and always divorces
confirmed.evidence: lines 789-799: the affair branch gates only on `hasAffairPartner(entity, ctx.entityById) && entity.energy > ... && !isSpouseNearby(...)` and then rolls `if (Math.random() < HUMAN_DAILY_AFFAIR_PREGNANCY_CHANCE * fertility) {` (line 799). The youth branch directly above instead requires `entity.age >= HUMAN_FERTILITY_START && entity.age < HUMAN_YOUTH_FERTILITY_END` (lines 754-755).
confirmed.impact: isValidAffairTarget (line 622) admits targets from HUMAN_ADULT_MIN_AGE = 16, so a 16-17-year-old single settler can become an established affair partner through the daily owner. tryDailyConception is called for every non-prisoner player human (humanTick.ts:330), so that settler then rolls the full adult affair rate 0.14 x fertility (fertility = 1 up to age 35) - roughly 45x (age 17) to 60x (age 16) the youth-gate chance (0.0045 x 0.50 at 16) - with no mutual youth-love link and no age check, contradicting SIMULATION_AUTHORITY.md section 5: "At ages 14-17 it requires the documented mutual youth-love, nearby, energy, and reduced-probability gate".
confirmed.fix: Restrict the affair branch to adults, e.g. add `&& !(entity.age >= HUMAN_FERTILITY_START && entity.age < HUMAN_YOUTH_FERTILITY_END)` to the condition at line 789 (or require `entity.age >= HUMAN_YOUTH_FERTILITY_END`), so ages 14-17 can only conceive through the youth branch.
confirmed.verification: pickAffairExposureReason (1043-1053) discards `_cheater/_lover/_humans` and returns 'caught' on a flat 22% roll gated only by hasStaffedPrison (1036-1041, any completed prison with a guard anywhere), and both daily-gossip call sites (326, 342) feed that verdict to exposeAffair, where 'caught' arrests both partners (1149-1152) and calls tryDivorceOnCaughtCheater(..., true), whose caughtInAct=true skips the isSpouseNearby gate (982) and forces divorceChance = 1 (986). Because the gossip gate only needs affairProgress ≥ 45/85 and no witness check at all, a pair that is merely gossiped about can be jailed and forcibly divorced with no spouse or guard present while the log asserts they 'were caught'. Fix: make the reason evidence-based inside the helper (spouse/guard proximity from the arguments it already receives) or have the daily gossip path pass 'rumor'.

confirmed.title: needsMedicalCare compares griefUntilTick with 0 instead of the current tick
confirmed.evidence: 37: `if ((entity.griefUntilTick ?? 0) > 0 && entity.energy < entity.maxEnergy * 0.7) return true;`
confirmed.impact: `griefUntilTick` is an absolute sim tick (set to `tick + TICKS_PER_DAY * 7` in humanLifecycleCleanup.ts:73 and `+3` for a lover at line 90) and is never reset to 0, so `> 0` stays true for the rest of the settler's life once they have grieved. Every ex-griever below 70% energy is permanently classified as needing medical care: they stay in tickHospitalDailyCare's patient list (line 183, so ward rounds treat them) and satisfy `shouldAttemptHospitalTreatment` (humanHospitalBehavior.ts:40) while on shift with energy 42-50%. All other grief checks in the codebase compare with the current tick (socialLife.ts:95, townHall.ts:176/248, citizenOverview.ts:129, storyEvents.ts:550/573).
confirmed.fix: Take the current tick (add a `tick` parameter or pass `state.tick` from the callers) and test `(entity.griefUntilTick ?? 0) > tick`.
confirmed.verification: griefUntilTick is an absolute tick written as tick + N*TICKS_PER_DAY (humanLifecycleCleanup.ts:73 and :90, humanLifecycle.ts:119-120) and never cleared, so `(entity.griefUntilTick ?? 0) > 0` stays true for life, unlike every other grief check (socialLife.ts:95, townHall.ts:176/248, citizenOverview.ts:129, storyEvents.ts:550/573) which compare against the current tick. Consequently any settler who has ever grieved is permanently listed as a patient in tickHospitalDailyCare (line 183) whenever energy < 70% and satisfies shouldAttemptHospitalTreatment (humanHospitalBehavior.ts:40, effective in the 42-50% band where the line-36 threshold has not already fired), giving free hospital routing/healing. Minimal fix: accept the current tick and test `> tick`.

confirmed.title: tickHospitalDailyCare passes patient proximity as doctorPresent
confirmed.evidence: 189: `const near = Math.hypot(p.x - hx, p.y - hy) < 70;` … 192: `if (treatPatientAtHospital(state, p, hospital, { doctorPresent: near })) {`
confirmed.impact: `doctorPresent` is documented/implemented as "a doctor is on site" — its default is a proximity scan of the hospital's occupants (86-89). Passing the PATIENT's distance to the ward makes every patient in the ward round receive the +0.35 doctor strength bonus (~+5 energy per treatment) and the '❤ Treated' floating text even when no assigned occupant is anywhere near the ward, i.e. it is less accurate than the default it overrides.
confirmed.fix: Drop the option (`treatPatientAtHospital(state, p, hospital)`) so the real doctor check runs, or compute the occupant proximity explicitly and pass that boolean.
confirmed.verification: Line 189 computes `near` as the PATIENT's distance to the ward centre and line 192 passes it as the `doctorPresent` option, overriding treatPatientAtHospital's default (86-89) that scans the hospital's occupants for a real doctor within 48px of the ward. Every patient treated in a daily ward round therefore gets the +0.35 doctor strength term (line 91) and the '❤ Treated' text even when no occupied doctor is near. Minimal fix: call treatPatientAtHospital(state, p, hospital) and let the real check run.

confirmed.title: clearEntityChat leaves chatDialogueSessionKey set, so a vanished session leaves the settler flagged dialogue-busy
confirmed.impact: Callers force phrases without checking isDialogueBusy/chatTicks — e.g. humanLeisureBehavior.ts:100 (`sayHumanChatPhrase(entity, impulse.bubble, 55)`), humanRelationships.ts:1494-1495, townHall.ts:237+, villageLeadership.ts:621. If the speaker currently holds a solo session (`solo:<id>`), the entry stays in the module-level dialogueSessions Map forever: every later solo attempt reuses the same key, hits `dialogueSessions.has(key)` and returns without showing anything, so that settler never speaks a tree dialogue again and the Map entry leaks for the session lifetime. For a pair key the entry is only reclaimed when the other participant finishes; if both sides are force-phrased in the same window (humanRelationships.ts:1494-1495 does exactly that) the pair can never dialogue again.
confirmed.fix: Delete the entry before clearing the fields: `const staleKey = entity.chatDialogueSessionKey; if (staleKey) dialogueSessions.delete(staleKey);` and, in tickHumanChat, clear `chatDialogueSessionKey`/`chatPartnerId` when `dialogueSessions` has no entry for the key (the resolveSessionEntities null path currently only calls clearEntityChat), so the counterpart cannot stay isDialogueBusy forever.
confirmed.verification: clearEntityChat (167-170) clears only chatTicks/chatPhrase, and tickHumanChat falls through to it at line 372 whenever advanceDialogue returns false — including the case where resolveSessionEntities finds no entry in the module-level dialogueSessions map (line 197-198), which happens after a partner dies (cleanupEntityDialogueState deletes the session at 593 but only clears the dead entity's key) or after resetDialogueSessions() on load (renderer.ts:22). The survivor keeps chatDialogueSessionKey, so isDialogueBusy (60-62) stays true and excludes them from ambient targeting, banter and greetings (humanSocial.ts:61/84, socialLife.ts:349/355/386) until a later chat start overwrites the key; unlike clearDialogueSession (172-189) and cleanupEntityDialogueState (595-596), this path never clears it. Minimal fix: also clear chatDialogueSessionKey and chatPartnerId in clearEntityChat.

confirmed.title: economyLedger/foodHistory are written by the tick but missing from the worker rollback backup
confirmed.evidence: `SimPrepKeys` (L10-87) lists `resources`, `storageMax`, `villageForge`, `researchProgress`, … but not `economyLedger` or `foodHistory`; `extractSimPrep` copies only those keys (e.g. L116 `resources: { ...state.resources },` L117 `storageMax: { ...state.storageMax },`) and `applySimPrep` restores only them (L185-265). Meanwhile the daily tick writes them: economyLedger.ts:47 `state.economyLedger = { day, produced: {}, consumed: {} };` / L56 `ledger.produced[source] = (ledger.produced[source] ?? 0) + amount;` / L31-39 push into `state.foodHistory`. The backup is used to undo an already-applied tick: gameWorker.ts:314 `const prepBackup = extractSimPrep(world);` … L345 `applySimPrep(world, prepBackup);` ('Render buffer pool exhausted').
confirmed.impact: That rollback restores resources/entities but leaves the rolled-back tick's ledger entries in place. The same tick is then retried (or simply lost), so `ledger.produced`/`consumed` and the archived `foodHistory` day double-count or claim food that was never kept — the exact numbers the Food ledger, dashboard 'Food today' (dashboardData.ts:269-279) and the 30-day history display. Same class of gap applies to `foodSpoilageRate`, which the tick would write once updateStorageCaps is wired in.
confirmed.fix: Add `'economyLedger' | 'foodHistory' | 'foodSpoilageRate'` to `SimPrepKeys` and clone them in `extractSimPrep` (e.g. `economyLedger: state.economyLedger ? { day: state.economyLedger.day, produced: { ...state.economyLedger.produced }, consumed: { ...state.economyLedger.consumed } } : undefined`, `foodHistory: state.foodHistory ? state.foodHistory.map((s) => ({ ...s, produced: { ...s.produced }, consumed: { ...s.consumed } })) : undefined`) and assign them back in `applySimPrep`.
confirmed.verification: SimPrepKeys (10-87) and extractSimPrep/applySimPrep omit economyLedger, foodHistory and foodSpoilageRate, while the daily tick writes the first two (economyLedger.ts:47, 56 and 31-39) and gameWorker.ts takes extractSimPrep as a rollback backup at line 314 and restores it at 339/345/355 (buffer-pool and exception paths). The rollback therefore restores resources/entities but leaves the failed tick's ledger entries and archived food sample in place, so the Food ledger and dashboard 'Food today' over-report one tick's worth of production and consumption. Minimal fix: add the three keys to SimPrepKeys and clone/restore them (the foodSpoilageRate part is speculative — updateStorageCaps currently has no caller).

confirmed.title: Autumn herd spawns deer on impassable terrain (deep water, mountains, river/bank)
confirmed.evidence:
44:    if (edge === 0) { x = 40; y = height / 2 + spread; }
(48-54 createEntity(EntityType.Deer, x, y, ...) — no isPassableWildlifePosition check anywhere in spawnHerdAtEdge)
confirmed.impact: Every other spawn path in the codebase gates on terrain (worldGen.spawnWildlifeAtRandomPassable line 224, spawnWildlifeRing line 349); this one uses fixed edge coordinates. Measured by importing the repo's own isPassableWildlifePosition and running tickMigration on real maps (40 maps x 6 presets): coastal 119/400 herd deer spawn on deep/shallow water in 40/40 maps; verdant 45/400 (water/river/riverBank); harsh 76/400 (25 inside Mountains); riverlands 77/400. So a third of a coastal herd starts standing in the sea, on tiles the rest of the simulation treats as unpassable (UNPASSABLE_WILDLIFE_TERRAIN, worldGen.ts:71-78); those deer must wander out before normal land behaviour applies (120 ticks after arrival most blocked deer were still on unpassable tiles), and the player sees deer swimming in the ocean.
confirmed.fix: In spawnHerdAtEdge, validate each candidate point before createEntity with isPassableWildlifePosition(state, x, y, 8) (nudge along the edge, or fall back to spawnWildlifeRing(state, EntityType.Deer, edgeMidX, edgeMidY, count, 40, 120) which already contains the passability retry loop).
confirmed.verification: spawnHerdAtEdge (migration.ts:37-60) uses fixed edge coordinates (x=40 / width-40 / y=40 / height-40) and never calls isPassableWildlifePosition, unlike worldGen's other spawn paths (worldGen.ts:155), and I reproduced the effect with the repo's own predicate over 10 medium maps per preset: unpassable herd deer were 29/100 on coastal (in 10/10 maps), 16/100 riverlands, 13/100 harsh, 9/100 verdant. Because tickLayerSystems' deep-water sliding physics zeroes velocity for a next position on water (tickLayerSystems.ts:614-628), a deer that starts inside it is effectively stuck and eventually starves. Fix: validate each candidate point before createEntity (nudging along the edge) or spawn via the existing passability-retry helper.

confirmed.lines: 89; missing in src/game/simBuffers/simDelta.ts:52-139 and src/game/simWorker/simPrep.ts:10-87 | 89 (write); missing in src/game/simBuffers/simDelta.ts field list 109-133 and src/game/simWorker/simPrep.ts 58-87

confirmed.title: The 'split a married couple' repair is unreachable, so canAdmitAll is always true
confirmed.impact: createImmigrantSettler is called with maxMembers = openSlots (line 82) and only returns a 2-member couple when `maxMembers >= 2` (worldGen.ts:493). Consequently a 2-person result implies openSlots >= 2, and the only other result is a single settler, so `newcomers.length <= maxHumanPopulation - counts.humans` is always true: the else-branch at 87 and the entire spouse-unlink block at 90-95 (setting relationshipStatus/partnerId/pregnant on newcomers[0], which is the never-pregnant husband) can never run. confirmed.verification: createImmigrantSettler (worldGen.ts:480-551) returns a two-member couple only when maxMembers >= 2 and otherwise a single settler, and dailyPopulation.ts:82 passes maxMembers = openSlots = maxHumanPopulation - counts.humans, which is unchanged when re-read at line 86, so `newcomers.length <= maxHumanPopulation - counts.humans` is always true and the else-slice (87) plus the spouse-unlink block (90-95) can never execute. confirmed.title: grantRaidSpoils subtracts resources instead of capping when stores are above their storage cap
confirmed.impact: room is not floored at 0, so when a resource already exceeds its cap a successful outgoing raid or accepted tribute removes that resource. Example: food 1000 with a cap that has dropped to 800 (demolishing a Barn or Silo recomputes caps in economy.ts:8-21 while stores stay put; demolition refunds add resources uncapped in buildingPlacementActions.ts:180-182) - winning a raid with 40 food spoils evaluates Math.min(800-1000, 40) = -200 and drops food to 800. The rest of the codebase floors headroom (resourceUtils.ts:43, VisitorCampPanel.tsx:30) and clampRaidGoldGain already floors gold, so this is an omission, not the established convention.
confirmed.fix: Floor each room term: const room = Math.max(0, state.storageMax.food - state.resources.food); (and the same for wood, stone, gold).
confirmed.verification: Lines 682/687/692 compute `room = state.storageMax.X - state.resources.X` with no floor, so when a resource exceeds its cap `gained.X` becomes negative and `state.resources.X += gained.X` silently destroys the overflow and reports a negative loot figure — while resourceUtils.ts:43 and clampRaidGoldGain (line 672) both floor their headroom. The claimed trigger is wrong, though: updateStorageCaps has no caller anywhere (grep finds only its definition and a doc string), so caps never drop on demolition; the overflow must come from uncapped gains such as refundHalfBuildingCost (buildingPlacementActions.ts:180-182) or inventionFair.ts:246, which limits the loss to a few units — hence low. Minimal fix: wrap each room term in Math.max(0, ...).

confirmed.title: Moon-Howler cooldown state is written every full moon but absent from save, worker prep and tick delta
confirmed.evidence:
moonHowler.ts:693  `  state.lastMoonHowlerExorcismTick = state.tick;`
moonHowler.ts:812  `      state.moonHowlerPriestsFleeUntil = state.tick + MOON_HOWLER_EXORCISM_INTERVAL_HOURS * TICKS_PER_HOUR;`
confirmed.impact: Neither field is in WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS (saveSchema.ts:4-26) nor in SimPrepKeys (src/game/simWorker/simPrep.ts:10-87), and simDelta's world tuple only carries renffrOmen/renffrChatterUntilTick (simDelta.ts:126-127). Both are therefore undefined after save/load or after worker preparation while world.tick is restored. Reloading during a full-moon night makes `state.tick - (state.lastMoonHowlerExorcismTick ?? -9999)` always pass the 2-hour gate (line 673-678) and `state.tick < (state.moonHowlerPriestsFleeUntil ?? -1)` false (line 659), so the surviving priests immediately retry the rite within the same night instead of retreating for the declared cooldown — each failed rite still carries a 40% priest-death branch (MOON_HOWLER_OUTCOME_KILL_PRIEST).
confirmed.fix: Add 'lastMoonHowlerExorcismTick' and 'moonHowlerPriestsFleeUntil' to WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS (saveSchema.ts) and to SimPrepKeys/extractSimPrep (simPrep.ts), and scale them in migrateTickTimeline (saveLoad.ts:228-234) like the other absolute tick deadlines.
confirmed.verification: Both fields are WorldState members (gameTypes.ts:751-752) used as durable pacing state — written at 693 and 812 and read at 659 and 676 (plus humanTick.ts:609) — yet they appear in neither WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS (saveSchema.ts:4-26), SimPrepKeys/SimPrepPayload (simPrep.ts:10-87) nor SimTickDelta (delta.ts:126-127 carries renffrOmen/renffrChatterUntilTick but not these), and no test references them. So a save/reload during a full-moon night clears the two-hour rite cooldown and the priests_scared window (allowing the cure outcome to be re-rolled), and a worker error rollback restores everything except these two fields. Minimal fix: add both keys to the save allow-list, the prep payload and the tick delta (or declare them intentionally transient and stop treating them as persisted pacing state).

confirmed.title: recentSourceKind scans from the oldest end of a newest-first log and records the wrong source event
confirmed.evidence: 81 comment: `* Scans backwards through the event log to find the most recent matching event category.`; 85: `const scanLimit = Math.max(0, log.length - 40);`; 87: `for (let i = log.length - 1; i >= scanLimit; i--) {`. Because logEvent unshifts (eventLog.ts:23), index log.length-1 is the OLDEST entry, so the loop walks entries len-40..len-1 (the 41 oldest) and returns the first match found from that end.
confirmed.impact: The rumour's subject and text (59-65, 134) come from the colony's earliest events instead of the newest: a birth, combat or scandal that just happened is ignored in favour of day-1 scaffolding, so the card narrates stale history. Line 124 compounds it: `[FLAG_SOURCE_EVENT]: state.eventLog[state.eventLog.length - 1]?.id ?? 0` stores the oldest entry's id, not the matched event, and no code ever reads FLAG_SOURCE_EVENT (only the declaration at 28 and this write exist).
confirmed.fix: Iterate the newest end — `for (let i = 0, last = Math.min(log.length, 40); i < last; i++)` — return the matched entry along with its kind, and store that entry's id in FLAG_SOURCE_EVENT (or delete the unused flag).
confirmed.verification: logEvent unshifts (eventLog.ts:23), so index log.length-1 is the OLDEST entry, yet recentSourceKind (rumourLedger.ts:87) walks from log.length-1 down to log.length-40 and returns the first match — the 41 oldest events — contradicting its own comment, so the rumour category (and therefore RUMOUR_TEXT, line 59-65) is chosen from ancient history; line 124 likewise stores the oldest entry's id and nothing ever reads FLAG_SOURCE_EVENT (grep finds only the declaration and this write). Minimal fix: iterate from index 0 up to min(len,40) to scan the newest entries, return the matched entry, and store its id; severity low because only one story card's flavour text is affected.

confirmed.title: migrateTickTimeline scales some absolute-tick fields but not pregnancyDueProgress or pendingStoryEvents deadlines
confirmed.evidence: L244-245: `// pregnancyProgress is 0..PREGNANCY_TICKS absolute progress — scale with day length` / `scaleField(rec, 'pregnancyProgress');` — the sibling `entity.pregnancyDueProgress` (set from the same constant at humanRelationships.ts:640) is not in the scaled list; `pendingStoryEvents[].createdAtTick/expiresAtTick` are also skipped even though storyEvents.ts:158 compares them against `state.tick`.
confirmed.impact: In any load that needs a rescale (`_ticksPerDay !== TICKS_PER_DAY`), progress is multiplied by `scale` while the threshold keeps the old unit. With scale>1 (24→72 ticks/day) a mid-pregnancy settler's `pregnancyProgress` jumps past `pregnancyDueProgress`, so humanLifecycle.ts:63-66 delivers on the next pregnancy tick; with scale<1 the pregnancy never reaches term. Pending story cards likewise expire instantly (scale>1) or linger far past their window (scale<1). Currently latent only because `parseSaveJson` rejects every `_version` except the current one and current saves always write `_ticksPerDay = TICKS_PER_DAY`.
confirmed.fix: Add `scaleField(rec, 'pregnancyDueProgress');` next to the existing `pregnancyProgress` line, and scale `createdAtTick`/`expiresAtTick` for each entry of `world.pendingStoryEvents` in the same migration.
confirmed.verification: migrateTickTimeline (218-288) scales pregnancyProgress (245) and the nested moonHowlerSaved copy (249) but not pregnancyDueProgress, which is produced from the same PREGNANCY_TICKS constant (entityFactory.ts:166, humanRelationships.ts:640/660/676) and compared as `pregnancyProgress < dueProgress` (humanLifecycle.ts:64-66), so on a 24-tick legacy save the progress triples while the due value does not and every pregnant settler gives birth on the first tick after load. It also has no loop for world.pendingStoryEvents, whose expiresAtTick is written with TICKS_PER_DAY*3 (storyEvents.ts:305) and read as `state.tick < e.expiresAtTick` (storyEvents.ts:158), so all open story cards are filtered away on the same load. Fix: add scaleField(rec, 'pregnancyDueProgress') (and the snapshot copy) and a pendingStoryEvents loop beside the raid loops.

confirmed.title: The 'divorce' event type has no Chronicle filter although the file contract promises one filter per stored type
confirmed.evidence: L3-6 comment: 'Each stored event type receives one direct filter' — but the option list (L7-22) contains all/conception/birth/death/marriage/scandal/building/research/trade/migration/disaster/combat/event/season/milestone and no `divorce` entry, while `GameEventLog['type']` includes `| 'divorce'` (gameTypes.ts:784), writers emit it (humanRelationships.ts:885, 997, 1015) and the panel has art for it (EventLogPanel.tsx:23 `divorce: '💔'`).

confirmed.verification: EVENT_LOG_FILTER_OPTIONS (7-22) lists fifteen categories but not 'divorce', even though 'divorce' is part of GameEventLog['type'] (gameTypes.ts:784), is written by humanRelationships.ts:995 and :1013, and has a dedicated icon and colour in EventLogPanel.tsx:23/41 — so the file's 'one direct filter per stored event type' contract is false and divorces are only visible under 'All'.
