confirmed.title: Player commands issued while the sim worker is booting are stranded if the worker never boots (or faults), instead of being applied on the main-thread authority
confirmed.evidence:
src/game/gameLoop.ts:552-554: `if (this.workerBooting && this.workerHost) { this.deferredWorkerCommands.push({ cmd, sessionGen: this.sessionGen }); return;`
src/game/gameLoop.ts:198: `console.warn('[GameLoop] Worker init failed — falling back to main-thread ticks', err);`
confirmed.impact: Commands are only replayed by flushDeferredWorkerCommands(), which is called exclusively on a successful worker init (line 193), recovery (line 295) or importSave (line 510). The init-failure catch (196-207) and fallbackFromWorker (385-404) set workerEnabled=false and continue on the main thread without flushing or clearing the queue, so every command the player (or useVirtualPlayer) issued during the boot window is silently dropped while the game keeps running; if a recovery later succeeds, those older commands are replayed on top of the newer commands that were already applied locally, inverting player intent. Nothing blocks input during boot — the only guard, isSimWorkerBooting() (line 410), is never called anywhere in src.
confirmed.fix: In the init-failure catch and in fallbackFromWorker, after setting workerBooting/workerEnabled to false, call this.flushDeferredWorkerCommands() so the queued commands run through the same main-thread domain implementation (or clear the queue explicitly and document the drop).
confirmed.verification: The cited code is exactly as described: `applyCommand` queues into `deferredWorkerCommands` while `workerBooting && workerHost` (552-555), and that queue is drained only by `flushDeferredWorkerCommands()` at 193, 295 and 510. The init-failure `.catch` (196-207) and `fallbackFromWorker` (385-404) set `workerBooting=false`/`workerEnabled=false` without flushing or clearing, so boot-window commands are never applied locally and the game resumes on the main thread; a later successful `attemptWorkerRecovery` then replays them via `flushDeferredWorkerCommands()` (295) on top of the newer commands that were already applied locally in the interim, inverting intent. `isSimWorkerBooting()` (410) has no caller anywhere in src and tests/gameLoop.commandDispatch.test.ts contains no deferred-queue case, so nothing locks the current behaviour. Minimal fix: in both the init-failure catch and `fallbackFromWorker`, call `this.flushDeferredWorkerCommands()` after clearing `workerBooting`/`workerEnabled` (the queue then applies through the same domain implementation via `applyCommandLocal`), or explicitly clear it and log the drop.

confirmed.title: Save allow-list omits live simulation state: visitor quest, Moon Howler cooldowns, village happiness, ledger history
confirmed.evidence:
saveSchema.ts:16 `'visitorGroups', 'activeVillageRequest', 'villageRequestCooldownUntilDay', 'villageRequestHistory',`
saveSchema.ts:23 `'dismissedNotificationIds', 'lastWildlifeReplenishLogDay', 'eventsThisYear',`
gameTypes.ts:740-741 `foodHistory?: FoodDaySample[];` / `visitorQuest?: VisitorQuest;`
gameTypes.ts:751-752 `lastMoonHowlerExorcismTick?: number;` / `moonHowlerPriestsFleeUntil?: number;`
moonHowler.ts:673 `const last = state.lastMoonHowlerExorcismTick ?? -9999;`
confirmed.impact: `WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS` is the only list that `pickWorldFieldsForSave` writes and `pickWorldStateFromSave` reads, so after save -> load `state.visitorQuest` is undefined: an accepted smith quest (its `progress`, `expiresDay`, and the 30 gold/4 reputation reward) silently disappears, and `deliverVisitorQuest` can no longer be satisfied (it only sets `status:'completed'`, never grants a new quest for the same group). The same field is also absent from `SimPrepKeys`/`SimTickDelta` (no match anywhere in simWorker/simBuffers), so in worker mode the main thread never receives a quest the worker created and the quest card cannot appear at all. `lastMoonHowlerExorcismTick`/`moonHowlerPriestsFleeUntil` are the church-rite rate limit and priest-fear timer: after a reload line 673 reads `-9999`, so the rite can fire on the first full-moon night regardless of the cooldown (save-scumming the cure roll), and already-scared priests stop being scared. `villageHappiness` reverts to the `?? 50` default in PopulationPanel, and `foodHistory`/`economyLedger` history is dropped (the delta carries both, so this is a save-only gap).
confirmed.fix: Add the sim-owned fields to the allow-list (`'visitorQuest'`, `'lastMoonHowlerExorcismTick'`, `'moonHowlerPriestsFleeUntil'`, `'villageHappiness'`, `'foodHistory'`, `'economyLedger'`) and carry `visitorQuest` through `SimPrepKeys`/`SimTickDelta` and the load defaults in loadGameFromParsed; keep genuinely transient presentation fields (screenShakeImpulse, huntVisuals) out.
confirmed.verification: `WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS` (saveSchema.ts:4-26) is indeed the only list used by `pickWorldFieldsForSave` (46-51) and `pickWorldStateFromSave` (saveLoad.ts:65-71), and it contains none of `visitorQuest`, `lastMoonHowlerExorcismTick`, `moonHowlerPriestsFleeUntil`, `villageHappiness`, `foodHistory`, `economyLedger` (the only other persisted fields are the four transient ones in `pickTransientWorldFieldsForSave`, viewState.ts:338-345). `visitorQuest` is likewise absent from `SimPrepKeys`/`SimTickDelta` (simPrep.ts:10-87, simDelta.ts), so in worker mode `groupEvents.ts:416 -> maybeStartVisitorQuest` writes a quest the main thread never receives and App.tsx:1545 can never render it, while Moon Howler's rite cooldown falls back to `-9999` after any reload (moonHowler.ts:673), letting the cure roll fire again on the first full-moon night. Fix: add `visitorQuest`, `lastMoonHowlerExorcismTick`, `moonHowlerPriestsFleeUntil` (and, if persistence is wanted, `villageHappiness`/`foodHistory`/`economyLedger`) to the allow-list and carry `visitorQuest` through `SimPrepKeys`/`SimTickDelta`; note `pushCompletedDayToHistory` documents food history as transient, so that part is the weakest of the listed gaps.

confirmed.title: Housing pickers accept rival-camp houses; two callers pass buildings.filter(isResidenceBuilding), which keeps faction 'rival' residences
confirmed.evidence: residencySelection.ts:267-268 `const unit: Entity[] = [custodian]; visited.add(custodian.id);` — the bucket loop never checks `visited.has(custodianId)` before building the unit (contrast the fallback loop at line 284: `if (visited.has(human.id)) continue;` and the partner guard at line 270 `if (partner && !visited.has(partner.id))`).
confirmed.impact: Concrete failure: mother M has minor child A (custodian M), father F has minor child B (custodian F, B's mother dead), and M and F are partners (a blended family created by remarriage — reachable through humanTick.ts:910/tryCompleteCourtshipMarriage). Bucket[M]=[A] builds unit [M,F,A] and marks F visited, but bucket[F]=[B] still builds unit [F,B] containing F again. In assignMissingResidences (residencyReconciliation.ts:230-239) every unit that needs reassignment clears and re-places ALL of its members, so F is moved twice per pass and the two units keep stealing him: [F,B] is placed in an empty house, then [M,F,A] (now invalid) is cleared and placed in another empty house, and the 24-pass loop never records `reassigned === 0`, so it runs all 24 passes on every assign pulse (4x/day). The stable end state leaves the minor child B alone in one house while F, M and A occupy another — the exact opposite of assignFamilyToResidence's contract ('keeps children with custodian'); ensureOrphanAdoption cannot repair it because B still has a living natural custodian, so the split persists across pulses.
confirmed.fix: Add the missing guard at the top of the bucket loop: `if (visited.has(custodianId)) continue;` (and attach that bucket's children to the custodian's existing unit, or rebuild the children buckets from the emitted units) so each settler belongs to exactly one housing unit; the child whose custodian is already in a unit must join that unit rather than fall through to the single-entity fallback at line 283.
confirmed.verification: The pickers only skip leader houses and do not filter faction (`pickResidenceForFamily` 631-633, likewise `pickSharedResidenceForFamily` 582-584 and `pickLeastCrowdedResidence` 58-63), while `listPlayerResidences` (35-37) is the sanctioned filter; `humanTick.ts:914` and `humanRelationships.ts:908` both pass `buildings.filter(isResidenceBuilding)`, and rival camps really do create completed `House` buildings with `faction: 'rival'` (groupEvents.ts:447-456 -> createRivalBuilding 308-324; rivalEvents.ts:172 can add more). Because `countResidentsInBuilding` is called with player-only humans, a rival house counts 0 residents and scores as empty (EMPTY_HOUSE_BONUS for a lone settler, or score 0 versus 2 for an already-housed couple), so `syncPartnerResidence` (residencyReconciliation.ts:269-291) and `reassignDivorcedResidences` can move player settlers into the enemy camp; `syncResidenceOccupants` skips rival buildings (115) so the section-5 residence/occupants invariant is false until the next assign pulse clears the stale id in `assignMissingResidences` (205-212, ≤18 ticks). Fix: add `if (residence.faction === 'rival') continue;` beside the leader-house skip in the three pickers, or pass `listPlayerResidences(buildings)` at both call sites.

confirmed.title: Best-skill candidate scan in _assignIdleWorkerToBuildingMut is unreachable
confirmed.evidence: L153: "if (!idleHuman && preferredHumanId === undefined) {" guards an O(N) best-skill scan (L154-165), but `idleHuman` was set on L146-150 by pickAdultSettler, which always returns the first matching entity as a fallback (L49-51); the scan re-applies exactly the same predicate (L157 `isEligibleIdleWorker(entity, state)`), so the guard is true only when the scan can find nothing.
confirmed.impact: The documented optimisation on L152 ("O(N) scan for best skill instead of O(N log N) full array sort") never executes; the fallback manual worker is always the first eligible settler in entity order, so the intended highest-skill preference for manual assignment is silently lost (also two full entity scans are implied where a comment claims one).
confirmed.fix: Delete L152-166, or change pickAdultSettler to return only an explicit preferred match and keep the scan as the genuine fallback selection.
confirmed.verification: `pickAdultSettler` (36-55) returns the first entity passing the filter as a fallback whenever no preferred id matches, so its result is undefined only when the predicate matches nothing; the scan at 153-165 re-applies the identical `isEligibleIdleWorker(entity, state)` predicate (149 vs 157), so `bestCandidate` can never be found there and `idleHuman` is never assigned by that block. The intended highest-skill preference for manual assignment is therefore not implemented and the block is dead (only the transfer branch at 169-178 then runs). Fix: delete lines 152-166, or make `pickAdultSettler` return only an explicit preferred match and keep the scan as the real fallback.

confirmed.title: The whole strip replacement/refund machinery is unreachable because nothing ever writes replacesBuildingId
confirmed.evidence: `readonly replacesBuildingId?: number;` (stripBuild.ts:29) and `replacesBuildingId?: number;` (stripTopology.ts:131) are only ever READ: the complete cross-repo grep for `replacesBuildingId` returns reads in buildingPlacementActions.ts (lines 207-208, 230, 269) and the two type declarations — no producer exists (`resolveWallStripPlan`, `resolveRoadStripPlan` and `resolveStripPlan` never set it, and both UI call sites send the preview segments unchanged).
confirmed.impact: The documented feature ('Existing player building to be demolished/replaced (refunded at 50%)', stripBuild.ts:28; 'Existing player building removed (corner swap or straight-through rebuild)', stripTopology.ts:130) never runs: `refundHalfBuildingCost` (buildingPlacementActions.ts:178) and the whole `replacing`/`replacementId` branch (lines 207-223, 269-284) are dead, so no replaced building is ever refunded and no corner/straight-through rebuild exists. The only way to populate the field is a hand-built `placeStripChain` payload, which the command door accepts because `isStripSegment` validates only finite x/y (commands.ts:199-203).
confirmed.fix: Either populate it at the source (emit `replacesBuildingId: existing.id` from resolveWallStripPlan's 'existing piece' branch, replacing the silent `continue`, so corner/straight-through swaps actually refund) or delete the field, the `replacing` preview branch and `refundHalfBuildingCost` so the code stops advertising a live rule.
confirmed.verification: A repo-wide search for `replacesBuildingId` returns only the two type declarations (stripBuild.ts:29, stripTopology.ts:131) and reads in `buildStripPreview`/`placeStripChain` (buildingPlacementActions.ts:207-208, 230, 269); neither `resolveWallStripPlan` (stripTopology.ts:134-174), `resolveRoadStripPlan` (176-202) nor `resolveStripPlan` (204-219) ever sets it, and the existing-piece branch at 159-162 merely `continue`s. Consequently `refundHalfBuildingCost` (178) is called only from the unreachable `replacementId` branch (269-284), so no replaced building is ever refunded and the documented replacement rule in the comments (stripBuild.ts:28, stripTopology.ts:130) never fires. Since no producer exists this is arguably an unshipped feature plus dead code; the minimal correct action is to delete the field/branch/refund helper, or emit `replacesBuildingId: existing.id` from the wall plan's existing-piece branch if the swap is actually wanted.

confirmed.title: pickBeautySpot returns the up-left corner of its search window when the grid has no beauty
confirmed.evidence: 96: `state.entities.filter((e) => e.type === EntityType.Human && e.alive),` passed to `computeVillageHappiness` (documented at 71 as "average beauty under each settler").
confirmed.impact: Rival settlers and visitor groups (who camp on unbeautified ground far from the village) are counted in the average that produces `state.villageHappiness`, so the Village-mood readout falls purely because a visitor group or rival camp exists on the map — e.g. 10 settlers on beauty 3 plus 8 rivals/visitors on beauty 0 yields 53 instead of 56. `villageHappiness` is display-only (PopulationPanel.tsx:154), so the impact is an incorrect HUD number rather than a simulation change.
confirmed.fix: Filter to colony settlers, e.g. `state.entities.filter((e) => e.type === EntityType.Human && e.alive && isPlayerHuman(e))` (isPlayerHuman is already the project's owner predicate).
confirmed.verification: `bestValue` starts at -1 while `stampDecor` only ever adds non-negative amounts into an Int16Array initialised to 0, so in an all-zero neighbourhood the first in-bounds cell of the dy/dx scan (`tx-radius`, `ty-radius`) beats -1 and is returned, making the documented fallback `best = {x: cx, y: cy}` dead. The only production caller is humanTick.ts:1241-1248, which steers idle pairs toward the result with a 0.35 probability per leisure tick, so pairs in a decor-free village are persistently nudged up-left (up to 5 tiles = 50 px at TERRAIN_TILE_SIZE 10) instead of staying near their company; tests/beauty.decor.test.ts:84-95 only covers a grid containing a garden and the null-grid case. Fix: seed the comparison with the caller's tile (`let bestValue = grid.values[ty * grid.cols + tx] ?? 0;` keeping `best = {x: cx, y: cy}` and the strict `>` test) so a zero-beauty window returns (cx, cy).

confirmed.title: nextBigNewsId is module-level state that is only restored on the main thread, so worker-generated big news reuse already-dismissed ids
confirmed.evidence: simEffects.ts:93 `nextBigNewsId = maxSeq + 1;` driven only by simEffects.ts:86-87 `for (const item of state.bigNews) { const match = /^bn_(\d+)$/.exec(item.id) ...`; simEffects.ts:102-104 `const seq = nextBigNewsId++; state.bigNews.push({ id: \`bn_${seq}\`, ...`. The load path empties that array first: saveLoad.ts:367 `bigNews: [],` then saveLoad.ts:446 `syncBigNewsIdFromState(world);` — while the dismissal ids ARE persisted (saveSchema.ts:22 `'villageForge', 'tutorialSeen', 'dismissedBigNewsIds', ...`) and re-applied as a display filter (useTransientGameFeedback.ts:304-311 `const dismissedIds = new Set(loadedWorld.dismissedBigNewsIds ?? []); ... setHiddenBigNewsIds(dismissedIds);` and :319-321 `.filter((news) => !news.dismissed && !hiddenBigNewsIds.has(news.id))`).
confirmed.impact: Every big-news card a player dismisses (manually or by the 8s auto-dismiss timer, useTransientGameFeedback.ts:241-244 -> dismissBigNewsItem -> dismissedBigNewsIds) leaves a `bn_N` id in the save. After reloading that save, `syncBigNewsIdFromState` sees an empty bigNews list, so the counter restarts at 1 (and the worker thread, which never syncs at all, also starts at 1) and re-issues ids that are already in the persisted dismissed set. `activeBigNews` filters on id, so the first N announcements after a load — festival starts, full-moon Howler warnings, raid-incoming banners — are never shown, where N is the number of announcements dismissed in the previous session (hundreds after a long game). No test covers this (grep of tests for `bigNews`/`dismissedBigNews` returns nothing).
confirmed.fix: Make ids collision-proof across sessions: change `syncBigNewsIdFromState` to take `Pick<WorldState,'bigNews'|'dismissedBigNewsIds'>` and also scan `state.dismissedBigNewsIds` for `/^bn_(\d+)$/` when computing `maxSeq`, and call it from the worker's session/import path (`src/game/simWorker/gameWorker.ts` `resetWorkerSession`/`importSave` handler) as well as from `loadGameFromParsed`; alternatively mint tick-scoped ids (`bn_${state.tick}_${seq}`) and update both regexes in syncBigNewsIdFromState.
confirmed.verification: The mechanism is real: `nextBigNewsId` is module-scoped (81) and `syncBigNewsIdFromState` has exactly one caller, saveLoad.ts:446 on the main thread, while `gameWorker.resetWorkerSession` (gameWorker.ts:118-124) installs an imported world without resyncing it. However the finding's trigger is wrong — `bigNews` is NOT in `WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS` and `loadGameFromParsed` resets `bigNews: []` (saveLoad.ts:367) before syncing, so a load leaves both realms at id 1 and no duplicate occurs after a reload. The reachable path is a new worker instance handed a world that already carries `bn_*` ids (worker fault -> `fallbackFromWorker` -> `attemptWorkerRecovery` -> `init(this.world)`/`importSave`); the reused ids then collide with `dismissedBigNewsIds` and `preserveBigNewsDismissals` (simDelta.ts:15-26) silently suppresses the new card, with duplicate ids inside the worker's own array. Fix: call `syncBigNewsIdFromState(nextWorld)` in `resetWorkerSession` (next to `hydrateWorldRuntimeCaches`), or derive the next id from `state.bigNews` inside `addBigNews`.

confirmed.title: Prisoner early-exit skips shared per-tick upkeep: chat/dialogue timers freeze and pregnancy progress stops
confirmed.evidence: humanTick.ts:388-403 `if (isPrisoner) { ... syncEntityGrids(ctx, entity); continue; }` exits the iteration before humanTick.ts:794-801 `if (isPlayerHuman(entity) && entity.gender === 'female' && entity.pregnant && !conceivedToday && entity.pregnancyProgress !== undefined) { tickPregnancyAndBirth(state, ctx, entity, { livingHumanAt }); }`. Pregnancy can coexist with imprisonment: arrest happens in exposeAffair -> arrestForScandal (humanRelationships.ts:1149-1152, 1203) and the daily gossip path only excludes a pregnancy fathered by the lover (humanRelationships.ts:313-318 `if ((entity.pregnant && entity.pregnantById === lover.id) || ...) return;`), so a married woman pregnant by her husband can be arrested as 'caught'.
confirmed.impact: While imprisoned, `pregnancyProgress` never advances (and the mother also takes no energy loss and no meal), so the term silently stretches by the 2.5-6 day sentence; if a save is taken during that window the progress field and the birth date the player sees diverge from the declared 24-day pregnancy. Any invariant/test that expects a pregnancy to advance every tick while `entity.pregnant` holds is violated for this edge case.
confirmed.fix: Move the pregnancy gate above the prisoner branch (or run it for prisoners before `continue`), i.e. advance existing pregnancy for imprisoned pregnant settlers while still skipping movement/needs.
confirmed.verification: The prisoner branch sets velocity, walks to the prison and `continue`s at 402, before `tickHumanChat` (405) and before the pregnancy gate at 794-802; `chatTicks` is decremented only in humanChat.ts:364 and `tickPregnancyAndBirth` has exactly one caller, humanTick.ts:801 (humanLifecycle.ts:63 is the only progress increment), so both really do freeze for the whole sentence. This is reachable in normal play because `exposeAffair` -> `arrestForScandal` (humanRelationships.ts:1149-1152, 1164-1217) can jail a married pregnant settler for `ticksForDays(2.5 + random*3.5)`, delaying the birth past its due progress and leaving a dialogue bubble frozen; no invariant breaks and no test covers prisoners. Fix: hoist `tickHumanChat(entity, resolveChatPartner)` and the pregnancy block above the `if (isPrisoner)` early exit (or call both before the `continue`).

confirmed.title: reassignDivorcedResidences re-houses an imprisoned custodian and moves minors into the prisoner's home
confirmed.evidence: line 938 `custodian.residenceBuildingId = pickResidenceForHuman(custodian, villagers, residences);` has no prison guard, while the leaver branch immediately below does: line 942 `if (leaver.prisonBuildingId == null) {` ... line 949 `leaver.residenceBuildingId = undefined;`
confirmed.impact: exposeAffair arrests both offenders first (lines 1150-1151) and arrestForScandal clears residenceBuildingId (line 1202) before tryDivorceOnCaughtCheater calls reassignDivorcedResidences. When the offending partner is the wife she becomes the custodian (lines 910-912), so she is immediately handed a fresh residence, the free spouse is evicted to another house (line 947) and the minor children are assigned to the imprisoned mother's house (lines 953-966). The asymmetry with the leaver guard shows the prisoner case was considered only for one of the two settlers.
confirmed.fix: Mirror the leaver guard for the custodian, e.g. wrap lines 936-939 in `if (custodian.prisonBuildingId == null) { ... } else { custodian.residenceBuildingId = undefined; }`, and skip the minor-custody assignment (lines 953-966) when the custodian is imprisoned.
confirmed.verification: The custodian branch at 936-939 has no prison guard while the leaver branch at 942-950 does, and `arrestForScandal` clears `residenceBuildingId` (1202) before `tryDivorceOnCaughtCheater` calls `reassignDivorcedResidences(spouse, cheater, ...)` (1005). When the arrested cheater is the wife she becomes the custodian (910-912), gets a fresh residence through `pickResidenceForHuman` (938), the free spouse is evicted to another house (947) and the minor children are pointed at the imprisoned mother's new house (953-966) — an asymmetry with the leaver guard that shows the prisoner case was only handled once. Impact is limited (no invariant error, the id is a valid player residence) but it is clearly unintended. Fix: mirror the leaver guard for the custodian (`if (custodian.prisonBuildingId == null) { ... } else { custodian.residenceBuildingId = undefined; }`) and skip the minor-custody block when the custodian is imprisoned.

confirmed.title: Ordinary-workplace preview set is defined by exclusion, so residences, roads and decor are counted as affected workplaces and their residents as assigned workers
confirmed.impact: fixedTypes only excludes Church/TownHall/School/Tavern/Hotel, so the 'ordinary' set also contains House/Mansion/LeaderHouse (whose `occupants` are residents, per SIMULATION_AUTHORITY.md §3) as well as Road, Bridge, Wall, Well, Garden, Statue, Lamp, Fence, Silo, WildlifePreserve. `affectedWorkplaces` counts every completed road segment and every house, and `assignedWorkers` sums all housed residents - the WorkSchedulePanel (WorkSchedulePanel.tsx:104-107) then shows the player a badly inflated 'N workplaces / M assigned workers are affected' preview for the ordinary work window. Existing test tests/scheduleFeedback.test.ts only builds Farm/Tavern/Hotel so it cannot catch this.
confirmed.fix: Build the ordinary set from actual staffable workplaces instead of excluding five types — e.g. drop residence types with `isResidenceBuildingType(type)` and OR on an explicit workplace allow-list (the same predicate workforce.ts uses to choose a workplace), so Road/Bridge/Wall/decor and houses are not counted.
confirmed.verification: `staffedBuildingTypes('ordinary')` only excludes Church/TownHall/School/Tavern/Hotel (16-23), so the returned set includes House/Mansion/LeaderHouse, Road, Bridge, Wall, Well, Garden, Statue, Lamp, Fence and the rest; line 33 then counts every completed building of those types and line 34 sums all of their occupants that are living non-faction entities, which for a residence means its residents (minors included). WorkSchedulePanel.tsx:104-107 renders that as "N workplaces / M assigned workers are affected", but the preview is display-only and never mutates state, so the defect is an inflated label rather than a simulation error — hence low, not medium. Fix: build the ordinary set from the same staffable-workplace predicate the workforce owner uses (and drop residence types via `isResidenceBuildingType`) instead of excluding five types.

confirmed.title: Lazy day rollover leaves the raw economyLedger field stale for consumers that bypass getEconomyLedger
confirmed.verification: `ensureLedger` only resets the counters when the new day's first record happens (44-48), so `state.economyLedger.day` stays on yesterday until the first meal or production tick, while `getEconomyLedger` (67-71) exists precisely to return null for a stale day. dashboardData.ts:269-279 and 368-388 read `state.economyLedger` directly and label the totals "Food today"/"foodProducedToday" (rendered as "Food produced today" in GameDashboard.tsx), so early in a day the dashboard reports the previous day's totals as today's and contradicts the Village tab, which goes through `getEconomyLedger` (VillageTabPanel.tsx/citizenOverview.ts). Player-visible but informational only. Fix: roll the ledger at the day boundary from the daily layer (exported `rollEconomyLedgerForDay(state)`), or route dashboardData through `getEconomyLedger(state)`.

confirmed.title: Tamed animals whose owner died keep eating rations forever and can never be hunted
confirmed.verification: `countTamedAnimals` counts every living entity with `tamedBy != null` without checking the owner (38), and the owner lookup at 84-86 silently yields nothing when the owner is dead, so such a pet contributes to the daily `tamed * ANIMAL_DAILY_FOOD` ration with no energy bonus; the only writer that clears `tamedBy` is `cureMoonHowler` (moonHowler.ts:533) and no death path clears it, while `isValidHuntPrey` rejects any prey with `tamedBy != null` (simulationEntities.ts:60). The result is a permanent food sink and un-huntable animals in long games — real but small and self-inflicted only when a pet outlives its owner. Fix: count only pets whose `tamedBy` resolves to a living human (reuse the lookup `tickAnimalCare` already performs), or clear `tamedBy` in the human-death cleanup owner.

confirmed.title: Herd deer bypass the entity-id index that every other spawn path maintains
confirmed.evidence:
44:    if (edge === 0) { x = 40; y = height / 2 + spread; }
(48-54 createEntity(EntityType.Deer, x, y, ...) — no isPassableWildlifePosition check anywhere in spawnHerdAtEdge)
confirmed.impact: Every other spawn path in the codebase gates on terrain (worldGen.spawnWildlifeAtRandomPassable line 224, spawnWildlifeRing line 349); this one uses fixed edge coordinates. Measured by importing the repo's own isPassableWildlifePosition and running tickMigration on real maps (40 maps x 6 presets): coastal 119/400 herd deer spawn on deep/shallow water in 40/40 maps; verdant 45/400 (water/river/riverBank); harsh 76/400 (25 inside Mountains); riverlands 77/400. So a third of a coastal herd starts standing in the sea, on tiles the rest of the simulation treats as unpassable (UNPASSABLE_WILDLIFE_TERRAIN, worldGen.ts:71-78); those deer must wander out before normal land behaviour applies (120 ticks after arrival most blocked deer were still on unpassable tiles), and the player sees deer swimming in the ocean.
confirmed.fix: In spawnHerdAtEdge, validate each candidate point before createEntity with isPassableWildlifePosition(state, x, y, 8) (nudge along the edge, or fall back to spawnWildlifeRing(state, EntityType.Deer, edgeMidX, edgeMidY, count, 40, 120) which already contains the passability retry loop).
confirmed.verification: `spawnHerdAtEdge` creates the deer and only `out.push(deer)` (58), unlike worldGen.ts:123 (`indexLivingEntity`) and `pushNewEntity` (simulationEntities.ts:27, `ctx.entityById.set(...)`), and `ensureEntityByIdMap` reuses the cached canonical map without rescanning (entityIndex.ts:29-33) while nothing in the tick path rebuilds it (only worldGen/saveLoad/hydrate do). The missing entry is observable: tickLayerSystems.ts:212-215 clears `huntTargetId` whenever `entityById.get(targetId)` is not alive, so any hunter that targets a herd deer loses the target on the next systems pass, and other O(1) id lookups (simQueries.getLivingEntity callers, blueberry/hunt helpers) treat the deer as missing for its whole life; the herd still departs correctly because that path scans `state.entities`. Fix: call `indexLivingEntity(state, deer)` (or `ctx.entityById.set`) after setting `deer.migrationTag` — it does not push into `state.entities`, so the BUG-12 concern in the comment is unaffected.

confirmed.title: The half-couple admission guard is unreachable — canAdmitAll is always true
confirmed.impact: createImmigrantSettler is called with maxMembers = openSlots (line 82) and only returns a 2-member couple when `maxMembers >= 2` (worldGen.ts:493). Consequently a 2-person result implies openSlots >= 2, and the only other result is a single settler, so `newcomers.length <= maxHumanPopulation - counts.humans` is always true: the else-branch at 87 and the entire spouse-unlink block at 90-95 (setting relationshipStatus/partnerId/pregnant on newcomers[0], which is the never-pregnant husband) can never run. The dangling-partnerId protection it appears to provide is dead.
confirmed.fix: Either delete lines 86-95 (createImmigrantSettler already caps by maxMembers) or, if the guard is meant to be real, make createImmigrantSettler able to exceed the passed cap (e.g. always roll the couple and let the caller truncate).
confirmed.verification: `openSlots = state.maxHumanPopulation - counts.humans` (60) is the same expression used at 86, and `counts.humans` cannot change in between; `createImmigrantSettler` (worldGen.ts:480-531) returns at most `maxMembers`, returning [] for `maxMembers < 1` and two members only when `maxMembers >= 2`. So `newcomers.length <= openSlots` always holds, `toAdmit === newcomers`, and the couple-splitting cleanup at 90-95 (`relationshipStatus`/`partnerId`/pregnancy clearing) can never execute — the situation the comment describes cannot be produced by this call. Dead code only; no behaviour is lost. Fix: delete lines 85-95 and use `const toAdmit = newcomers;`, or pass an explicit couple cap such as `Math.min(2, openSlots)` to make the guard meaningful.

confirmed.title: tryFirstWeekVisitor doc comment contradicts its own guard (day 4-7 versus tick window for days 7-13)
confirmed.evidence: line 1853 `/** Once per game: friendly visitors on day 4–7 if the player has shelter and no camp yet. */` versus line 1861 `if (state.tick < 7 * TICKS_PER_DAY || state.tick >= 14 * TICKS_PER_DAY) return null;`
confirmed.impact: The comment is the only specification for this once-per-game beat and it is wrong twice: the window is days 7-13, and the 'no camp yet' clause is never tested (the function relies on state.firstWeekVisitorSpawned, line 1859, plus the fact that nothing else can spawn a camp that early). A maintainer aligning the code with the comment would silently undo the deliberate move from day 3-7 to day 7-14 made in commit e1a6d8c, and the comment keeps the reader from noticing that a colony whose first House completes after day 13 never gets the visit at all.
confirmed.fix: Rewrite the comment as `/** Once per game: friendly visitors on days 7-13 (tick < 14 * TICKS_PER_DAY) if the player has a completed House or Mansion; state.firstWeekVisitorSpawned makes it one-shot. */` and drop the 'no camp yet' clause that the code never checks.
confirmed.verification: The comment at 1853 claims "day 4-7 ... and no camp yet" while the guard at 1861 is `state.tick < 7 * TICKS_PER_DAY || state.tick >= 14 * TICKS_PER_DAY` (absolute days 7-13) and the only other condition is a completed player House/Mansion (1863-1869); the one-shot flag `firstWeekVisitorSpawned` (1859/1871) means there is no "no camp yet" test at all. The runtime behaviour is a deliberate one-shot window, so the defect is the misleading specification, and a colony whose first House completes after day 13 never gets the visit. Fix (documentation only): rewrite the comment to state days 7-13, the House/Mansion requirement, and the one-shot flag, and drop the untested "no camp yet" clause.

confirmed.title: pruneDeadBarracksOccupants has no callers, so the only barracks-occupant repair never runs
confirmed.impact: A whole-repo search finds no caller (only the declaration at line 117), so the documented tick/load cleanup never runs; the function is dead code whose stated contract is unfulfilled. Its body also drops any occupant who is dead, missing, non-Soldier, or imprisoned without clearing human.homeBuildingId, so if it were ever invoked for a live-but-imprisoned or reassigned soldier it would leave homeBuildingId pointing at the barracks while that id is gone from occupants - the exact section-5 invariant that collectSimulationInvariantErrors reports as 'missing from that workplace'. Death cleanup is already handled by killHuman -> removeHumanFromBuildingOccupants (humanLifecycleCleanup.ts:45-47), so the function's only unique effect is that hazard.
confirmed.fix: Delete pruneDeadBarracksOccupants (its removal case is already covered by killHuman), or, if load-time pruning is genuinely wanted, clear homeBuildingId for every pruned id and call it from a named transition.
confirmed.verification: A repo-wide search for `pruneDead` / `pruneDeadBarracksOccupants` finds only the definition at 117 — no tick, load, prep or test call site — so the helper documented at 113-116 as the tick/load repair is dead. The failure it targets is real for the invariant checker (a living non-Soldier or imprisoned occupant left in `occupants` is exactly the `listed in workplace #<id> ... but homeBuildingId is <x>` error at simulationInvariants.ts:91-95), although the practical exposure is limited because `arrestForScandal` removes the occupant and clears `homeBuildingId` (humanRelationships.ts:1187-1195) and `killHuman`/`removeWorkerTransition` clean up death and job changes. Fix: call it from the assign/daily reconciliation or the load path, or delete the unused export.

confirmed.title: Vacancy-election due check runs only at the New Year, so the declared 3-month campaign stretches to ~1.4 years and can swallow a scheduled term election
confirmed.evidence:
const electionYear = currentFraction + VACANCY_ELECTION_DELAY_YEARS;
  state.pendingElectionYear = electionYear;   // ... while the only caller is: if (yearRollover) { const vacancyCeremony = tryStartVacancyElectionCeremony(state, state.year, state.dayInYear); }
confirmed.impact: tryStartVacancyElectionCeremony takes dayInYear and compares the full fractional date (`if (currentFraction < state.pendingElectionYear) return false;`), but its only caller sits inside `if (yearRollover)` in dailyWorldEvents.ts, so it is invoked with dayInYear === 0 once per year. A leader who dies on, say, day 20 of year 3 gets pendingElectionYear = 3.06, but the ceremony cannot start until tick 0 of year 4 (about a 0.95-year wait instead of the declared 3 months); the ceremony then never happens mid-year, so the effective delay is uniformly 0.25-1.25 years. getVillageCeremonyStatus/formatElectionDelay keep telling the player 'No village head - merit election in 3 months (Year 4)' and then 'Leadership election imminent - settlers will gather soon.' for up to nine more months, and focusHints reports '0.25 years'.
confirmed.fix: Call `tryStartVacancyElectionCeremony(state, state.year, state.dayInYear)` from the daily path unconditionally (next to `tickLeaderVacancy`, outside the yearRollover block) - the function is already idempotent (it bails on a null pendingElectionYear, an active ceremony, or a future date) - or change the schedule to a whole year boundary so the displayed delay matches the actual one.
confirmed.verification: `tryStartVacancyElectionCeremony` compares `year + dayInYear/DAYS_PER_YEAR` against `pendingElectionYear` (931-934) but its only caller (dailyWorldEvents.ts:230) sits inside `if (yearRollover)` (222-223), and `tickLeaderVacancy` refuses to re-enter once a pending year exists (villageLeadership.ts:889, 902-904), so the due date is only evaluated at integer year boundaries; with `VACANCY_ELECTION_DELAY_YEARS = 0.25` (line 30) a vacancy on day 300 of year 3 (pending 4.083) misses the year-4 rollover and only fires at year 5 — about 14 months, not the 3 months the UI promises (getElectionCeremonyStatus 480-486, getYearsUntilElection 383-387) — and `tryStartTermElectionCeremony` is refused because `pendingElectionYear != null` (958), silently skipping year 4's scheduled term election; the auditor's "~1.4 years" figure is slightly overstated (the range is ~1.0-1.25 years for last-quarter vacancies, and anything in days 0-270 slips to the next New Year). Fix: evaluate the due date at the daily cadence (call `tryStartVacancyElectionCeremony` from `tickLeaderVacancy` or the daily layer whenever `pendingElectionYear != null`) and keep the term-election suppression only while the vacancy is genuinely imminent.

confirmed.title: Opening-night answers are misrouted into stage 2, making resolveStage3 unreachable and always applying the 'cancel the show' outcome
confirmed.evidence: 151: `if (status === STATUS.preparing) return resolveStage2(state, choiceId as Stage2Choice);` — resolveStage1 sets FLAG_STATUS to STATUS.preparing (157) and nothing ever changes it afterwards (resolveStage2 writes only FLAG_SUPPORT at 192/201/205), while the stage-3 card carries the same STORY_KEY (233) and the choices 'correct_story'/'let_legend_grow'/'interrupt' (238-240) match no case in resolveStage2's switch, so they fall into 207-215 `case 'cancel_show': default: {`
confirmed.impact: Answering 'Opening Night' with any of its three choices runs the stage-2 cancel branch: FLAG_RESOLVED/'theatre_story_resolved' is stamped (210) and addBigNews reports 'The troupe leaves offended / The show is cancelled' (213). No reputation is ever granted and resolveStage3 (249-273), including the FLAG_SUPPORT qualityBonus (252) and the 'resolved' logEvent (272), is dead code reachable only if FLAG_STATUS were 0 or >=3. The guided campaign still marks the chapter complete because it reads theatre_story_resolved (guidedCampaign.ts:51), which hides the wrong outcome. Player-visible: three distinct choices always produce one identical 'cancelled' result.
confirmed.fix: Add a distinct status for the resolved-support state (e.g. `performing: 3` to STATUS), set `[FLAG_STATUS]: STATUS.performing` in resolveStage2 for the three non-cancel answers, extend tickTravelingTheatre's guard at 224 to accept it (`!== STATUS.preparing && !== STATUS.performing`), and route `status === STATUS.performing` to resolveStage3 in resolveTravelingTheatre.
confirmed.verification: `FLAG_STATUS` is written only to `script_selected` (93) and `preparing` (158), and `tickTravelingTheatre` pushes the Opening Night card setting only `FLAG_STAGE3` (230), never changing the status; `resolveTravelingTheatre` therefore routes the stage-3 answer through `resolveStage2` (151) because the status is still `preparing`, and since no case in that switch matches `correct_story`/`let_legend_grow`/`interrupt` it falls into `case 'cancel_show': default:` (207-215), stamping `FLAG_RESOLVED` and posting '🎭 The troupe leaves offended'. The stage-3 rewards/reputation are consequently dead code — every Opening Night answer produces the cancellation outcome — and the story is reachable in normal play (storyEvents.ts:240-246 dispatches by `storyKey`, and no test in tests/ covers the theatre). Fix: dispatch on the answered card id (e.g. `if (STAGE3_CHOICES.has(choiceId)) return resolveStage3(...)` before the two status checks, since the id sets are disjoint), or add a `performance` status set by `tickTravelingTheatre` alongside `FLAG_STAGE3`.

confirmed.title: Legacy Church migration runs on every load and strips the player's assigned priest
confirmed.evidence: L531: `const clearedChurchSeats = clearAutoFilledChurches(world);` — called unconditionally from `loadGameFromParsed`; L327-328: `if (human && human.alive && human.homeBuildingId === church.id) {` / `removeWorkerTransition(human, world.buildings);`
confirmed.impact: `loadGameFromParsed` is the browser-load and file-load path, so this runs on every reload. A priest the player assigned by hand is released: `removeWorkerTransition` clears `homeBuildingId` and resets `job`/`occupation` to Settler (workforce.ts:226-228). Nothing refills the Church (`assignMissingWorkers` deliberately skips manual buildings), so Church strength silently drops from 1 to 0.5 (`getChurchStrength`, workforce.ts:107-114) after every save/refresh, and the 'one-time' guard `applySaveMigration('church-manual-staffing')` only guards the log line, never the clearing — the second and later reloads strip the priest with no message at all.
confirmed.fix: Gate the clear on the migration marker instead of running it every load: `const needsChurchMigration = !(world.appliedSaveMigrations ?? []).includes('church-manual-staffing'); const clearedChurchSeats = needsChurchMigration ? clearAutoFilledChurches(world) : 0;` (the marker is already written by the following `applySaveMigration` call when seats were cleared).
confirmed.verification: `clearAutoFilledChurches(world)` is called unconditionally at 531 in `loadGameFromParsed`, and for any completed player Church it releases every occupant whose `homeBuildingId === church.id` through `removeWorkerTransition` (327-328), which clears `homeBuildingId` and resets `job`/`occupation` to Settler (workforce.ts:219-229); the `applySaveMigration('church-manual-staffing')` guard is only consulted for the log line (489-494, 532-537), and it never suppresses the clearing. Player entity fields are persisted whole (entities travel inside `pickWorldFieldsForSave`), so a hand-assigned priest is re-cleared on every browser/file load, `getChurchStrength` drops from 1 to 0.5 because it counts `homeBuildingId` (workforce.ts:107-114), and nothing refills the Church because `assignMissingWorkers` skips manual buildings (workforce.ts:148, 278); tests/church.manualStaffing.test.ts tests the helper in isolation and does not exercise the load path. Fix: gate the clear on the marker (`const needsChurchMigration = !(world.appliedSaveMigrations ?? []).includes('church-manual-staffing'); const cleared = needsChurchMigration ? clearAutoFilledChurches(world) : 0;`).

confirmed.title: Event-log id allocator is per-realm and is never re-synced when a world is handed to the worker, so worker chronicle entries are dropped by the delta dedupe
confirmed.evidence: L4: `let nextEventLogId = 1;`  L12: `nextEventLogId = Math.max(...state.eventLog.map((e) => e.id)) + 1;`  L24: `id: nextEventLogId++,` — the only callers of `syncEventLogIdFromState` are `saveLoad.ts:445` and `worldGen.ts:683` (both main thread). The worker entry points `simPrep.ts:245 world.eventLog = prep.eventLog;` and `gameWorker.ts:118-124 resetWorkerSession` never call it, and `SimPrepPayload` carries `eventLog` (simPrep.ts:67,161) but no id counter.
confirmed.impact: Any freshly created (or recovered) worker starts allocating ids from 1 while the imported log already holds ids 1..N (N = entries in the save, up to the 2000 cap). `applySimTickDelta` skips tail entries whose id already exists (`simDelta.ts:513 if (!existingIds.has(entry.id))`), so the first N events the worker logs never reach the display copy: after loading a mid/late game the in-game Chronicle silently freezes for hundreds-to-thousands of events even though the simulation keeps logging. The same untracked counter is used by the optimistic display path (`gameLoop.ts:540-542 applyWorkerCommand` on a clone of the worker's shadow world), which can allocate an id that the worker has already used, producing duplicate ids in one log (duplicate React `key={evt.id}` in EventLogPanel.tsx:197).
confirmed.fix: Make the allocator travel with the log: add `import { syncEventLogIdFromState } from '../eventLog';` to `simPrep.ts` and call `syncEventLogIdFromState(world)` immediately after `world.eventLog = prep.eventLog;` (L245) — alternatively call it in `gameWorker.ts resetWorkerSession` (L118-124) so the worker's ids continue above the restored log.
confirmed.verification: `nextEventLogId` is module-scoped (4) and `syncEventLogIdFromState` has only the two main-thread callers saveLoad.ts:445 and worldGen.ts:683, while `resetWorkerSession` (gameWorker.ts:118-124) installs the imported world — whose `eventLog` carries ids 1..N from the save — without resyncing, so a fresh worker allocates ids from 1 again (24). `applySimTickDelta` skips incoming tail entries whose id already exists in the display log (simDelta.ts:504-517), so after loading a save in worker mode the main-thread Chronicle silently ignores the worker's new entries until its counter passes the saved maximum (up to the 2000-entry cap), while the worker's own log holds duplicate ids; tests/simDelta.eventLog.test.ts only uses non-colliding ids and does not lock the allocator. Fix: import and call `syncEventLogIdFromState(world)` in the worker right after the world is installed (`simPrep.ts:245` or preferably `gameWorker.resetWorkerSession`), or compute the next id from `state.eventLog` inside `logEvent`.

confirmed.title: Off-screen wildlife throttle counts ticks, not wildlife-layer calls, so it was never rescaled for the 72-tick day / 4-tick layer
confirmed.evidence:
src/game/tickLayerSystems.ts:253-254: `const wildlifeActive = wildlifeInFocus || (state.tick + entity.id) % OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE === 0;`
src/game/simFocus.ts:25-26: `/** How often off-screen wildlife runs full AI (every N wildlife-layer calls). */ export const OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE = 8;`
confirmed.impact: tickWildlife runs only when `state.tick % WILDLIFE_LAYER_INTERVAL === 0` (LAYER_SYSTEMS_INTERVAL = 4, gameTick.ts:198), but the throttle is tested against the raw tick, so off-screen fauna get full AI on every second layer pulse (every 8 ticks), not one in eight pulses as the constant's declared unit states. The sibling OFFSCREEN_HUMAN_THROTTLE was explicitly rescaled for TICKS_PER_DAY=72 (8 -> 24, locked by tests/dayCycle.cadence.test.ts:95-99) but this one was left at 8, so off-screen wildlife decisions per in-game day are 3x the legacy rate (9/day vs 3/day) and the off-screen AI budget is 4x the declared one.
confirmed.fix: Either count layer pulses (`(Math.floor(state.tick / WILDLIFE_LAYER_INTERVAL) + entity.id) % OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE === 0`) or keep tick units and set the constant to `8 * TICKS_PER_HOUR`; update the docstring and extend tests/dayCycle.cadence.test.ts with the wildlife throttle assertion.
confirmed.verification: gameTick.ts:198 runs tickLayerSystems only when state.tick % 4 === 0, while tickLayerSystems.ts:253-254 tests (state.tick + entity.id) % 8 on the raw tick, and simFocus.ts:25 states the unit as 'every N wildlife-layer calls'; the human sibling was rescaled to 24 and is locked by tests/dayCycle.cadence.test.ts:95-99. The consequence is worse than the claimed 3x rate: since the layer tick is always a multiple of 4, (tick+id) % 8 === 0 has no solution for ids ≡ 1, 2 or 3 (mod 4), so ~75% of out-of-focus fauna never pass the throttle gate (the `continue` at 255-259 skips movement, hunting, grazing at 526-571 and reproduction at 681-736) while the unconditional metabolic drain at line 242 still runs every pulse — they starve off-camera; the ids that do pass (≡ 0 mod 4) run AI every second pulse, not one in eight. Minimal fix: gate on the layer-pulse index, e.g. (Math.floor(state.tick / WILDLIFE_LAYER_INTERVAL) + entity.id) % OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE === 0, or keep tick units and set the constant to 8 * TICKS_PER_HOUR with the docstring corrected, and add the assertion to tests/dayCycle.cadence.test.ts.

confirmed.title: Irrigation's research effect target `drought_resist` is never read, so the tech has no effect
confirmed.evidence:
gameTypes.ts:909 `{ id: 'agriculture_3', ... name: 'Irrigation', description: 'Farms work 50% better in drought', ... effects: [{ target: 'drought_resist', multiplier: 1.5 }], ... }`
grassEcology.ts:55-56 `case WeatherType.Drought:` / `return 0.5;`
(whole-repo grep for `drought_resist` matches only gameTypes.ts:909; no code calls `getMultiplier(state, 'drought_resist')` and nothing checks `hasTech(state, 'agriculture_3')`)
confirmed.impact: A tier-3 research that costs 60 wood / 60 stone / 80 gold (and prerequisites agriculture_1+agriculture_2) advertises "Farms work 50% better in drought", but the drought farm penalty is applied unconditionally in `getWeatherFarmMultiplier` and the effect record is never queried, so the player pays for and receives nothing. The same 'declared target with no consumer' pattern exists for `all_food` (908), `lumber_pollution` (913), `building_health` (914), `human_lifespan` (916) and `plague_immunity` (917), but those nodes' promises are delivered by other mechanisms (building `unlockRequirement` ids, `hasTech('forestry_2')` in dailyEcology.ts:82, `hasTech('medicine_2')` in worldEvents.ts:171), so only `drought_resist` is a live defect.
confirmed.fix: Consume the effect where the drought penalty is applied — e.g. in `getWeatherFarmMultiplier` (or its farm caller in dailyBuildingEconomy) multiply the `Drought` factor by `getMultiplier(state, 'drought_resist')` — or delete the unused `effects` entry and the drought sentence from the node description.
confirmed.verification: gameTypes.ts:909 declares `effects: [{ target: 'drought_resist', multiplier: 1.5 }]` for agriculture_3 and a repo-wide grep finds no reader: getMultiplier(state, 'drought_resist') is never called and grassEcology.getWeatherFarmMultiplier returns the 0.5 Drought factor unconditionally (its only callers, dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:346/637, combine it with farm_yield/global_efficiency only). The node is reachable and purchasable — research.syncResearchUnlocks unlocks it once agriculture_2 is unlocked, and startResearch charges 60 wood / 60 stone / 80 gold — so the player pays for a promised effect that no code delivers; unlike all_food/forestry_2/medicine_2, whose promises are met by other mechanisms (buildings.ts:287 unlockRequirement, dailyEcology.ts:82 hasTech('forestry_2'), worldEvents.ts:171 hasTech('medicine_2')). Minimal fix: multiply the Drought factor by getMultiplier(state, 'drought_resist') where the penalty is applied, or delete the inert effect entry and the drought sentence from the description.

confirmed.title: auditHousingSharingIssues/isUnnecessarilySharingHousing (and residenceHasCapacity) have no callers, and the dead audit counts rival and leader residences as empty housing
confirmed.evidence: residencySelection.ts:267-268 `const unit: Entity[] = [custodian]; visited.add(custodian.id);` — the bucket loop never checks `visited.has(custodianId)` before building the unit (contrast the fallback loop at line 284: `if (visited.has(human.id)) continue;` and the partner guard at line 270 `if (partner && !visited.has(partner.id))`).
confirmed.impact: Concrete failure: mother M has minor child A (custodian M), father F has minor child B (custodian F, B's mother dead), and M and F are partners (a blended family created by remarriage — reachable through humanTick.ts:910/tryCompleteCourtshipMarriage). Bucket[M]=[A] builds unit [M,F,A] and marks F visited, but bucket[F]=[B] still builds unit [F,B] containing F again. In assignMissingResidences (residencyReconciliation.ts:230-239) every unit that needs reassignment clears and re-places ALL of its members, so F is moved twice per pass and the two units keep stealing him: [F,B] is placed in an empty house, then [M,F,A] (now invalid) is cleared and placed in another empty house, and the 24-pass loop never records `reassigned === 0`, so it runs all 24 passes on every assign pulse (4x/day). The stable end state leaves the minor child B alone in one house while F, M and A occupy another — the exact opposite of assignFamilyToResidence's contract ('keeps children with custodian'); ensureOrphanAdoption cannot repair it because B still has a living natural custodian, so the split persists across pulses.
confirmed.fix: Add the missing guard at the top of the bucket loop: `if (visited.has(custodianId)) continue;` (and attach that bucket's children to the custodian's existing unit, or rebuild the children buckets from the emitted units) so each settler belongs to exactly one housing unit; the child whose custodian is already in a unit must join that unit rather than fall through to the single-entity fallback at line 283.
confirmed.verification: A repo-wide grep finds no call site for residencySelection.auditHousingSharingIssues / isUnnecessarilySharingHousing or residencyOccupancy.residenceHasCapacity (residencyOccupancy.ts:86) besides the dayCycle.ts re-export block (lines 79/92/97), so nothing ever consumes the computed issues. The dead audit's `buildings.filter(isResidenceBuilding)` at line 498 includes rival-camp houses and the Leader's House, and countResidentsInBuilding ignores rival humans, so those beds read as empty — matching the claim. The suggested replacement is inaccurate, however: listPlayerResidences (line 35-37) filters only `b.faction !== 'rival'` and does not skip the manor, so the fix must add an isLeaderHouseResidence exclusion. Minimal fix: delete the unused trio, or filter properly and add a caller plus a test.

confirmed.title: Demolition reports the nominal refund even when the capped add added nothing
confirmed.evidence: lines 188-190 `addResource(state, 'wood', refundWood);` (its capped return value is discarded) followed by line 201 `addFloatingText(state, building.x, building.y - 10, \`Refunded: ${refundWood}w ${refundStone}s\`, '#eab308');`.
confirmed.impact: `addResource` -> `addCappedResource` (resourceUtils.ts:38-48) clamps to `storageMax` and returns the amount actually added. With a full wood store (worldGen.ts:577 caps wood at 1000, stone at 500) demolishing a Wall reports 'Refunded: 4w 7s' while 0 wood and 0 stone were received, so the player-facing ledger disagrees with the authoritative resources.
confirmed.fix: Capture the returns and print what was actually granted, e.g. `const gotWood = addResource(state, 'wood', refundWood); const gotStone = addResource(state, 'stone', refundStone);` and use `gotWood`/`gotStone` in the floating text.
confirmed.verification: demolishBuilding discards the returns of addResource at lines 188-190 and prints the nominal refundWood/refundStone in the floating text at line 201; resourceUtils.addCappedResource (lines 38-48) clamps to getStorageCap and returns the amount actually added. worldGen.ts:577 caps wood at 1000 and stone at 500, so demolishing with a full store shows 'Refunded: Xw Ys' while 0 (or less) reached storage; the authoritative resources themselves are correct, so this is a misreported player-facing number only. Minimal fix: capture the returns and print those, e.g. `const gotWood = addResource(...); const gotStone = addResource(...)`.

confirmed.title: pathCache stores origin-dependent waypoint lists under origin-independent keys, so a settler can be steered back to a stale path origin
confirmed.evidence: 269: `const steps = Math.max(4, Math.min(128, Math.ceil(span / (TERRAIN_TILE_SIZE * 0.5))));` (comment 268: "Sub-tile sampling steps prevent tunneling through 1-tile diagonal obstacles")
confirmed.impact: `TERRAIN_TILE_SIZE` is 10 (gameTypes.ts:992) and the intended step is 5px, but the 128 cap makes the real spacing span/128: 11.7px for a full medium-map line (1200x900 -> span ~1500px) and ~25px on a huge map (2560x1920 -> span ~3200px), i.e. larger than the tile itself. A 1-tile river or mountain strip can fall between two samples, so `lineCrossesBlocked` returns false, `steerWithPath` returns 'direct' (316/349) and the human walks straight through water/mountain — the exact failure the module was written to prevent. Humans have no terrain collision (only wildlife has the deep-water guard, tickLayerSystems.ts:609-628), so nothing downstream corrects it.
confirmed.fix: Raise the cap so the step can never exceed half a tile (and the tile width for every supported map size), e.g. `const steps = Math.max(4, Math.min(1024, Math.ceil(span / (TERRAIN_TILE_SIZE * 0.5))));`.
confirmed.verification: steerWithPath caches pathWaypoints(findPath(...)) under the caller's key (lines 319-331) and pathCache is cleared only when the PathGrid object changes (lines 288-291) or the cache exceeds 200 entries (line 329), while simulation/humanMovement.commutePathCacheKey builds `c_<entityId>_<buildingId>_<h|w>` from the entity id alone (lines 92-93). pathWaypoints includes the start tile as wp[0] (pathfinding.ts:254-257) and the skip loop at line 335 can only move forward, so when the same settler's home leg later starts somewhere else (humanTick.ts:710, humanLeisureBehavior.ts:62/104 all call commuteHumanToBuilding with arrivingHome=true from wherever the settler stands) the entity steers toward the old origin — a visible wrong-direction detour, travelled by direct velocity with no collision check. Minimal fix: cache { originX, originY, wp } and recompute when the entity is farther than ~2 tiles from the stored origin.

confirmed.title: Juvenile size uses HUMAN_ADULT_MIN_AGE (16) while isJuvenile is later overwritten from HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS (12), producing half-size adults
confirmed.evidence: entityFactory.ts:66 `isJuvenile ?? (isHuman && opts?.ageYears !== undefined ? opts.ageYears < HUMAN_ADULT_MIN_AGE : false);` with `HUMAN_ADULT_MIN_AGE = 16` (dayCycleConstants.ts:12), used at entityFactory.ts:110 `size: effectiveJuvenile ? config.size * 0.5 : config.size,`; but the same function then calls entityFactory.ts:159 `setHumanBirthFromAge(entity, opts.ageYears, opts.colonyDay ?? 0);`, which recomputes the flag with a different threshold — dayCycle.ts:212 `entity.isJuvenile = entity.age < HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS;` (HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS = 12, dayCycle.ts:126), and `syncHumanAgeFromCalendar` (dayCycle.ts:246) uses 12 as well.
confirmed.impact: For any caller that passes `ageYears` without an explicit `isJuvenile` (the exported factory API and the branch the code was written for), an entity aged 12–15 is created with `isJuvenile === false` but `size === config.size * 0.5`; `tryGraduateHumanChild` (dayCycle.ts:135 `if (!entity.isJuvenile || entity.age < HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS) return false;`) then refuses to promote it, so the settler renders at half size for life while every age-gated rule treats them as an adult. Today's in-repo callers all pass `isJuvenile` explicitly (worldGen.ts:499/510/539/770/781, groupEvents.ts:284, settlerInteractionActions.ts:91) so the path is latent, not live.
confirmed.fix: Use the dayCycle owner's threshold for the auto-detect branch (`opts.ageYears < HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS`) so `size` and `isJuvenile` agree after `setHumanBirthFromAge`, or drop the auto-detect branch and require the caller's `isJuvenile` argument.
confirmed.verification: createEntity derives size and the initial isJuvenile from `opts.ageYears < HUMAN_ADULT_MIN_AGE` (16) at lines 65-66/110/117, then calls setHumanBirthFromAge for every ageYears value (line 159), and that owner sets `entity.isJuvenile = entity.age < HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS` (12) at dayCycle.ts:212 — so ageYears 12-15 (or isJuvenile: true plus an adult age) yields a half-size entity with isJuvenile false. The mismatch is real and reachable through the public factory, but latent today: every current caller passes isJuvenile=false with an age >= 16 (worldGen.ts:499/510/515/539/775/787, groupEvents.ts:277-285, settlerInteractionActions.ts:84-92) or isJuvenile=true with no ageYears (humanLifecycle.ts:142-155), so no player-visible effect exists. Minimal fix: use HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS in the factory, or assign entity.size after setHumanBirthFromAge from entity.isJuvenile.

confirmed.title: Second implementation of the settler energy-drain rule in the throttled path, with a different modifier set
confirmed.evidence: humanTick.ts:430-434 `let minimalEnergyLoss = hasWell ? config.energyLossPerTick * 0.8 : config.energyLossPerTick; if (hasHospital) minimalEnergyLoss *= 0.9; if (isWinter && !canHeat) minimalEnergyLoss *= 1.5; minimalEnergyLoss *= traitMultiplier(entity, 'hardy', 0.85);` — the on-screen path instead calls `humanEnergyLoss(entity, config, {...})` (humanTick.ts:516). humanNeeds.ts:161-162 applies `if (isNearHome && isRestingPeriod) { loss *= ENERGY_MODIFIERS.HOME_RESTING_REDUCTION; }` (0.5), humanNeeds.ts:142 applies the greenthumb 0.7 winter resistance, and humanNeeds.ts:174 applies `traitMultiplier(entity, 'fierce', ...)` (0.9).
confirmed.impact: An off-screen settler drains ~2x the energy of an identical on-screen settler at night (resting half-rate missing), plus 11% (fierce) and up to ~43% extra in an unheated winter (greenthumb missing). Because `active` is false purely from viewport focus (humanTick.ts:377-384), exhaustion and `killFromExhaustion` (humanTick.ts:437-439, 1474-1476) become a function of where the player is looking: a settler standing in their own home can die of exhaustion off-screen while the same settler would rest on-screen.
confirmed.fix: Call the single owner in the off-screen branch as well: `entity.energy -= humanEnergyLoss(entity, config, { hasWell, isWinter, canHeat, hasHospital, tick: state.tick, hourOfDay, buildingById });` (the helper is already imported at humanTick.ts:99 and is only a handful of multiplications), deleting the divergent inline copy.
confirmed.verification: The not-active branch of tickHumans re-implements the drain at humanTick.ts:430-434 with only well/hospital/winter/hardy, while the owner humanEnergyLoss (humanNeeds.ts:127-176) also applies greenthumb, fierce and the 0.5 home-resting reduction; this same function already routes both the meal rule (tryEatColonyMeal at line 436) and the active path (lines 516-524) through the shared owners, which is exactly the pattern the CHANGELOG's larder fix established (BUG_REPORTS/2026-09-10-larder-meal-rule-duplicated.md exists). Because the `active` gate includes inFocus (lines 377-384), a settler resting at home loses 0.5x base energy on camera and 1.0x off camera, so camera position changes exhaustion-death odds. Minimal fix: replace lines 430-434 with the same humanEnergyLoss(entity, config, {...}) call used at 516-524.

confirmed.title: RELATIONSHIP_CONFIG carries a second, unread definition of the amicable-divorce rate
confirmed.evidence: lines 63-64 inside RELATIONSHIP_CONFIG: `AMICABLE_DIVORCE_ANNUAL_RATE: 0.075,` / `AMICABLE_DIVORCE_DAILY_CHANCE: 0.075 / DAYS_PER_YEAR,`; the value actually used is the exported duplicate at line 860 `export const MARRIAGE_DAILY_AMICABLE_DIVORCE_CHANCE = MARRIAGE_ANNUAL_AMICABLE_DIVORCE_RATE / DAYS_PER_YEAR;`, read at line 877 `if (rng() >= MARRIAGE_DAILY_AMICABLE_DIVORCE_CHANCE) return;`

confirmed.verification: A repo-wide search shows RELATIONSHIP_CONFIG.AMICABLE_DIVORCE_ANNUAL_RATE and .AMICABLE_DIVORCE_DAILY_CHANCE (lines 63-64) have no reader; every other member of that object is read (SCHOOLYARD_BOND_* at 394-428, SCANDAL_COOLDOWN_TICKS at 891, DIVORCE_CAUGHT_CHANCE at 986/1010), so the omission is specific to the divorce pair. tryDailyAmicableDivorce rolls against the separate exported MARRIAGE_DAILY_AMICABLE_DIVORCE_CHANCE (line 860, used at 877), which is derived from MARRIAGE_ANNUAL_AMICABLE_DIVORCE_RATE — tuning the config field silently does nothing, violating AGENTS.md 5.2 / SIMULATION_AUTHORITY §3's one-source-of-truth rule. confirmed.title: Friendship map keys are never pruned, so dead settlers keep counting as friends and boosting energy
confirmed.evidence: 193: `for (const val of Object.values(p.friendships)) {` … 201: `p.energy = Math.min(maxEnergy, currentEnergy + boost);` — no liveness check, unlike the feud loop's 153: `if (!other) { delete feuds[key]; continue; }`
confirmed.impact: The feud half of the same function explicitly deletes records whose counterpart is no longer among the living (`byId`), but nothing prunes `friendships` — reconcileFamilyReferencesAfterRemoval clears partner/affair/children links only. A survivor therefore keeps every dead friend's score and keeps collecting up to +2 energy/day from them forever ('Strong friends lift each other's spirits'), and each settler's friendship record grows monotonically as roommates and co-workers die. friendCount() (45-52) likewise counts dead friends.
confirmed.fix: In the same daily pass, delete friendship keys whose counterpart is missing from `byId` (mirroring the feud cleanup) and compute `strongCount` only over living counterparts.
confirmed.verification: advanceSocialRelationships prunes feuds for missing partners (relationships.ts:150-156) but the strong-friendship loop (lines 189-203) counts every friendship key >= 60 without consulting the byId map built from living people (line 73), so a dead friend keeps contributing to strongCount and its key is never deleted; the daily energy boost is min(2, strongCount * 0.8) at line 200, so the effect is real but saturates once three strong keys exist. The finding overstates one detail: friendCount (line 45) and activeFeudCount (line 55) have no callers anywhere, so the 'UI badges' half has no consumer. Minimal fix: resolve each key against byId inside the strong-friendship loop and delete or skip missing settlers, mirroring the feud cleanup.

confirmed.title: Hospital treatment gate is a day-stable roll re-evaluated every tick, so treatment (skill and food) repeats per tick
confirmed.impact: The roll is constant for the whole colony day, so once it passes and the settler is within 36px of a staffed hospital the call happens on every tick. Human energy loss is 4.2/3 = 1.4 per tick (speciesConfig.ts:134), so `heal = min(deficit, 8 + strength*14)` is >= 0.5 nearly every tick and treatPatientAtHospital does not bail: each call grants `gainSkill(state, id, JobType.Doctor, 0.08)` to every hospital occupant (hospitalCare.ts:106-108) and has a 25% chance to spend 1 food (hospitalCare.ts:99-101). A pending mother or low-energy settler hovering at the ward therefore produces dozens of treatments per day (up to ~18 food and several skill points per occupant) instead of the intended ~20%-of-days event.
confirmed.fix: Gate the attempt once per settler per day (a `lastHospitalTreatmentDay` marker set after a successful treatment) or move it into the daily ward round that already exists (`tickHospitalDailyCare`, hospitalCare.ts:173), rather than re-rolling a day-stable value every tick.
confirmed.verification: tickHumanHospitalPatientCare is called every tick for active humans (humanTick.ts:1095) and gates treatment on personDayRoll(entity.id, state.tick, 840) < 0.2 (line 94), which humanSchedule.ts:97-107 defines as stable for a whole colony day; treatPatientAtHospital then heals, has a 25% chance to spend 1 food and grants gainSkill(JobType.Doctor, 0.08) to every hospital occupant on each call (hospitalCare.ts:99-108). shouldAttemptHospitalTreatment (lines 40-43) passes unconditionally for a pregnant settler, and with a 1.4/tick drain the heal is > 0.5 almost every tick, so a pregnant settler parked in the ward is treated ~72 times per qualifying day instead of on ~20% of days — roughly 18 food and 5.8 skill points per occupant, with doctor skill capped at 100 in ~17 days. Minimal fix: latch one treatment per settler per colony day, or move the work into the existing daily tickHospitalDailyCare round (hospitalCare.ts:173).

confirmed.title: NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_DAYS guard can never fire, so valley stage changes are never rate-limited
confirmed.evidence: ecologyStage.ts:365-368 `const cooldownOk = day - (state.valleyLastStageNotifyDay ?? -999) >= NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_DAYS || rising || valleyStageIndex(next) <= valleyStageIndex(prev) - 1;` and line 370 `if (!cooldownOk && !rising) return;`
confirmed.impact: `announceStage` is only reached when `next !== current` (line 453), and every transition it can produce is exactly one step (line 445 `STAGE_ORDER[Math.min(newIdx, 3)]` with newIdx = currentIdx+1 capped at 2, line 450 `currentIdx - 1`). Therefore `!rising` implies `valleyStageIndex(next) === valleyStageIndex(prev) - 1`, the third disjunct is always true, `cooldownOk` is always true, and the early return at line 370 is unreachable: the 3-day re-notify cooldown and the `valleyLastStageNotifyDay` field it depends on can never suppress a message.
confirmed.fix: Either drop the third disjunct and gate on the cooldown alone (`if (day - (state.valleyLastStageNotifyDay ?? -999) < NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_DAYS) return;`), or delete NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_DAYS, `valleyLastStageNotifyDay` and the guard if one notification per transition is the intent.
confirmed.verification: announceStage is called only when next !== current (ecologyStage.ts:453), and the only writers of `next` produce exactly one-level moves — up at line 431 (currentIdx + 1, possibly capped down to equal current, in which case announceStage is never called) and down at line 450 (STAGE_ORDER[max(0, currentIdx - 1)]) — so the third disjunct at line 368 is true for every recovery and `rising` for every escalation, making cooldownOk always true. NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_DAYS (line 72) and valleyLastStageNotifyDay (written at 372, read only at 366) are therefore dead, and a village oscillating across the strained/stable boundary pushes a fresh notification each time. Latent only because ValleyEcology.ENABLED is false (gameConstants.ts:148). Minimal fix: drop the always-true third disjunct so the cooldown throttles recovery notices, or delete the guard plus the unused constant/field.

confirmed.title: Duplicate Grassland return makes the dry-grassland branch a no-op

confirmed.title: Challenge ledger records the nominal food reward instead of the amount storage actually accepted

confirmed.title: Unreachable storage-shortfall branch in tradeWithVisitors would return a paid-for, partially delivered world
confirmed.evidence: line 1451 `const added = addCappedResource(state, key, amount);` / line 1452 `if (added < amount) {` / line 1453 `return rejectVisitorTrade(` ... `'Trade cancelled — not enough storage space.'`

confirmed.title: Local pushNews builds big-news ids from array length, producing duplicate ids when two pushes happen on one tick at the cap
confirmed.impact: room is not floored at 0, so when a resource already exceeds its cap a successful outgoing raid or accepted tribute removes that resource. Example: food 1000 with a cap that has dropped to 800 (demolishing a Barn or Silo recomputes caps in economy.ts:8-21 while stores stay put; demolition refunds add resources uncapped in buildingPlacementActions.ts:180-182) - winning a raid with 40 food spoils evaluates Math.min(800-1000, 40) = -200 and drops food to 800. The rest of the codebase floors headroom (resourceUtils.ts:43, VisitorCampPanel.tsx:30) and clampRaidGoldGain already floors gold, so this is an omission, not the established convention.
confirmed.fix: Floor each room term: const room = Math.max(0, state.storageMax.food - state.resources.food); (and the same for wood, stone, gold).
confirmed.verification: frontierCombat's local pushNews builds the id from the live array length (line 373) and trims only after the push (line 380), so with bigNews already at the 50-entry cap the first push uses length 50 and is shifted back to 50, letting a second same-tick push reuse `raid_<tick>_50`; tickPendingOutgoingRaidEvents pushes once per expired event (line 1231) and every event expiring on that tick is processed together, so two rivals' war-bands produce the collision. Reaching the cap is routine because addBigNews keeps the array at 50 once it fills (simEffects.ts:111), and ids are dismissal identity — useTransientGameFeedback filters by id (lines 61-62 and 192) — so dismissing one banner also removes the duplicate, and the id scheme bypasses the monotonic addBigNews/syncBigNewsIdFromState owner (simEffects.ts:84-111). Minimal fix: call addBigNews from frontierCombat instead of the local pushNews (groupEvents.ts:37-47 already uses a counter-based id).

confirmed.lines: 207-209, 242, 259, 277, 288 | 207-209 (callers: src/game/humanVenueBehavior.ts:88 and :122, both reached per tick from src/game/humanTick.ts:1086-1107)
confirmed.title: Civic petitions re-award every tick: per-day rolls are used as per-tick gates, so reputation/gold/food move at tick rate
confirmed.impact: personDayRoll hashes entityId + getAbsoluteCalendarDay(tick) (dayCycleClock.ts:28, humanSchedule.ts:98-107), so it returns the SAME value for all 72 ticks of a colony day: the guard is a per-day pass/fail, not a rate limit. resolveCivicPetition is called every tick for an official on duty near the hall (humanVenueBehavior.ts:88 -> officialHandlePetitioners, whose petitioner pick at townHall.ts:329 is also day-stable) and every tick for a free-roaming settler near a hall (humanVenueBehavior.ts:121-122); `active` is true every tick for in-focus humans and for ALL humans whenever there is no camera focus (humanTick.ts:378-384, 429-442). So a scandalized/grieving settler near a staffed hall takes the 'heard' branch (line 251-259) and gets +1 village reputation EVERY TICK (up to 72/day, pinning the 0-100 clamp within a day or two), a forced chat line via sayHumanChatPhrase (which ignores chatTicks and clears the dialogue session key, humanChat.ts:332-341), and a floating text every tick; the food-aid branch debits up to 4 food/tick and the stipend branch 1 gold/tick until the settler's energy passes the branch threshold. The declared intent ('at most one meaningful petition per person per few days', and +1 reputation per petition) is defeated.
confirmed.fix: Enforce a real per-person cadence: add an explicit day stamp (e.g. `lastCivicPetitionDay?: number` on Entity, checked/set here as `if (petitioner.lastCivicPetitionDay === day) return { kind: 'none' }; petitioner.lastCivicPetitionDay = day;`) and carry it through saveSchema/simPrep/simDelta; if no new field is wanted, gate the decision to the day-boundary tick (`if (state.tick % TICKS_PER_DAY !== 0) return { kind: 'none' };`) so the day-stable rolls can only be evaluated once per day.
confirmed.verification: resolveCivicPetition's only per-person gate is personDayRoll(petitioner.id, state.tick, 821 + day) > 0.4 (line 209), and personDayRoll is documented and implemented as constant for a whole colony day (humanSchedule.ts:97-107), while both realtime callers invoke the resolver every tick: officialHandlePetitioners (humanVenueBehavior.ts:88) and the free-time path (humanVenueBehavior.ts:121-122), even though the intended cadence already exists as the daily tickTownHallAudiences (townHall.ts:345-362, at most two petitions per day). On a qualifying day the same branch re-applies per tick: the grief/scandal 'heard' branch grants addReputation(1) and +6 energy with no other condition (lines 247-261), the leader-audience branch likewise (264-278), and the aid branches restore energy to a level that keeps them eligible for several more ticks; grief lasts 5-7 days (humanLifecycleCleanup.ts:72-73), so a grieving settler parked at the hall drives reputation to the 100 cap in roughly 100 ticks and spends food/gold at tick rate. Minimal fix: latch one resolved petition per petitioner per colony day (a stamped field or a per-day marker), or move the effects into the daily owner so the per-day roll only selects the day.

confirmed.title: tickInventionFair re-pushes a fresh Demonstration card every colony day because nothing records that the card was already offered

confirmed.fix: Read FLAG_INVENTION in tickInventionFair/resolveStage2 to vary the demonstration description and the keep/improve effect per invention, or delete the flag and its hashSalt computation.
confirmed.verification: tickInventionFair only returns on FLAG_RESOLVED or a non-funded FLAG_STATUS (lines 199-203) and pushes a card whose id embeds state.tick (line 212) without stamping any one-shot flag, unlike its sibling travelingTheatre.ts:225-230 which latches FLAG_STAGE3 before pushing; it runs once per day (dailyWorldEvents.ts:125), pushStoryCard dedupes by id only (storyHelpers.ts:27-32), cards live 4 days and App.tsx:1458-1460 renders up to two, so a duplicate 'The Demonstration' appears each day until the player answers.
