confirmed.title: SimTickDelta never carries `visitorQuest`, so the smith quest is invisible to the main thread in worker mode
confirmed.evidence: L92-94: `activeVillageRequest: WorldState['activeVillageRequest'];` / `villageRequestCooldownUntilDay: number;` / `villageRequestHistory: NonNullable<WorldState['villageRequestHistory']>;` — the sibling `WorldState.visitorQuest` (gameTypes.ts:741) appears nowhere in `SimTickDelta`, `extractSimTickDelta` or `applySimTickDelta`.
confirmed.impact: `visitorQuest` is created/expired only inside the worker (`groupEvents.ts:416` → `maybeStartVisitorQuest`, `dailyWorldEvents.ts:99` → `tickVisitorQuest`, both called from the tick layers). With the worker active the display world's `visitorQuest` stays undefined forever, so App.tsx:1544-1546 (`getVisitorQuest(world)`) never renders the traveling-smith card, and virtualPlayer.ts:778 (`const quest = getVisitorQuest(state)`) never sees it, so auto-play's step 14 can never deliver the quest and always falls through to a trade. The feature only works in main-thread fallback mode.
confirmed.fix: Add `visitorQuest: WorldState['visitorQuest']` to `SimTickDelta`, emit `visitorQuest: deltaCloneOptional(world.visitorQuest, cloneMode)` in `extractSimTickDelta`, and restore `world.visitorQuest = deltaCloneOptional(delta.visitorQuest, cloneMode)` in `applySimTickDelta`.
confirmed.verification: WorldState.visitorQuest (gameTypes.ts:741) is written only inside the sim (visitorQuest.ts:34 and 47, driven by groupEvents.maybeStartVisitorQuest and dailyWorldEvents.tickVisitorQuest) and appears nowhere in SimTickDelta, extractSimTickDelta or applySimTickDelta (simDelta.ts:52-139, 258-338, 441-523) nor in SimPrepKeys, so the main-thread world never receives it; the worker is on by default in a browser (GameWorkerHost.isGameWorkerEnabled, lines 570-579, returns true unless VITE_USE_GAME_WORKER disables it). The display world therefore keeps visitorQuest undefined, so App.tsx:1544-1546 never renders the traveling-smith card and virtualPlayer.ts:795 never sees a quest to deliver (the cited line 778 is the talkToVisitorLeader branch; the getVisitorQuest call sits at 795) — the quest silently expires and only the 'smith moved on' news shows. Minimal fix: add visitorQuest to SimTickDelta with the deltaCloneOptional extract/apply entries exactly as suggested.

confirmed.title: Time-cyclic `winter_watch` predicate makes the first-spring guide regress and reappear every year instead of finishing
confirmed.evidence: L66: `isComplete: (w) => w.dayInYear >= 250,`  L79: `const idx = TUTORIAL_CAMPAIGN.findIndex((s) => !s.isComplete(world));`  L80: `return idx === -1 ? null : TUTORIAL_CAMPAIGN[idx];` — `dayInYear` is `getCalendarDay(tick)` (gameTick.ts:77), which wraps modulo `DAYS_PER_YEAR` (dayCycleClock.ts:23-26), so it returns to 0 at every year boundary.
confirmed.impact: The step list assumes predicates only ever go false→true, but `winter_watch` goes true→false every new year. In year 2 day 0 the later `year_two` step (`w.year >= 2`) stays complete while `winter_watch` becomes incomplete again, so `findIndex` returns index 5 and `currentCampaignStep` reports `winter_watch`: App.tsx:1645-1652 renders TutorialCampaignBanner as 'Guide 6/7 — Prepare for winter' for the first 250 days of every year from year 2 onward, and the condition `campaignStep === null` that App.tsx:417-419 documents ('the banner simply stops rendering') is never reached outside winter.
confirmed.fix: Make the predicate monotonic: `isComplete: (w) => w.year >= 2 || w.dayInYear >= 250,` (keeps tests/tutorialCampaign.test.ts:92-111 green and stops the regression).
confirmed.verification: winter_watch's predicate is `w.dayInYear >= 250` (tutorialCampaign.ts:66) and dayInYear is assigned from getCalendarDay in gameTick.ts:77, which wraps modulo DAYS_PER_YEAR (dayCycleClock.ts:23-26); so at the start of every year >= 2 the step goes true -> false while year_two stays complete, and currentCampaignStep's findIndex (line 79) returns index 5, rendering 'Guide 6/7 - Prepare for winter' for days 0-249 of every year and never reaching the null/finished state App.tsx:417-419 documents. tests/tutorialCampaign.test.ts only exercises year 2 with dayInYear = 260 (lines 102-111), so nothing locks the regression. Minimal fix: make the predicate monotonic, `isComplete: (w) => w.year >= 2 || w.dayInYear >= 250`, which keeps both existing assertions green.

confirmed.title: frame() re-arms requestAnimationFrame only as its last statement, so one throw from gameTick permanently freezes the main-thread game (no rollback, no fallback)
confirmed.evidence:
src/game/gameLoop.ts:865: `gameTick(this.world, focus);`
src/game/gameLoop.ts:900: `this.rafId = requestAnimationFrame(this.frame);`
confirmed.impact: In main-thread mode — the documented fallback authority — the tick, view update, draw and notify calls are unguarded, and the next frame is scheduled only after all of them succeed. Any throw (e.g. assertSpatialGridInvariants at gameTick.ts:214 raises when the grid-invariant check is enabled, or a domain-owner error) escapes the rAF callback before line 900, so ticks, rendering and UI notifications stop forever with no recovery path, while the partially advanced tick (state.tick already incremented, lastProcessedCalendarDay not yet written) is left un-rolled-back. The worker path has exactly this protection (gameWorker.ts:354-357 wraps gameTick and calls applySimPrep on failure) and GameLoop even falls back to the unprotected path on a worker fault.
confirmed.fix: Wrap the body of frame() (tick loop + updateView + draw + notify) in try/catch that logs the error, and move `this.rafId = requestAnimationFrame(this.frame)` into a `finally` block so the loop always continues.
confirmed.verification: GameLoop.frame (gameLoop.ts:807-901) has no try/catch: gameTick(this.world, focus) at 865, updateView/draw at 890-891 and notify at 897 are all unguarded and `this.rafId = requestAnimationFrame(this.frame)` is the last statement (900), so any throw aborts the callback and no further frame is scheduled; there is no window.onerror/unhandledrejection handler anywhere in src (only GameWorkerHost's worker 'error' listener), so main-thread mode has no recovery. The worker path does guard the same call — src/game/simWorker/gameWorker.ts:316-357 wraps gameTick and calls applySimPrep(world, prepBackup) on failure — and fallbackFromWorker (gameLoop.ts:385-404) deliberately routes faults into this unprotected path. Fix: wrap the frame body in try/catch that logs, and move the requestAnimationFrame call into a finally block. Severity medium is right: it is a robustness gap that needs a throw (e.g. assertSpatialGridInvariants at gameTick.ts:214 when SPATIAL_GRID_INVARIANT is set), not an always-on defect.

confirmed.title: Hunting-Spot output reads the research key `hunt_yield`, which no research node defines, so hunt research can never boost it
confirmed.evidence:
gameTypes.ts:923 `... description: 'Unlocks Barracks · settlers hunt farther (+20% range) and bring home more meat (+25% food)', ... effects: [{ target: 'hunt_range', multiplier: 1.2 }, { target: 'hunt_food', multiplier: 1.25 }], ...`
dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:432 `const huntMult = getMultiplier(state, 'hunt_yield');`
simHelpers.ts:67-90 `export function getMultiplier(state: WorldState, key: string): number {` ... `return multiplier + add;`
confirmed.impact: No research node in the game declares the target `hunt_yield` (whole-repo grep: only this call site), so `getMultiplier` finds no match and returns 1 for ever: the Hunting Spot production line is completely immune to `hunt_food` (defense_2 +25%, defense_4 +30%, defense_8 +15%). Settler hunts do receive the bonus (combat.getHuntFoodMultiplier -> humanNeeds.ts:107), so the node's promise is only half-delivered. If the intent is that building-based hunting should also scale with Stone/Iron Spears, the key is a typo for `hunt_food`; if not, the lookup is a permanent no-op.
confirmed.fix: Either change dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:432 to `getMultiplier(state, 'hunt_food')` (or call `getHuntFoodMultiplier(state)`), or remove the dead lookup and document that building hunting is intentionally unaffected by spear research.
confirmed.verification: A whole-repo grep for `hunt_yield` matches only dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:432; createInitialResearchNodes (gameTypes.ts:905-933) defines hunt_range and hunt_food only (defense_2/4/8), and getMultiplier (simHelpers.ts:67-90) starts at multiplier=1/add=0 and returns 1 when nothing matches, so `huntMult` is permanently 1. The Hunting Spot amount (dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:440-442) therefore ignores hunt_food, while free-roam hunts do use it through getHuntFoodMultiplier (combat.ts:109-111) at humanNeeds.ts:107. Minimal fix: `const huntMult = getHuntFoodMultiplier(state);` (or getMultiplier(state, 'hunt_food')) if building hunting should scale with spear research; otherwise delete the dead lookup. Low severity: the only effect is that Hunting Spot meat never receives the declared research bonus.

confirmed.title: removeWorkerTransition strips the settler out of residence occupants, breaking the residence↔occupants invariant
confirmed.impact: A housed settler released from a job is deleted from their home's occupants list while `residenceBuildingId` still points at that home, so SIMULATION_AUTHORITY §5 residence occupancy is false. `collectSimulationInvariantErrors` reports "human N residenceBuildingId H missing from that residence's occupants" (simulationInvariants.ts:191-194) and the dev pulse in gameTick.ts:282 logs it. Reachable from (a) the player command `removeWorkerFromBuilding` (buildingStaffingActions.ts:290), (b) the assignment layer's builder soft-steal `clearJobAssignment` (L385-387) called from assignBuilderInPlace L449, and (c) `clearAutoFilledChurches` on save load (saveLoad.ts:531), which runs after the load-time residence sync at saveLoad.ts:486 so the mismatch survives into the session. Until the next LAYER_ASSIGN_INTERVAL pulse (≤18 ticks) `collectHousingDiagnostics` (housingDiagnostics.ts:37,56) and `getResidenceCapacity(b) - b.occupants.length` bed checks (storyEvents.ts:50,319) read a phantom open bed, and it also writes `residence building.occupants`, a field decisionRegistry.ts:84 declares housing-owned.

confirmed.verification: removeWorkerTransition (workforce.ts:219-229) filters the human id out of every building's occupants, and residence lists use the same field (syncResidenceOccupants, residencyReconciliation.ts:112-120, filters to residenceBuildingId), while only homeBuildingId is cleared at 226 — so a housed settler removed from a job is deleted from their house's occupants while residenceBuildingId still points at it, which collectSimulationInvariantErrors reports as "human N residenceBuildingId H missing from that residence's occupants" (simulationInvariants.ts:189-194). Real callers pass the full list: buildingStaffingActions.ts:290, clearJobAssignment (workforce.ts:385-387) from assignBuilderInPlace:449, and saveLoad.ts:328 (clearAutoFilledChurches, called at saveLoad.ts:531 *after* the load-time residence sync at 486). The existing test tests/workforce.transitions.test.ts:288-303 asserts invariants stay clean after removal but only passes `[farmB]`, so it does not lock the all-buildings behaviour in. Downgraded from high to medium because residence occupant lists are a UI mirror, housing decisions read residenceBuildingId (countResidentsInBuilding, residencyOccupancy.ts:83), and the mismatch is repaired by the next LAYER_ASSIGN_INTERVAL pulse (tickLayerAssign.ts:35, ≤18 ticks) — but storyEvents.countFreeShelterBeds (storyEvents.ts:47-51) can read a phantom bed if the strip happens later in the same daily tick. confirmed.title: An imprisoned settler is never removed from a construction crew and keeps working the site
confirmed.impact: A settler jailed while on a construction crew (crew members have homeBuildingId == null, so the arrest's homeBuildingId branch is skipped entirely) stays in the unfinished site's `occupants`: dailyBuildingEconomy.tickBuildingProgress keeps counting them as a worker (L145) and grants them builder skill daily (L159-163) in prison, and after release `isOnConstructionCrew` keeps them out of ordinary job assignment until that site completes.

confirmed.verification: prepareWorkforce's prisoner branch (workforce.ts:483-490) only clears homeBuildingId/occupation/job and never touches building occupants, and syncJobBuildingOccupants (294-323) rebuilds only completed workplaces plus the Prison (297), so an incomplete site keeps the prisoner in its crew. arrestForScandal (simulation/humanRelationships.ts:1187-1212) clears homeBuildingId and residenceBuildingId but not crew membership, and crew members have homeBuildingId == null (addToConstructionCrew:238), so the arrest's homeBuildingId branch is skipped; nothing else removes an imprisoned human from incomplete sites (grep isImprisoned shows only add-side filters). tickBuildingProgress therefore still counts them (dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:145) and grants Builder skill (159-163), and isOnConstructionCrew keeps them out of normal job assignment after release (workforce.ts:52-60, buildingStaffingActions.ts:23-31). confirmed.title: connectionsAt's fallback for fewer than two connections can never fire
confirmed.evidence: lines 166-174: `north: north || (!south && !north), south, east: east || (!west && !east), west,` … `if (countConnections(conn) < 2) { return { north: true, east: true, south: false, west: false }; }`.
confirmed.impact: `north || (!south && !north)` is true whenever `south` is false, so N+S >= 1; identically E+W >= 1, so `countConnections(conn) >= 2` always. The fallback return is unreachable, which means the comment's stated purpose ('a lone crossing reads as zero connections and skips corners') is not achieved by this branch — a lone crossing is instead forced to `{north:true, east:true}` by the line-167/169 coercions, i.e. it is classified as a `straight`/`elbow` rather than through any fallback. Any future reader relying on the guard will not get the documented behavior.
confirmed.fix: Delete the unreachable `if (countConnections(conn) < 2)` block and state the actual coercion contract in the comment, or replace the coercions with the intended explicit check (`if (!north && !south && !east && !west) return { north: true, east: true, south: false, west: false };`).
confirmed.verification: In connectionsAt (stripJunction.ts:144-179) the coercions `north: north || (!south && !north)` and `east: east || (!west && !east)` reduce to `north || !south` and `east || !west`, so at least one of N/S and one of E/W is always true and countConnections (40-42) is always ≥2; the guard at 172-174 is unreachable dead code. The auditor's impact statement is partly wrong: the documented lone-crossing result ({north:true,east:true}) is exactly what the coercions already produce, so behaviour matches the comment — the defect is dead code/readability only. Fix: delete the unreachable block (or replace the coercions with the explicit all-false check) and state the real contract in the comment.

confirmed.title: getPathGrid cache key omits the map preset, although tiles (and therefore blocked cells) depend on it
confirmed.evidence: 269: `const steps = Math.max(4, Math.min(128, Math.ceil(span / (TERRAIN_TILE_SIZE * 0.5))));` (comment 268: "Sub-tile sampling steps prevent tunneling through 1-tile diagonal obstacles")
confirmed.impact: `TERRAIN_TILE_SIZE` is 10 (gameTypes.ts:992) and the intended step is 5px, but the 128 cap makes the real spacing span/128: 11.7px for a full medium-map line (1200x900 -> span ~1500px) and ~25px on a huge map (2560x1920 -> span ~3200px), i.e. larger than the tile itself. A 1-tile river or mountain strip can fall between two samples, so `lineCrossesBlocked` returns false, `steerWithPath` returns 'direct' (316/349) and the human walks straight through water/mountain — the exact failure the module was written to prevent. Humans have no terrain collision (only wildlife has the deep-water guard, tickLayerSystems.ts:609-628), so nothing downstream corrects it.
confirmed.fix: Raise the cap so the step can never exceed half a tile (and the tile width for every supported map size), e.g. `const steps = Math.max(4, Math.min(1024, Math.ceil(span / (TERRAIN_TILE_SIZE * 0.5))));`.
confirmed.verification: getPathGrid keys its module-global cache on `${seed}|${bldSig}|${width}x${height}` (pathfinding.ts:65) while blocked cells are derived from map.tiles (72-77), which terrainGen.ts generates per preset (PRESET_MODIFIERS, waterLevel/mountainThreshold/river carving at 389-434); other map caches do include the preset (terrainLayer.ts:336,367, pixiTerrain.ts:166, terrain.ts:132). restoreWorldMapFromSave regenerates a compact save from seed+preset (saveLoad.ts:163-173) and WorldMap.preset exists (gameTypes.ts:987), so a stale grid would be reused and pathCache would not even clear (setCurrentPathMap compares object identity, pathfinding.ts:286-292). Downgraded to low because no production path reaches the collision: initGame's seed is random unless explicitly passed (worldGen.ts:568) and no in-repo caller passes one (App.tsx:120, App.tsx:892), so two same-seed/different-preset maps cannot arise in normal play. Fix: include `map.preset` in the cache key.

confirmed.title: clearHuntersTargetingPrey early-returns on a tick-start index, so hunters that acquired the prey mid-tick keep a dangling target
confirmed.verification: clearHuntersTargetingPrey (simulationEntities.ts:158-180) returns as soon as the tick-start index contains the prey (163-172), so the aliveness-scanning loop at 175-179 never runs for the ordinary case where another wolf/hunter already had that prey indexed (index built once per tick at gameTick.ts:184 from buildHuntTargetByPreyIndex, 125-156). Hunters that acquire the prey later in the same tick (humanHuntingBehavior.ts:171, tickLayerSystems.ts:381) keep a huntTargetId that points at a just-removed entity until their own next human tick clears it (humanTick.ts:310-313). Minimal fix: after clearing the indexed hunters, also run the entityById scan (or, cheaper, delete the prey entry only after clearing and keep the scan unconditional). Low severity: every reader guards on aliveness (humanStatus.ts:153-154, renderer/humans.ts:325-326, humanTick.ts:310-312) and chases are re-decided by a fresh spatial query each tick.

confirmed.title: `canPursueSecretAffair` is called without the colony work schedule, so the realtime affair gate uses the legacy 07:00-16:00 window
confirmed.evidence: humanTick.ts:220-222 `const nurturingSettlerCount = allHumans.filter((h) => h.alive && !h.isJuvenile && h.traits?.includes('nurturing')).length;` — `allHumans` is built from `byType[EntityType.Human]` plus newborn entities (humanTick.ts:198-208) with no `isPlayerHuman` filter, while every other social list in the file filters it (`playerHumans` at :116, `isPlayerHuman` at :212, :330, :409). The value is fed to `getSchoolAgeMultiplier(entity, updatedBuildings, nurturingSettlerCount)` (humanTick.ts:298), whose contract is education.ts:78-79 `// Nurturing settlers in the village help every child mature a bit faster. const nurtureBoost = Math.min(0.2, nurturingCount * 0.04);`.
confirmed.impact: Up to three visiting/rival 'nurturing' settlers (entityFactory.ts:74 rolls traits for every human, including visitors, rivals and caravan carriers) contribute up to +0.12 to every colony child's maturation multiplier while they stand in the valley, silently shortening childhood based on who happens to be visiting.
confirmed.fix: Filter to colony settlers: `allHumans.filter((h) => h.alive && isPlayerHuman(h) && !h.isJuvenile && h.traits?.includes('nurturing'))`.
confirmed.verification: All three call sites (humanTick.ts:948, 1036, 1209, inside tickHumans 161-1503) omit the 7th argument, so canPursueSecretAffair uses its default `getWorkSchedule({ workSchedule: undefined })` = DEFAULT_WORK_SCHEDULE {7,16} (humanRelationships.ts:1314-1321, workSchedule.ts:4-5,21-24) even though `workSchedule` is already computed in the same function at humanTick.ts:186. isWorkScheduleHour (workSchedule.ts:132-134) then judges work hours from the legacy window, so hours 07:00-08:00 count as work and e.g. 15:00 is treated as work for a 09:00-15:00 colony, diverging from the daily owner, which deliberately passes getWorkSchedule(state) (humanRelationships.ts:1361). Fix: pass `workSchedule` as the 7th argument at 948, 1036 and 1209. Low severity: the divergence only shifts tryst feasibility/feedback in the staggered path, not affair establishment (daily owner).

confirmed.title: Grief window compared against 0 instead of the current tick, making 'grieving' permanent
confirmed.evidence: 37: `if ((entity.griefUntilTick ?? 0) > 0 && entity.energy < entity.maxEnergy * 0.7) return true;`
confirmed.impact: `griefUntilTick` is an absolute sim tick (set to `tick + TICKS_PER_DAY * 7` in humanLifecycleCleanup.ts:73 and `+3` for a lover at line 90) and is never reset to 0, so `> 0` stays true for the rest of the settler's life once they have grieved. Every ex-griever below 70% energy is permanently classified as needing medical care: they stay in tickHospitalDailyCare's patient list (line 183, so ward rounds treat them) and satisfy `shouldAttemptHospitalTreatment` (humanHospitalBehavior.ts:40) while on shift with energy 42-50%. All other grief checks in the codebase compare with the current tick (socialLife.ts:95, townHall.ts:176/248, citizenOverview.ts:129, storyEvents.ts:550/573).
confirmed.fix: Take the current tick (add a `tick` parameter or pass `state.tick` from the callers) and test `(entity.griefUntilTick ?? 0) > tick`.
confirmed.verification: needsMedicalCare (hospitalCare.ts:33-39) tests `(entity.griefUntilTick ?? 0) > 0`, but griefUntilTick is only ever written as an absolute future tick (humanLifecycleCleanup.ts:73,90; humanLifecycle.ts:119-120) and never cleared, so the clause is true for the rest of that settler's life; every other consumer compares it to the clock (socialLife.ts:95, townHall.ts:176/248, storyEvents.ts:550/573, citizenOverview.ts:129). The extra patients therefore enter tickHospitalDailyCare's list (hospitalCare.ts:182-184) and can consume the daily treatment cap and reputation award (186-200), and shouldAttemptHospitalTreatment keeps routing them (humanHospitalBehavior.ts:40) — note the patient sort by medicalUrgency means genuinely urgent cases are still treated first, so the auditor's "starving genuinely sick settlers" is only partly true. Fix: thread the current tick into needsMedicalCare and compare `(entity.griefUntilTick ?? 0) > tick`. The auditor's cited consumer file `humanCare.ts` does not exist; the real consumer is hospitalCare.ts:183.

confirmed.title: Medicine food cost bypasses the economy ledger
confirmed.evidence: 156: `if (personDayRoll(doctor.id, state.tick, 901 + best.id) > 0.35) return false;` then 92-95 `const heal = Math.min(..., (8 + strength * 14) * ...)`; 99 `if (state.resources.food >= 1 && Math.random() < 0.25) {`; 107 `gainSkill(state, id, JobType.Doctor, 0.08);`
confirmed.impact: `personDayRoll` is constant for a whole colony day, and doctorTreatNearby runs from the per-tick human tick (humanTick.ts:1079 -> humanHospitalBehavior.ts:57). On an eligible day the doctor therefore re-applies the whole treatment every tick: ~11+ energy per tick per patient, 0.08 Doctor skill per occupant per tick (skill 100 within a couple of in-game hours), a 25%/tick chance of spending 1 food (tens of food per shift), and repeated '❤ Treated' feedback. hospitalCare imports no PER_TICK_RATE_SCALE at all, while comparable per-tick effects are scaled (hotelStay.ts:248 `0.8 * PER_TICK_RATE_SCALE`). The same per-day-roll-per-tick shape governs patient self-treatment (humanHospitalBehavior.ts:94), so this is a module-level cadence choice, not a single-statement slip.
confirmed.fix: Give the treatment an explicit cadence: e.g. `if (!isStartOfClockHour(state.tick)) return false;` in doctorTreatNearby/patient care, or scale heal, skill gain and the 25% food roll by PER_TICK_RATE_SCALE so one passing day yields a bounded amount of care.
confirmed.verification: The code is exactly as cited: treatPatientAtHospital deducts `state.resources.food -= 1` (hospitalCare.ts:100) without recordFoodConsumed, and citizenOverview.foodNetToday = produced − consumed (citizenOverview.ts:169) therefore overstates net food. However the ledger is a meals ledger by design — ECONOMY_SOURCE_LABELS has no consumption source other than 'meals' (economyLedger.ts:11-17) and only the meal path calls recordFoodConsumed (humanNeeds.ts:65) — while ~11 other food expenditures bypass it too (groupEvents treaties/gifts/refugees, weddingDiplomacy feasts, townHall festival, frontierCombat raids, settlerInteractionActions recruitment, travelingTheatre hospitality, animalCare, storyEvents, deerParliament, tradeCaravans). So this is at most a ledger-completeness nit capped at 1 food per treatment (25% chance), not a defect unique to hospitalCare; adding a 'medicine' source would be a small feature. Fix if desired: `recordFoodConsumed(state, 'medicine', 1)`.

confirmed.title: Kid-play chat roll uses Math.random() while the sibling bubble roll in the same function uses the run-seeded RNG
confirmed.impact: The decision to emit a child bubble - and therefore the resulting chatPhrase/chatTicks written into authoritative entity state (transported in simDelta field list, simBuffers/simDelta.ts:175) - is decided by the unseeded global RNG, so a replayed or re-run identical seed produces different dialogue state. The seeded helper is used for the equivalent roll eleven lines below and in humanChat, so the seeded stream is the intended owner; tests/deterministicSeed.test.ts snapshots tick/resources/entities without chat fields, so this divergence is not covered.
confirmed.fix: Replace `Math.random()` with `seededRandomForRun(`chat-bubble-kid:${entity.id}:${state.tick}`)`, matching the seeded pattern used at line 100 and in humanChat.ts.
confirmed.verification: tickHumanChildLeisure rolls the child bubble gate with the unseeded `Math.random()` (humanLeisureBehavior.ts:36) which decides whether sayHumanChatPhrase writes chatPhrase/chatTicks — authoritative entity fields carried in SimTickDelta (simBuffers/simDelta.ts:175, CATALOG_PATCH_KEYS) — whereas the equivalent adult roll eleven lines later uses seededRandomForRun(`chat-bubble:...`) (line 100, imported at 71), as do all other chat rolls (humanChat.ts:387/438/461/523, humanVenueBehavior.ts:57, humanTick.ts:874/876). A same-seed replay can therefore diverge in dialogue state, and tests/deterministicSeed.test.ts snapshots only tick/resources/id/type/rounded x,y,energy/job (lines 6-21), so it does not cover this. Fix: use `seededRandomForRun(`chat-bubble-kid:${entity.id}:${state.tick}`)`. Low severity: presentation-state drift only, and unseeded Math.random is used elsewhere in the sim (combat, hunting, festivals), so this is not a unique determinism guarantee.

confirmed.title: Town Hall tax base is built from state.entities, which still contains settlers who died earlier this tick
confirmed.evidence: L767 `const villagers = state.entities.filter(isPlayerHuman);` L768 `tickTownHallCivic(state, building, villagers);` L769 `tickTownHallAudiences(state, building, villagers);` — `isPlayerHuman` (playerHuman.ts:12-17) does not test `alive`, and gameTick only prunes `state.entities` at the very end of the tick (gameTick.ts:234 `state.entities = allAlive;`), after the daily layer at gameTick.ts:220-222. The same function already has an alive-filtered list in scope: L292 `const playerWorkers = allAlive.filter(isPlayerHuman);`.
confirmed.impact: A settler killed earlier in the same tick (predator, illness, old age) is still a Human with `alive === false` in `state.entities` during the daily layer, so `tickTownHallCivic` counts them in `const adults = playerHumans.filter((h) => !h.isJuvenile).length;` (townHall.ts:88) and pays `adults * 0.4` extra tax gold for that pulse; the dead entity is also handed to `tickTownHallAudiences`. tickTownHallAudiences happens to re-filter `h.alive` (townHall.ts:352), so the visible damage is limited to the tax count, but the module mixes two different population sources in one function.
confirmed.fix: Pass the already-built alive-filtered list: `const villagers = playerWorkers;` (or `ctx.playerHumans`) at L767 instead of re-filtering `state.entities`.
confirmed.verification: tickBuildingProduction (dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:275-282) feeds tickTownHallCivic `state.entities.filter(isPlayerHuman)` (line 767); isPlayerHuman never checks `alive` (playerHuman.ts:12-17) and gameTick only replaces state.entities at the very end (gameTick.ts:234), so humans killed in the earlier realtime layer (tryDailyHumanMortality via humanTick.ts:315, killHuman sets alive=false only) are still in that list. tickTownHallCivic then counts all non-juveniles for taxes (townHall.ts:88-89) while its sibling consumer re-filters `h.alive` itself (townHall.ts:352), confirming the alive filter belongs at the call site. Impact is small because `Math.floor` usually absorbs the extra 0.4 gold per corpse, hence low; fix: `const villagers = allAlive.filter(isPlayerHuman);` (allAlive is already the alive list passed into tickBuildingProduction) or filter `e.alive`.

confirmed.title: Redundant pressureRatio branch: ratio ≥ 2.0 is already covered by the ≥ 1.6 branch above it
confirmed.evidence: ecologyStage.ts:133 `if (grazing.pressureRatio >= 1.6) grazingStress = Math.max(grazingStress, 2);` / line 134 `if (grazing.pressureRatio >= 2.0) grazingStress = 2;`
confirmed.impact: Line 133 already assigns 2 for every ratio >= 1.6, so line 134 is a no-op for all inputs. If the second threshold was meant to be a distinct tier (e.g. requiring ratio >= 2.0 for the two-bad-driver stage-3 boost at line 222), that behaviour is not implemented anywhere and the grazing driver under-reports at extreme ratios.
confirmed.fix: Delete line 134, or make the >= 2.0 tier drive something real (e.g. count it toward `badCount` / the stage-3 condition) instead of re-assigning the same value.
confirmed.verification: In computeRawEcologyStress the line `if (grazing.pressureRatio >= 1.6) grazingStress = Math.max(grazingStress, 2)` (ecologyStage.ts:133) already forces 2 for any ratio ≥ 2.0, so line 134 can never change grazingStress — it is dead code that suggests a second tier that does not exist. The secondary claim is wrong: a report reading 'critical' is already mapped to stress 2 by line 131 (`if (grazing.level === 'critical') grazingStress = 2`), so the driver does honour ecosystemPressure.ts:81's 1.35 threshold and does not disagree with the headline. Fix: delete line 134 (or give the 2.0 tier a real, distinct effect). Low severity: no behavioural change today.

confirmed.title: InitGameOptions.width/height size the world state but never reach generateWorldMap
confirmed.evidence:
581:    entityByType: emptyEntityByType(),
826:  rebuildEntityByIdMap(state);   // no buildEntityByType / entityByType fill anywhere in initGame
confirmed.impact: indexLivingEntity only maintains entityById (entityIndex.ts:42-45), so after initGame every bucket is a defined empty array. Probe on initGame({size:'medium',seed:1}): 694 living entities / entityById.size 694 / entityByType grass=0 rabbit=0 deer=0 wolf=0 fox=0 human=0 tree=0. Because an empty array is not nullish, the documented fallbacks are bypassed: entityCatalog.resolveAliveByType (158-159 `world.entityByType?.[type] ?? world.entities.filter(...)`) returns [] instead of scanning, renderSnapshot.ts:91-93 `?? buildEntityByType(entities)` likewise, and assertSimInvariants check #5 ('entityByType reflects the alive population', simInvariants.ts:66-74) is false for a fresh world. It self-heals on the first gameTick, so the window is a pre-tick world such as the paused quick-start overlay (App.tsx:902) plus any tooling/test that inspects a freshly initialized world; saveLoad deliberately strips entityByType to undefined (saveLoad.ts:176-190), so initGame is the only producer of a defined-but-empty index.
confirmed.fix: At the end of initGame, next to rebuildEntityByIdMap(state) (line 826), add `state.entityByType = buildEntityByType(state.entities);` (import buildEntityByType from './simFocus').
confirmed.verification: initGame resolves width/height for state (worldGen.ts:573-574, stored at 592-593) but generates the map through the MapSize overload `generateWorldMap(size, preset ?? 'verdant', mapSeed)` (687), whose tile grid is derived solely from MAP_SIZE_DIMENSIONS[size] (terrainGen.ts:361-367), so a caller supplying width/height would get state dimensions that disagree with map.width/height; terrainGen.ts:374-381 already shows the same width/height-vs-size mismatch being handled for the pixel overload. Latent only: InitGameOptions.width/height exist (worldGen.ts:236-243) but no in-repo caller passes them (only App.tsx:120 and App.tsx:892, neither with width/height), so the divergence is unreachable today — hence low. Fix: forward the resolved dimensions (use the pixel overload) or drop width/height from InitGameOptions.

confirmed.title: Seasonal festival is cancelled for the whole season when a random festival is still active on its single check day
confirmed.impact: The comment at lines 46-48 promises '5 days at the start of each season: 20 guaranteed festival days per year', but the seasonal festival has exactly one eligible tick per season and the `!state.festival` condition blocks it whenever a random festival is active. Random festivals last 20-39 days (line 75) and can be running on days 3 (a day-350 start carrying over), 183 (a day-150 start) and 273 (a day-250 start), and there is no retry, so that season's seasonal festival is silently lost - the 'guaranteed' 20 days can be 0, 5 or 10.
confirmed.fix: Record a pending seasonal festival (or a per-season flag) and start it on the first free day, e.g. `if (!state.festival && dayInYear >= seasonalStart + 3 && dayInYear < seasonalStart + 8 && !state.seasonalFestivalDone?.includes(seasonalStart))` setting the flag when it starts.
confirmed.verification: tickFestivals gates the seasonal festival on exactly one tick-of-year, `!state.festival && dayInYear === seasonalStart + 3` (dailyWorldEvents.ts:49-51), with no retry later in the season, so any still-running random festival suppresses it even though the comment at 46-48 promises 20 guaranteed festival days/year. Random festivals are rolled every FESTIVAL_CHECK_TICKS = 50 days (69-71; dayCycle.ts:308) and last 20-39 days (line 75), so a festival started on day 150 with ≥33 days left covers day 183 and one started on day 250 with ≥23 days covers day 273 — plausible, not certain, hence low. Fix: widen the window (e.g. `dayInYear >= seasonalStart + 3 && dayInYear <= seasonalStart + 8`) while keeping the `!state.festival` guard so it still fires at most once per season.

confirmed.lines: 129-134 (add lookup 131-132); researchedEffect 30-52 | 129-133 (accumulation at 44-47; effect data at gameTypes.ts:925,929)
confirmed.title: getCounterAttackChance sums tiered adds, making every predator counter-attack a guaranteed kill (1.0 chance)
confirmed.impact: Whenever Iron Spears has been forged (or Iron Swords researched), both nodes are researched, so researchedEffect(...,'add') returns 0.45 + 0.55 = 1.0 and this function returns 1.0. rollCounterAttack (combat.ts:157-159) computes roll = (hash % 1000)/1000 in [0, 0.999] and returns roll < chance, so it is always true: in tickLayerSystems.ts:394-403 every predator contact (Wolf, Fox, and the cursed Moon Howler) kills the predator instead of the settler, making predator deaths of settlers impossible late game. The explicit 0.55 / 0.45 fallback on line 133 is unreachable. getPredatorBlockChance (117-122) accumulates the same way (0.35 + 0.6 + 0.72 = 1.67); its Math.min(0.85, chance) cap masks the sum and makes the tier Math.max chance,0.72/0.6/0.35 branches dead, so the applied block rate is the cap rather than the researched tier.
confirmed.fix: Treat these as tier effects, not additive stacks: resolve the highest researched tier (e.g. if (hasIronSwords(state)) return 0.55; if (hasIronSpears(state)) return 0.45;) and keep any researched-effect override capped, e.g. return Math.min(0.85, add). Re-check getPredatorBlockChance after the same change.
confirmed.verification: researchedEffect accumulates every matching researched node with `value += effect.add` (combat.ts:47), so once defense_4 ({counter_attack, add:0.45}, gameTypes.ts:925) and defense_8 ({add:0.55}, 929) are both researched — defense_8 requires defense_4 and defense_6 — getCounterAttackChance returns 1.0 exactly (129-134, the `hasIronSwords ? 0.55 : 0.45` fallback and the declared 45%/55% tiers become unreachable). rollCounterAttack computes roll in [0, 0.999] and returns `roll < chance` (148-160), so every wolf/fox/werewolf that reaches a settler with a forged weapon dies, including the Moon Howler (tickLayerSystems.ts:391-426), contradicting the project's own tier law 'Weapon/armor tiers replace lower ones — do not stack' (frontierCombat.ts:248). Fix: `if (add !== undefined) return Math.min(hasIronSwords(state) ? 0.55 : 0.45, add);`. High: guaranteed predator kills are a clearly wrong, player-visible combat outcome, but no state corruption.

confirmed.title: Rare replacement roll repeats on all three ticks of hour 20, so a 15%-per-moon event becomes ~39%
confirmed.evidence:
moonHowler.ts:161  `    && hourOfDay === NIGHT_START`
moonHowler.ts:163  `    && rng() < MOON_HOWLER_REPLACEMENT_CHANCE`
moonHowler.ts:1016  `  if (shouldApplyNewMoonHowlerCurse(colonyDay, hourOfDay, humanPop, activeMoonCurses, rng)) {`  (called from tickLayerRealtime.ts:97 on EVERY tick)
confirmed.impact: TICKS_PER_HOUR = 3, so hourOfDay is 20 for tickOfDay 60, 61 and 62 — three consecutive ticks. Nothing latches the roll: the only guard is `activeCursed === 0`, which a failed roll does not change, and tickMoonHowlerCycle runs once per tick via tickLayerRealtime. A quiet full moon therefore gets three independent 15% rolls: P = 1 - 0.85^3 = 38.6% per full moon, i.e. ~10 replacement Howlers per 360-day year instead of the ~3.9/year implied by the constant (and the ~1-2/year the comment at lines 78-84 claims). SIMULATION_AUTHORITY §5 says a replacement appears 'only through a rare replacement roll'; the one-Howler invariant still holds, but the declared rare-event pacing is ~2.6x off. The existing tests call the pure predicate once per case (tests/moonHowler.rare.test.ts:129-219) so the per-tick repetition is not locked in.

confirmed.verification: shouldApplyNewMoonHowlerCurse (moonHowler.ts:151-165) is evaluated from tickMoonHowlerCycle line 1016, which runs on every tick via tickLayerRealtime.ts:97-105 with no latch and with a fresh rng() draw; since TICKS_PER_HOUR is 3 (hour 20 spans tickOfDay 60-62) and NIGHT_START is 20 (dayCycleConstants.ts:15), a quiet full moon gets three independent 15% rolls, i.e. 1 − 0.85³ ≈ 38.6% instead of 15% (with DAYS_PER_MOON_CYCLE = 14, ~10 replacements/year vs the ~1-2/year claimed at lines 78-84). tests/moonHowler.rare.test.ts:129-156 calls the pure predicate once per case, so the per-tick repetition is not locked in. Fix: gate the roll to one tick per moon, e.g. `isStartOfClockHour(state.tick) && shouldApplyNewMoonHowlerCurse(...)`, or latch it on a per-colony-day field. Downgraded from high to medium: the one-Howler invariant and the 'no guaranteed Howler' rule still hold — only the declared rare-event pacing is ~2.6× off.

confirmed.title: Leader household includes adult children, so married children are dragged into the manor and other residents are evicted every day

if (prev?.alive && prev.occupation === LEADER_OCCUPATION) {
      prev.occupation = 'settler';

confirmed.title: visitorQuest is written by ticks but omitted from the save allow-list, the worker delta and worker prep, so the smith quest is lost on load and never reaches the display world
confirmed.evidence: 34: `state.visitorQuest = {` ... 38: `expiresDay: getAbsoluteCalendarDay(state.tick) + QUEST_EXPIRE_DAYS,` — 'visitorQuest' is absent from WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS (saveSchema.ts:4-26) and from SimTickDelta's field list/extract/apply (simDelta.ts:80-139, 280-338, 420-500), while its sibling story state ('storyFlags', 'pendingStoryEvents', 'tradeRoutes') is in all three.

Fix: add 'visitorQuest' to WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS, to the SimTickDelta interface + extract/apply, and to simPrep's restore list. confirmed.title: `huntVisuals` is written only in the worker and never shipped, so hunt lines stop rendering
confirmed.evidence: L78-79: `floatingTexts: WorldState['floatingTexts'];` / `deathParticles: WorldState['deathParticles'];` — the neighbouring per-tick presentation arrays are carried, but `WorldState.huntVisuals` (gameTypes.ts:750) is absent from `SimTickDelta` and from both extract/apply.

The renderer reads it from the display world via renderSnapshot.ts:112 into renderer/humans.ts:353, and the render sidecar/SoA does not carry it, so with the worker active the display copy's `huntVisuals` is undefined and no arrow/lunge is drawn. confirmed.title: `resolveCombatLogKind` has no event-type guard, so non-combat 'event' entries that mention a raid are reported as raids/defenses
confirmed.evidence: L50: `const msg = evt.message.toLowerCase();`  L53: `if (msg.includes('raid')) {`  L60: `return 'incoming_raid';` — the function never checks `evt.type`, and its caller passes the whole log: villagePortrait.ts:83-90 `const eventLog = state.eventLog ?? []; ... const kind = resolveCombatLogKind(eventLog[i]); if (kind === 'outgoing_raid') outgoingRaids++; else if (kind === 'defense' || kind === 'repelled' || kind === 'incoming_raid') defenses++;`
confirmed.impact: `groupEvents.ts:818` (also 1110, 1125) logs `logEvent(state, 'event', 'Raid called off — truce with ' + rival.name, rival.name)` with no `combatKind`; the heuristic matches `'raid'`, fails the 'raid on the village'/' raid on ' tests and returns `'incoming_raid'`. Every peace treaty therefore increments `defenses` in villagePortrait, which both misreports the village's history and can silently delete the `+10` war-score bonus (`villagePortrait.ts:97 (defenses > 0 && outgoingRaids >= defenses ? 10 : 0)`), moving the portrait's war label across its 25/50 thresholds.
confirmed.fix: Add a type guard as the first line after the kind fast-path: `if (evt.type !== 'combat') return null;` (combat writers always pass a kind, so this only removes false positives).
confirmed.verification: resolveCombatLogKind (eventLog.ts:48-63) is the legacy fallback for saves without combatKind but never checks `evt.type`; villagePortrait.ts:83-92 runs it over the whole eventLog, and groupEvents.ts:818 (also 1110, 1125) writes `logEvent(state, 'event', 'Raid called off — truce with ' + rival.name)` without a combatKind, which matches only the generic `msg.includes('raid')` branch and returns 'incoming_raid' (it fails the 'raid on the village'/' raid on ' tests). Each peace treaty therefore increments `defenses`, which can remove the +10 war-score bonus (villagePortrait.ts:94-98) and shift the portrait's war label across its thresholds. Fix: add `if (evt.type !== 'combat') return null;` after the combatKind fast-path. Medium: a real misreport with limited (portrait/label) impact.

confirmed.title: buildings.upgraded subtracts last year's per-year upgrade count from a cumulative total
confirmed.evidence:
stats.ts:83-86 `const currentUpgrades = state.buildings.reduce(` / `(sum, b) => sum + (b.level > 1 ? b.level - 1 : 0),` / `0,` / `);`
stats.ts:87 `const prevUpgrades = prevYearStats?.buildings.upgraded ?? 0;`
stats.ts:88 `const upgradesThisYear = Math.max(0, currentUpgrades - prevUpgrades);`
stats.ts:114 `upgraded: upgradesThisYear,`
stats.ts:138 `s.totalBuildingsUpgraded += latestYear.buildings.upgraded;`
confirmed.impact: `currentUpgrades` is a cumulative total of all upgrade levels in the village, while the field it is compared against (`buildings.upgraded`) is written as that year's *increase* (line 114) and read again as a level. Example: 2 upgrades in year 0 (cumulative 2, recorded 2); no upgrades in year 1 -> 2-2 = 0 (correct); no upgrades in year 2 -> 2-0 = 2 reported (phantom). `updateLifetimeStats` accumulates these into `lifetimeStats.totalBuildingsUpgraded`, which drifts and over-counts. Contrast `marriages`, which correctly uses the previous snapshot `prevYearStats.marriedCount`.
confirmed.fix: Give YearlyStats a cumulative baseline (`upgradedTotal: currentUpgrades`) and use `const prevUpgrades = prevYearStats?.upgradedTotal ?? 0;`, keeping `upgraded` as the per-year delta; or drop the subtraction and increment `lifetimeStats.totalBuildingsUpgraded` at the upgrade owner.
confirmed.verification: recordYearlyStats (stats.ts) sums `b.level - 1` over all buildings (lines 83-86), i.e. a cumulative upgrade count, but line 87 subtracts `prevYearStats.buildings.upgraded`, which stores the previous year's *delta* (line 114). Year 0 stores C0 and year 1 is therefore still correct, but every year ≥2 computes `C_n − delta_{n-1}` and `updateLifetimeStats` (line 138) adds that inflated value to `lifetimeStats.totalBuildingsUpgraded`. Minimal fix: persist the cumulative total (e.g. `buildings.upgradedTotal`) and subtract that; impact stays low because grep shows no renderer or other consumer of `totalBuildingsUpgraded`.

confirmed.title: The pickSharedResidenceForFamily fallback in assignFamilyToResidence is unreachable
confirmed.evidence: residencyReconciliation.ts:130-131 `const picked = pickResidenceForFamily(family, alive, residences, occupancy)\n    ?? pickSharedResidenceForFamily(family, alive, residences, occupancy);` — residencySelection.ts:631-633 and 582-584 show both functions skip leader houses and require the identical `familyFitsInResidence(family, residence, humans, occupancy)` predicate before a residence can become `best`.
confirmed.impact: For any non-empty family, whenever `pickResidenceForFamily` yields `undefined` the second call iterates the same residences with the same fit test and unchanged occupancy and also yields `undefined`, so the right-hand side can never contribute a placement; the `??` branch is dead and hides the fact that a family that fits nowhere is handled entirely by the split path below (adults individually, children by custodian). (Only a zero-length family — never produced by buildHousingUnits or syncPartnerResidence — could make the two disagree, via pickResidenceForFamily's `family.length === 0` early return.)
confirmed.fix: Delete the `?? pickSharedResidenceForFamily(family, alive, residences, occupancy)` fallback (and the now-unused import/private helper if nothing else uses it), or change one of the two scorers so the fallback expresses a real policy difference.
confirmed.verification: pickResidenceForFamily (residencySelection.ts:600-680) skips only leader houses, requires the same `familyFitsInResidence` predicate and always sets `best` when any residence passes, so for a non-empty family it returns undefined exactly when no residence fits — the same condition that makes pickSharedResidenceForFamily (residencySelection.ts:573-598) return undefined. buildHousingUnits (residencySelection.ts:248-291) always starts a unit with `collectOwnHousehold`, which unconditionally adds the living seed, so units are never empty and the `??` branch at residencyReconciliation.ts:130-131 can never contribute. Minimal fix: delete the fallback (harmless defensive redundancy today, no behaviour change).

confirmed.title: canAssignWorkerToBuilding's builder preview omits hasWorkAssignment/isImprisoned, enabling a button that always fails
confirmed.evidence:
L322-330: "return building.occupants.length < cap && state.entities.some(
      (entity) =>

        && entity.alive

(L97-100). The player is offered an action that can never succeed. The same function is the auto-play bot's eligibility test (virtualPlayer.ts:373).

With every adult employed the preview returns true, SelectedBuildingPanel.tsx:673 renders '+ Fill builders' (assignableWorkers is always empty for incomplete buildings), and the accepted command only prints 'No idle settlers!' at line 98. confirmed.title: StripPlacementPiece.replacesBuildingId is never written, so the wall/gate replacement rule and its 50% refund are unreachable and a gate dropped on a wall silently places nothing
confirmed.evidence: line 159: `if (existing && (existing.type === stripType || existing.type === BuildingType.Wall)) {` — `existing` comes from `findStripBuildingAt(..., 'wall')` whose family set is `WALL_STRIP_TYPES = {Wall, WallGate}` (stripTopology.ts:21-24, 229-233).
confirmed.impact: The guard is asymmetric. Dragging a Wall run: existing Wall -> skipped (`existing.type === BuildingType.Wall`), the run continues; existing WallGate -> neither clause is true, so a piece is emitted at/near the gate, `buildStripPreview` marks it invalid (overlapsAnyBuilding sees the gate), and because the UI commits only when `preview.segments.every((seg) => seg.valid)` (useCanvasInteractions.ts:166 and :479) the player gets NO wall at all — not even the segments that were clear of the gate. Dragging a WallGate run over an existing Wall is handled (second clause), which shows the intended 'same strip family' rule.
confirmed.fix: Skip any existing wall-family piece: `if (existing && isWallStripType(existing.type)) {` (the local helper already exists at line 28 and covers Wall + WallGate).
confirmed.verification: A workspace grep finds `replacesBuildingId` only as a declaration (stripTopology.ts:131, stripBuild.ts:29) and as readers (buildingPlacementActions.ts:207-230, 269-284) — no producer ever assigns it, so the replacement/refund path is dead. resolveWallStripPlan (stripTopology.ts:159-162) drops the piece whenever the existing building is any wall-family piece, including a plain Wall, so dragging a WallGate over a Wall yields an empty plan and useCanvasInteractions.ts:479 sends nothing: no gate, no 50% refund, no feedback. Minimal fix: emit `{type: stripType, x, y, rotation: stripRotation, replacesBuildingId: existing.id}` for the Wall→WallGate case, or delete the field and both unreachable branches.

confirmed.title: syncTreeGrid rebuilds only when the grid object is replaced; a reused tree grid is never reconciled
confirmed.evidence: 497: `if (grid !== existing) {`  498: `grid.rebuild(treeEntities, isTreeGridEntity);` — unlike syncGrassRenderGrid/syncMobileSimGrid/syncHumanSocialGrid there is no `else grid.reconcile(...)`, and `syncSpatialGridEntity` (574-582) only updates the grass and mobile grids.
confirmed.impact: The tree grid is a snapshot taken the first time it is created and is then frozen: any tree that enters the world afterwards is invisible to `findClosestEntityInRadius(ctx.treeGrid, ...)` (humanTick.ts:1404-1412 leisure tree sitting, blueberryForaging.ts:94-102 berry search) because those callers only use the `byType[Tree]` fallback when the grid is undefined. The yearly `nature_boom` event adds 15 trees (groupEvents.ts:1688-1693), so the grid's contract ('Trees - static scenery; indexed for leisure visits') is not upheld. Today the effect is masked because nature_boom pushes its trees only into `allAlive`/entityById and not into `state.entities` (see notes), so this is a latent-but-real cache-invalidation hole rather than an observed one.
confirmed.fix: Add `else grid.reconcile(treeEntities, isTreeGridEntity);` after the rebuild branch so a reused tree grid tracks additions and removals like the other grids.
confirmed.verification: syncTreeGrid (spatialGrid.ts:489-501) rebuilds only when `grid !== existing`, and resolveSpatialGrid (453-463) returns the existing grid whenever the layout matches, so after the first tick the tree grid is frozen; syncMobileSimGrid/syncHumanSocialGrid have `else grid.reconcile(...)` (778, 791) while syncTreeGrid has none. Because findClosestInEntityGrid (simQueries.ts:113-121) ignores the fallback array whenever a grid exists, trees added later are invisible to humanTick.ts:1404-1412 and blueberryForaging.ts:94-102 — and contrary to the finding's note, nature_boom's 15 trees (groupEvents.ts:1738-1743) do land in `state.entities` via gameTick.ts:234, so this is an observable miss, not a latent one. Minimal fix: add `else grid.reconcile(treeEntities, isTreeGridEntity)`.

confirmed.title: Moon Howler scan computes `howlerIds` that is never read, contains an empty `if` block, and its 'zero allocations' comment is false
confirmed.evidence: simulationInvariants.ts:247 `let howlerIds: number[] = [];` is only written (lines 252-253 `if (howlerCount <= 2) { howlerIds.push(e.id); }`) and never read; lines 255-258 are a no-op block (`if (howlerCount > 1) { // We can break early ... }`) and the message re-scans the whole entity list at line 264 `const allHowlerIds = state.entities.filter(e => e.alive && e.moonHowlerCursed).map(e => e.id);`.

(zero allocations)' comment advertises an optimisation the error path does not have (a second full scan plus a map allocation), and the unused buffer invites a future reader to trust ids that are truncated at 2 for any count > 2.
confirmed.fix: Delete line 247 and the push at 252-253, delete the empty `if (howlerCount > 1)` block at 255-258, and build the message from a single array collected in the same pass (`const howlerIds: number[] = []; ... howlerIds.push(e.id);` unconditionally, keeping only the `howlerCount > 1` check for the error).

Minimal fix: delete `howlerIds` and the empty block, collect ids unconditionally in the single pass, and build the message from that array. Diagnostics-only; no gameplay impact.

confirmed.title: Velocity is blended twice in the hangWithCompany leisure branch (0.45/0.55 then 0.5/0.5 in the shared tail), so company-following movement uses a different weight than every other leisure kind
confirmed.evidence: humanTick.ts:1293-1294 (inside `if (hangWithCompany && company)`) `entity.vx = entity.vx * 0.45 + idleVx * 0.55; entity.vy = entity.vy * 0.45 + idleVy * 0.55;`, then the chain is followed by the shared tail humanTick.ts:1441-1442 `entity.vx = entity.vx * 0.5 + idleVx * 0.5; entity.vy = entity.vy * 0.5 + idleVy * 0.5;` which is still inside the `if (!suppressIdle) {` block opened at humanTick.ts:1197 and therefore also runs for the company branch (idleVx/idleVy are non-zero there).
confirmed.impact: The tail re-applies the blend, so a settler walking with partner/child/coworker moves with an effective idle weight of 0.55*0.5 + 0.5 = 0.775 instead of the intended 0.55 (other leisure kinds get 0.5), and `spriteAngle` is computed twice from two different velocity vectors. Company-following steering is therefore much stronger/more snap-to-target than every other idle behaviour, i.e. the branch does not do what its own 0.45/0.55 line implies.
confirmed.fix: Delete the duplicate blend at humanTick.ts:1293-1294 (and its redundant spriteAngle assignment) and let the shared tail at 1440-1445 perform the single blend, as it already does for all other leisure kinds.
confirmed.verification: The `hangWithCompany && company` branch (humanTick.ts:1229-1298) blends at 0.45/0.55 and sets suppressIdle, but the shared tail at 1440-1445 sits inside the `if (!suppressIdle)` block opened at line 1197 (before suppressIdle was set), so it blends again at 0.5/0.5 whenever idleVx/idleVy are non-zero — effective idle weight 0.775 versus 0.5 for other leisure kinds, plus a redundant spriteAngle write. Minimal fix: delete lines 1293-1297 and let the shared tail perform the single blend. Impact is a snappier response, not a different destination.

confirmed.title: Scandal/divorce mode flags are always true, making the 0.7 caught-divorce chance and two guards unreachable
confirmed.evidence: line 938 `custodian.residenceBuildingId = pickResidenceForHuman(custodian, villagers, residences);` has no prison guard, while the leaver branch immediately below does: line 942 `if (leaver.prisonBuildingId == null) {` ... line 949 `leaver.residenceBuildingId = undefined;`

When the offending partner is the wife she becomes the custodian (lines 910-912), so she is immediately handed a fresh residence, the free spouse is evicted to another house (line 947) and the minor children are assigned to the imprisoned mother's house (lines 953-966). Behaviour today matches the caught-in-the-act rule §4 permits, so this is vestigial-flag dead code: delete the flags/branches and the misleading 0.7 constant.

confirmed.title: Hospital routing advances the settler's position in addition to the loop-bottom integration (double movement)
confirmed.impact: Position is written by a behaviour module that does not own movement (SIMULATION_AUTHORITY.md §3: movement owns 'Position, velocity, movement targets'), and the step is applied twice in the same tick, so a routed pregnant/sick settler walks to the ward at roughly 2x the intended 0.55*speed (plus the road multiplier), arriving early and bypassing the intended pacing. The same double-step also happens on ticks where the leisure block later blends vx, because the early `x += vx` already used the hospital vector.
confirmed.fix: Delete lines 82-83 (`entity.x += entity.vx; entity.y += entity.vy;`) and keep only the vx/vy/spriteAngle assignment, matching commuteHumanToBuilding — the main loop's single integration at humanTick.ts:1467 then applies the step exactly once.
confirmed.verification: tickHumanHospitalPatientCare (humanHospitalBehavior.ts:79-83) writes entity.x/y in addition to setting velocity, and it is called at humanTick.ts:1095 inside the per-human loop that integrates position once at 1467-1468 (×1.5 near roads); no `continue` separates them (all five `continue`s in the file are before line 520), so a routed settler advances 2-2.5× per tick and jitters around the hospital. Minimal fix: delete lines 82-83 so the loop-bottom integration remains the only position writer. Reachable in normal mid-game play whenever a staffed hospital exists and a pregnant settler is off-shift or near term.

confirmed.title: Greenhouse food production is never recorded in the economy ledger
confirmed.evidence: L638 `const amount = Math.floor(` … L649 `if (addResource(state, 'food', amount) > 0) {` L650 `rewardProductionSkills(state, building, 0.2, entityById);` L651 `}` — no `recordFoodProduced` call, unlike farms (L359), hunting (L454), fishing (L518) and silos (L780). `ECONOMY_SOURCE_LABELS` (economyLedger.ts:11-17) lists farms/hunting/silos/challenges/meals only, so 'fishing' (recorded at L518) also has no label and renders as its raw key in VillageTabPanel.tsx:85.

Concretely, a greenhouse-only village shows 'No food produced or eaten yet today — build farms or a hunting spot' (VillageTabPanel.tsx:71-77) and 'produced +0 · net 0' while food actually rises, and dashboardData.ts:269-279 reports the same wrong net; the archived foodHistory under-counts for up to 30 days. A greenhouse-only village therefore reads 'No food produced or eaten yet today' / net 0 in VillageTabPanel.tsx:71-77 and dashboardData.ts:270-278 while food actually rises, and foodHistory under-counts. Minimal fix: mirror the farm path — `const added = addResource(state,'food',amount); if (added > 0) { recordFoodProduced(state,'greenhouse',added); rewardProductionSkills(...); }` and add the two labels.

confirmed.title: Stage-notify cooldown guard can never fire — NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_DAYS has no effect
confirmed.evidence: ecologyStage.ts:365-368 `const cooldownOk = day - (state.valleyLastStageNotifyDay ?? -999) >= NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_DAYS || rising || valleyStageIndex(next) <= valleyStageIndex(prev) - 1;` and line 370 `if (!cooldownOk && !rising) return;`
confirmed.impact: `announceStage` is only reached when `next !== current` (line 453), and every transition it can produce is exactly one step (line 445 `STAGE_ORDER[Math.min(newIdx, 3)]` with newIdx = currentIdx+1 capped at 2, line 450 `currentIdx - 1`). Therefore `!rising` implies `valleyStageIndex(next) === valleyStageIndex(prev) - 1`, the third disjunct is always true, `cooldownOk` is always true, and the early return at line 370 is unreachable: the 3-day re-notify cooldown and the `valleyLastStageNotifyDay` field it depends on can never suppress a message.
confirmed.fix: Either drop the third disjunct and gate on the cooldown alone (`if (day - (state.valleyLastStageNotifyDay ?? -999) < NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_DAYS) return;`), or delete NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_DAYS, `valleyLastStageNotifyDay` and the guard if one notification per transition is the intent.
confirmed.verification: announceStage (ecologyStage.ts:350-396) is reached only when `next !== current`, and both producers of `next` move the stage by exactly one index (upward `STAGE_ORDER[Math.min(newIdx,3)]` at 445, downward `STAGE_ORDER[Math.max(0, currentIdx-1)]` at 450), so `!rising` always satisfies the third disjunct and `cooldownOk` is always true — the return at 370 and NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_DAYS/valleyLastStageNotifyDay can never suppress a message. Minimal fix: either gate on the cooldown alone (drop the third disjunct) or delete the constant and field. No state or gameplay corruption; a dead guard only.

confirmed.title: Every herd death is reported and accounted as 'hunted'
confirmed.evidence:
81:    const killed = active.spawned - alive;
85:      addBigNews(state, '🦌 The herds remember', `${killed} deer taken from the passing herd — next autumn will bring fewer.`, 'negative');
confirmed.impact: `alive` counts surviving tagged deer, so a deer killed by wolves, a predator, or any non-player cause is counted as taken and permanently shrinks migrationNextHerdSize (line 84). confirmed.title: Seasonal festivals are not actually guaranteed; a lone eligible tick can be blocked by a random festival
confirmed.impact: The comment at lines 46-48 promises '5 days at the start of each season: 20 guaranteed festival days per year', but the seasonal festival has exactly one eligible tick per season and the `!state.festival` condition blocks it whenever a random festival is active. Random festivals last 20-39 days (line 75) and can be running on days 3 (a day-350 start carrying over), 183 (a day-150 start) and 273 (a day-250 start), and there is no retry, so that season's seasonal festival is silently lost - the 'guaranteed' 20 days can be 0, 5 or 10.
confirmed.fix: Record a pending seasonal festival (or a per-season flag) and start it on the first free day, e.g. `if (!state.festival && dayInYear >= seasonalStart + 3 && dayInYear < seasonalStart + 8 && !state.seasonalFestivalDone?.includes(seasonalStart))` setting the flag when it starts.
confirmed.verification: tickFestivals (dailyWorldEvents.ts:37-92) gives the seasonal festival exactly one eligible tick per season (`dayInYear === seasonalStart + 3`, line 51) and skips it whenever `state.festival` is already active, while a random festival lasts 20-39 days (line 75) with no retry, so a festival that began up to 39 days earlier silently cancels that season's 'guaranteed' five days promised by the comment at 46-48. Minimal fix: remember a per-season pending/done flag and start the seasonal festival on the first free day inside a window (e.g. dayInYear in [seasonalStart+3, seasonalStart+8)). Downgraded to low: only the named festival and its +5 reputation are lost, and festival days are still provided by the random festival.

confirmed.title: The Demonstration card is re-queued every day and each duplicate can be resolved again for free wood/reputation
confirmed.evidence: 212: `id: `invention_stage2_${state.tick}`,` inside tickInventionFair, whose only guards are `if (storyFlag(state, FLAG_RESOLVED) > 0) return;` (199) and `!== STATUS.funded` (200) — unlike travelingTheatre's FLAG_STAGE3 guard (225-230) there is no once-only flag, and pushStoryCard dedupes by id only (storyHelpers.ts:29), so a new id is queued on every daily call from resolveDay until the player answers. resolveInventionFair (139-143) has no FLAG_RESOLVED check and FLAG_STATUS is never moved off STATUS.funded (188-193).

The lingering queue also blocks every other authored story, since their offer guards require an empty pendingStoryEvents (e.g. inventionFair.ts:87, dailyWorldEvents.ts:110-126).
confirmed.fix: Add a once-only flag (e.g. `const FLAG_DEMO_OFFERED = 'invention_fair_demo_offered'`), return early when it is > 0, and set it with setStoryFlags immediately before pushStoryCard; also return early in resolveInventionFair when `storyFlag(state, FLAG_RESOLVED) > 0`.
confirmed.verification: tickInventionFair (inventionFair.ts:198-229) pushes a card with a unique id (`invention_stage2_${state.tick}`) on every daily call until FLAG_RESOLVED is set — pushStoryCard dedupes by id only (storyHelpers.ts:27-32) — and resolveInventionFair (139-143) never checks FLAG_RESOLVED while FLAG_STATUS stays 'funded', so each leftover duplicate re-runs resolveStage2: 'dismantle' pays +4 wood, 'keep'/'improve' +1/+2 reputation (231-248), and the lingering queue blocks other authored stories. Minimal fix: set a once-only offered flag before pushStoryCard and return early in resolveInventionFair when `storyFlag(state, FLAG_RESOLVED) > 0`. confirmed.title: RenderSnapshot dirty key omits view.selectedEntityIds, so a shift-deselect can reuse a stale snapshot and keep drawing the removed settler's selection ring

confirmed.title: buildHousingUnits merges adult children into the parents' housing unit, so the adult-child move-out is undone inside the same assignMissingResidences call
confirmed.evidence: residencySelection.ts:267-268 `const unit: Entity[] = [custodian]; visited.add(custodian.id);` — the bucket loop never checks `visited.has(custodianId)` before building the unit (contrast the fallback loop at line 284: `if (visited.has(human.id)) continue;` and the partner guard at line 270 `if (partner && !visited.has(partner.id))`).
confirmed.impact: Concrete failure: mother M has minor child A (custodian M), father F has minor child B (custodian F, B's mother dead), and M and F are partners (a blended family created by remarriage — reachable through humanTick.ts:910/tryCompleteCourtshipMarriage). Bucket[M]=[A] builds unit [M,F,A] and marks F visited, but bucket[F]=[B] still builds unit [F,B] containing F again. In assignMissingResidences (residencyReconciliation.ts:230-239) every unit that needs reassignment clears and re-places ALL of its members, so F is moved twice per pass and the two units keep stealing him: [F,B] is placed in an empty house, then [M,F,A] (now invalid) is cleared and placed in another empty house, and the 24-pass loop never records `reassigned === 0`, so it runs all 24 passes on every assign pulse (4x/day). The stable end state leaves the minor child B alone in one house while F, M and A occupy another — the exact opposite of assignFamilyToResidence's contract ('keeps children with custodian'); ensureOrphanAdoption cannot repair it because B still has a living natural custodian, so the split persists across pulses.
confirmed.fix: Add the missing guard at the top of the bucket loop: `if (visited.has(custodianId)) continue;` (and attach that bucket's children to the custodian's existing unit, or rebuild the children buckets from the emitted units) so each settler belongs to exactly one housing unit; the child whose custodian is already in a unit must join that unit rather than fall through to the single-entity fallback at line 283.
confirmed.verification: The mechanism is real: buildHousingUnits' second loop (residencySelection.ts:283-288) calls collectOwnHousehold, which appends every alive childrenIds entry with no age filter (householdComposition.ts:19), and rebuildChildrenIds (residencyReconciliation.ts:48-54) rebuilds those links for adults too. For a parent with no minor children the unit spans both houses, isFamilyHousingValid fails, and the convergence loop (residencyReconciliation.ts:220-247) unassigns and re-homes the whole unit together, so a lone adult child's move-out never persists; I traced that an adult child who heads their own unit (partner/minor children) does end up split, but only after every call runs all 24 passes. This is exactly the root cause left unresolved in BUG_REPORTS/2026-09-13-move-out-reverted-by-residency-reconciliation.md. Minimal fix: build the second-loop unit as seed + living partner + isMinorChild members only.

confirmed.title: YOUTH_LOVE_MIN_AGE = 12 lets 12-13 year olds enter youth love, violating the section 5 invariant and the feature spec
confirmed.evidence: line 441: `export const YOUTH_LOVE_MIN_AGE = 12;` - consumed at line 473 `entity.age >= YOUTH_LOVE_MIN_AGE &&` (isEligibleForYouthLove) and line 553 `if (entity.age < YOUTH_LOVE_MIN_AGE || partner.age < YOUTH_LOVE_MIN_AGE) {`
confirmed.impact: SIMULATION_AUTHORITY.md section 5 states "Youth love begins only from age 14 through 17" (and section 3 row: "Youth love (ages 14-17)"); docs/archive/YOUTH_LOVE_FEATURE.md:29 lists ages 12-13 as "Not eligible". advanceYouthLove iterates every entry of ctx.playerHumans with no isJuvenile filter (line 541), so a 12- or 13-year-old passes isEligibleForYouthLove, can be matched (YOUTH_LOVE_MAX_AGE_GAP = 4 at line 443 even lets a 12-year-old pair with a 16-year-old via line 490), receives mutual youthLovePartnerId/progress 1 plus the "became sweethearts" Chronicle event (lines 599-611), and that link then blocks adult courtship at isEligibleToCourt (line 1229). No existing test covers youth-love ages, so the drift is unguarded.

confirmed.verification: YOUTH_LOVE_MIN_AGE = 12 (line 441) is consumed by isEligibleForYouthLove (473) and advanceYouthLove (553), and advanceYouthLove iterates playerHumans without any juvenile/age-14 gate (541), so a 12-year-old can be matched (YOUTH_LOVE_MAX_AGE_GAP 4 at 443/490), gets mutual youthLovePartnerId with progress 1 plus the 'became sweethearts' event (599-611), and that link blocks adult courtship (isEligibleToCourt:1229). SIMULATION_AUTHORITY.md §5 says 'Youth love begins only from age 14 through 17', README.md:158 says 'From age 14', and docs/archive/YOUTH_LOVE_FEATURE.md:29/42 lists 12-13 as not eligible; git shows 14 was changed to 12 in commit 349f49e with no doc update, and no test anywhere covers youth-love ages (the referenced tests/youthLove.lifecycle.test.ts does not exist). confirmed.title: Visitor position advanced twice per tick after steerWithPath already moved the entity

confirmed.title: Nature-tab "Why this score" is a second, drifted implementation of the ecosystem-health formula (no preserve bonus, 4-species wildlife)
confirmed.evidence: ecoBreakdown.ts:33 `const totalWildlife = counts.rabbits + counts.deer + counts.wolves + counts.foxes;` and ecoBreakdown.ts:51 `const health = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, 100 - buildingImpact - pollutionPenalty + wildlifeBonus));` — versus the owner at dailyEcology.ts:87-93 (`counts.rabbits + deer + wolves + foxes + werewolves + wildkin`) and dailyEcology.ts:101 `const rawEcoHealth = 100 - buildingImpact - pollutionPenalty + preserveBonus + wildlifeImpact;` with `preserveBonus += 4` per WildlifePreserve (dailyEcology.ts:76-78).

confirmed.fix: Add chronicleChapters to SimTickDelta (interface, extractSimTickDelta, applySimTickDelta) and to SimPrepKeys/extractSimPrep/applySimPrep, the same way storyFlags/pendingStoryEvents are carried; extend tests/simDelta.storyRoundtrip.test.ts to assert the round-trip.
confirmed.verification: chronicleChapters is written by advanceValleyChronicle:89 in the daily layer but is missing from SimPrepKeys/extractSimPrep/applySimPrep (simWorker/simPrep.ts:10-87) and from SimTickDelta/extract/apply (simBuffers/simDelta.ts:52-139), so worker-side unlocks never travel in the tick delta and applySimPrep rollback (gameWorker.ts:339/345/355) keeps the consumed chapter while reverting its reward. confirmed.title: Rite cooldown and priest-flee window are written every full moon but carried by no save/prep/delta path
confirmed.evidence:
moonHowler.ts:693  `  state.lastMoonHowlerExorcismTick = state.tick;`
moonHowler.ts:812  `      state.moonHowlerPriestsFleeUntil = state.tick + MOON_HOWLER_EXORCISM_INTERVAL_HOURS * TICKS_PER_HOUR;`
confirmed.impact: Neither field is in WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS (saveSchema.ts:4-26) nor in SimPrepKeys (src/game/simWorker/simPrep.ts:10-87), and simDelta's world tuple only carries renffrOmen/renffrChatterUntilTick (simDelta.ts:126-127). confirmed.lines: 791-802; tickLeaderVacancy 888-905; leaderHouse.ts:42-79 | 891-900 (with 902-905 as the only place that schedules an election; caller src/game/dailyWorldEvents.ts:230)
confirmed.title: Zero-candidate election reveal clears villageLeaderId without stepping the office down or scheduling a successor election
confirmed.impact: When the leader dies (or is otherwise non-acting) and every remaining adult is ineligible (e.g. the only other adult is serving a scandal sentence, or only juveniles remain - isEligibleForLeadership requires alive/Human/player/adult/not imprisoned), this branch nulls villageLeaderId and returns WITHOUT setting pendingElectionYear. Every later daily call then returns at the `leaderId == null` guard, so the vacancy-election schedule is never re-established even after settlers grow up or are released from prison: the colony has no head, no 'leadership vacancy' notice (focusHints.ts:109 and getElectionCeremonyStatus both require pendingElectionYear != null), and only reaches a leader again at the next even-year term election (tryStartTermElectionCeremony requires year % 2 === 0) - up to 2 game years with no election, while the leader invariant check (simulationInvariants.ts:271) is silently skipped because villageLeaderId is null. tickLeaderVacancy is also the only scheduler of pendingElectionYear besides save-load (validateVillageLeaderOnLoad:1019), so this state survives until the player reloads.
confirmed.fix: Schedule the vacancy election in this branch instead of only clearing the office, i.e. replace the early `return null` with the same `state.pendingElectionYear = state.year + (state.dayInYear ?? 0) / DAYS_PER_YEAR + VACANCY_ELECTION_DELAY_YEARS` write used below (keeping the office cleared and logging the vacancy), or re-arm when `state.villageLeaderId == null && state.pendingElectionYear == null && state.lastElectionYear !== 0`.
confirmed.verification: runVillageElection's zero-candidate branch (villageLeadership.ts:792-802) clears villageLeaderId without calling applyLeaderOccupation(prevId) or syncLeaderHouseResidency and without setting pendingElectionYear, and tickLeaderVacancy returns immediately when leaderId == null (892), so no successor election is ever scheduled; the deposition is reachable because startElectionCeremony only needs one candidate at start (629-639) while the ~60-day gossip/tension phases (getPhaseTicks:39-49) can outlive or imprison every candidate. The deposed incumbent keeps occupation 'leader' indefinitely because applyLeaderOccupation only steps down the id passed in (leaderHouse.ts:42-52) and workforce's keepOffice preserves the label (workforce.ts:206-209, 260-262). Minimal fix: capture prevId, call applyLeaderOccupation + syncLeaderHouseResidency, and schedule the successor using the vacancy delay.

confirmed.title: availableScripts uses eventLog.slice(-40), which is the oldest 40 entries of a newest-first log, not the recent history the comment claims
confirmed.evidence: 62: `const recent = state.eventLog.slice(-40);` with the local named `recent` and the module comment promising 'script selection from real history' (line 4). eventLog is newest-first: eventLog.ts:23 `state.eventLog.unshift({...})`, and simDelta.ts:236 takes `world.eventLog.slice(0, EVENT_LOG_DELTA_TAIL_MAX)` as the recent tail. `slice(-40)` therefore returns the last 40 entries of the array, i.e. the colony's oldest recorded events.
confirmed.impact: The theatre only becomes eligible at colony day 50-110 (MIN_DAY 50 + seeded window, line 23/54) by which time the 2000-entry log holds far more than 40 entries, so the offered plays (and the /foot/i famine detection at 75) are decided by the first days of the colony and freeze permanently — new disasters/combats/scandals can no longer unlock a script. If those oldest entries yield no script, the function returns at 89 without setting any flag and retries the same dead history every day, so the story never starts.
confirmed.fix: `const recent = state.eventLog.slice(0, 40);`
confirmed.verification: The event log is newest-first (logEvent unshifts, eventLog.ts:23; simDelta takes slice(0,n) as the tail, simBuffers/simDelta.ts:236; EventLogPanel renders from the front, EventLogPanel.tsx:66-73), so travelingTheatre.ts:62's slice(-40) selects the 40 OLDEST retained entries out of up to 2000. Script availability (64-77) is therefore decided by early-game history, and since maybeOfferTravelingTheatre returns early when the script list is empty (88-89) the whole theatre story can be suppressed forever once the first 40 events contain no matching type. Minimal fix: `const recent = state.eventLog.slice(0, 40);`.

confirmed.title: Tick-timeline migration rescales `pregnancyProgress` but not its due threshold
confirmed.evidence: L244-245: `// pregnancyProgress is 0..PREGNANCY_TICKS absolute progress — scale with day length` / `scaleField(rec, 'pregnancyProgress');` — the sibling `entity.pregnancyDueProgress` (set from the same constant at humanRelationships.ts:640) is not in the scaled list; `pendingStoryEvents[].createdAtTick/expiresAtTick` are also skipped even though storyEvents.ts:158 compares them against `state.tick`.
confirmed.impact: In any load that needs a rescale (`_ticksPerDay !== TICKS_PER_DAY`), progress is multiplied by `scale` while the threshold keeps the old unit. With scale>1 (24→72 ticks/day) a mid-pregnancy settler's `pregnancyProgress` jumps past `pregnancyDueProgress`, so humanLifecycle.ts:63-66 delivers on the next pregnancy tick; with scale<1 the pregnancy never reaches term. Pending story cards likewise expire instantly (scale>1) or linger far past their window (scale<1). Currently latent only because `parseSaveJson` rejects every `_version` except the current one and current saves always write `_ticksPerDay = TICKS_PER_DAY`.
confirmed.fix: Add `scaleField(rec, 'pregnancyDueProgress');` next to the existing `pregnancyProgress` line, and scale `createdAtTick`/`expiresAtTick` for each entry of `world.pendingStoryEvents` in the same migration.
confirmed.verification: migrateTickTimeline scales pregnancyProgress (saveLoad.ts:245, plus the nested moonHowlerSaved copy at 249) but never pregnancyDueProgress, and never scales pendingStoryEvents' createdAtTick/expiresAtTick — exactly as claimed — which would deliver or strand pregnancies and story cards for any rescaled load. The defect is currently unreachable: the function returns early unless parsed._ticksPerDay !== TICKS_PER_DAY (222-224), saveLoad.ts:107 is the only writer of _ticksPerDay and always writes TICKS_PER_DAY, and parseSaveJson rejects every non-current version, so no loadable save triggers a rescale. Minimal fix: add scaleField(rec, 'pregnancyDueProgress') and scale the pending story-card deadlines alongside the existing fields.
