confirmed.title: Both daily-layer entry guards are always true, so they document a tick-0 path that cannot exist
confirmed.evidence:
src/game/tickLayerDaily.ts:46: `if (isNewCalendarDayTick(state)) {`
src/game/tickLayerDaily.ts:51: `if (state.tick > 0) {`
confirmed.impact: gameTick is the only caller (gameTick.ts:220) and invokes the layer only when `state.tick % TICKS_PER_DAY === 0`; state.tick is incremented before that test (gameTick.ts:76), so the first possible call is tick 72, and markCalendarDayProcessed (dayCycle.ts:320-324) writes lastProcessedCalendarDay = floor(tick/72) at every boundary, so `day > lastProcessed` holds at every call. Both guards are therefore unconditionally true: the 'skip tick 0 initialization' comment is misleading, the schedule invariant is enforced only in gameTick, and any future direct caller (the module is exported through gameEngine.ts:308) would silently skip the social/chronicle block instead of failing loudly.
confirmed.fix: Delete the redundant `if (isNewCalendarDayTick(state))` and `if (state.tick > 0)` wrappers (or replace them with an explicit assertion that the tick is a day boundary) and drop the tick-0 comment.
confirmed.verification: Verified: tickLayerDaily is called only from gameTick.ts:220-221 after state.tick++ (line 76) and only when tick % TICKS_PER_DAY === 0, so the first call is tick 72; isNewCalendarDayTick (dayCycleClock.ts:95-110) tests `day > lastProcessedCalendarDay`, which markCalendarDayProcessed (dayCycle.ts:320-324) rewrites at every boundary, so both guards are unconditionally true and the 'skip tick 0 initialization' comment is misleading. However there is no behavioural defect (they are harmless defensive checks), and the supporting claim that the daily entry is exported through gameEngine.ts:308 is wrong — that line re-exports only tickGrassDaily. Minimal change if desired: delete the tick-0 comment (and optionally the redundant isNewCalendarDayTick wrapper).

confirmed.title: buildHousingUnits never checks whether the custodian is already visited, so one settler can belong to two housing units in the same pass
confirmed.evidence: residencySelection.ts:267-268 `const unit: Entity[] = [custodian]; visited.add(custodian.id);` — the bucket loop never checks `visited.has(custodianId)` before building the unit (contrast the fallback loop at line 284: `if (visited.has(human.id)) continue;` and the partner guard at line 270 `if (partner && !visited.has(partner.id))`).
confirmed.impact: Concrete failure: mother M has minor child A (custodian M), father F has minor child B (custodian F, B's mother dead), and M and F are partners (a blended family created by remarriage — reachable through humanTick.ts:910/tryCompleteCourtshipMarriage). Bucket[M]=[A] builds unit [M,F,A] and marks F visited, but bucket[F]=[B] still builds unit [F,B] containing F again. In assignMissingResidences (residencyReconciliation.ts:230-239) every unit that needs reassignment clears and re-places ALL of its members, so F is moved twice per pass and the two units keep stealing him: [F,B] is placed in an empty house, then [M,F,A] (now invalid) is cleared and placed in another empty house, and the 24-pass loop never records `reassigned === 0`, so it runs all 24 passes on every assign pulse (4x/day). The stable end state leaves the minor child B alone in one house while F, M and A occupy another — the exact opposite of assignFamilyToResidence's contract ('keeps children with custodian'); ensureOrphanAdoption cannot repair it because B still has a living natural custodian, so the split persists across pulses.
confirmed.fix: Add the missing guard at the top of the bucket loop: `if (visited.has(custodianId)) continue;` (and attach that bucket's children to the custodian's existing unit, or rebuild the children buckets from the emitted units) so each settler belongs to exactly one housing unit; the child whose custodian is already in a unit must join that unit rather than fall through to the single-entity fallback at line 283.
confirmed.verification: Verified in buildHousingUnits: the custodian is pushed into `unit` and marked visited (267-268) without a `visited.has(custodian.id)` test, while the partner and child members are guarded (270, 275); getChildCustodian (householdComposition.ts:37-56) returns the living mother first and otherwise the father, so a widower's child and his new partner's child have different custodians, and a 14-17-year-old mother custodies her baby while she is herself a child in her own custodian's bucket. The second bucket re-adds the already-visited member, and because pickResidenceForFamily (600+) prefers an empty house the two units settle in different houses, so each pass moves the shared member, `reassigned` never reaches 0, and residencyReconciliation.ts:220-247 burns all 24 passes 4x/day (LAYER_ASSIGN_INTERVAL 18, tickLayerAssign.ts:17), leaving the shared settler with whichever unit ran last. Minimal fix: `if (visited.has(custodian.id)) continue;` after line 265.

confirmed.title: Wall-run planning skips existing walls but not existing wall gates, so a run that touches a gate is refused wholesale
confirmed.evidence: line 159: `if (existing && (existing.type === stripType || existing.type === BuildingType.Wall)) {` — `existing` comes from `findStripBuildingAt(..., 'wall')` whose family set is `WALL_STRIP_TYPES = {Wall, WallGate}` (stripTopology.ts:21-24, 229-233).
confirmed.impact: The guard is asymmetric. Dragging a Wall run: existing Wall -> skipped (`existing.type === BuildingType.Wall`), the run continues; existing WallGate -> neither clause is true, so a piece is emitted at/near the gate, `buildStripPreview` marks it invalid (overlapsAnyBuilding sees the gate), and because the UI commits only when `preview.segments.every((seg) => seg.valid)` (useCanvasInteractions.ts:166 and :479) the player gets NO wall at all — not even the segments that were clear of the gate. Dragging a WallGate run over an existing Wall is handled (second clause), which shows the intended 'same strip family' rule.
confirmed.fix: Skip any existing wall-family piece: `if (existing && isWallStripType(existing.type)) {` (the local helper already exists at line 28 and covers Wall + WallGate).
confirmed.verification: Verified in resolveWallStripPlan: the skip test at line 159 covers `existing.type === stripType || existing.type === BuildingType.Wall`, but findStripBuildingAt(..., 'wall') matches WALL_STRIP_TYPES = {Wall, WallGate} (21-24, 229-241), so an existing WallGate is never skipped. Wall and WallGate both snap x to multiples of 60 and y to the shared grid (snapBuildingCenter, buildingRotation.ts:63-83), so any Wall drag spanning a gate emits a piece exactly on it; that segment fails canPlaceBuilding via overlapsAnyBuilding (placementUtils.ts:131) and useCanvasInteractions.ts:166/479 commits only when `preview.segments.every(seg => seg.valid)`, so the whole run — including clear segments — is silently refused. Minimal fix: `if (existing && isWallStripType(existing.type))` (helper already at line 28).

confirmed.title: Third copy of UNBUILDABLE_TERRAIN is exported but no consumer reads it
confirmed.evidence: lines 25-32 `export const UNBUILDABLE_TERRAIN = new Set<TerrainType>([...])` plus line 34 `export { isFootprintOnBuildableTerrain, isFootprintWithinMapBounds } from './placementUtils';`; the same set is defined privately at placementUtils.ts:10-17 (used by `isUnbuildableTerrainType`, line 25) and a third time at terrainGen.ts:113. confirmed.title: Candidate metric is counted before the predicate in grid mode but after it in naive mode
confirmed.verification: Verified: forEachAdaptiveInRadius's grid branch (125-128) calls grid.forEachInRadius with the default `recordCandidates = true` (spatialGrid.ts:295, 329), which counts every in-radius entity before the caller's predicate at line 126, whereas the naive branch counts after the predicate (56/63) and findClosestInRadius passes false and records after (spatialGrid.ts:383-394).
