confirmed.title: On-duty official service can never run: `ordinaryWorkplace` excludes the TownHall, so `onDayJobShift` is always false for an Official
confirmed.evidence: humanTick.ts:412 `(state.tick + entity.id) % 3 === 0` gates the call `tryAmbientRandomDialogue(entity, ambientChatNeighbors(entity), state.tick, 0.036 * PER_TICK_RATE_SCALE, ...)`. The candidate provider is `simAmbientChatNeighbors` (humanTick.ts:282-283), and humanSocial.ts:64 begins `if ((tick + self.id) % SOCIAL_STAGGER !== 0) { return []; }` with adaptiveSpatialQuery.ts:205 `export const SOCIAL_STAGGER = 6;`. Multiples of 3 are not all multiples of 6.
confirmed.impact: For every tick where (tick+id) % 6 === 3 (exactly half of the ticks the caller admits), ambientChatNeighbors() returns an empty array, so `tryAmbientRandomDialogue` can never pair the speaker with a nearby settler and always emits a solo remark. Paired ambient conversation therefore fires at roughly half the rate the code intends, which is precisely the monologue regression documented in tests/humanChat.ambientPairing.test.ts (BUG 2026-08-21-ambient-dialogue-often-becomes-leader-monologue) — that test calls tryAmbientRandomDialogue directly and so cannot see the caller-side gate.
confirmed.fix: Replace the caller's `(state.tick + entity.id) % 3 === 0` with the same stagger the callee uses: `(state.tick + entity.id) % SOCIAL_STAGGER === 0` (SOCIAL_STAGGER is already imported in humanTick.ts line 113). This keeps the expensive-neighbour-query short-circuit while guaranteeing every admitted roll actually receives candidates.
confirmed.verification: Verified: ordinaryWorkplace (538-541) excludes Church and TownHall, BUILDING_JOB_TYPES maps TownHall -> JobType.Official (gameTypes.ts:184), schoolTarget is set only for juveniles (364-367), so onDayJobShift (543-550) is false for every Official and officialHandlePetitioners (humanVenueBehavior.ts:85 -> townHall.ts:308) is unreachable — the hall description still promises petitions/audiences (townHall.ts:157). One impact bullet is overstated: officials do gain Official skill from petitions through the daily owner tickTownHallAudiences (townHall.ts:345-361, called every 3 days from dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:769), which grants +0.06 to hall occupants. Minimal fix: compute `onOfficialShift = entity.job === JobType.Official && workplace?.type === BuildingType.TownHall && workplace.completed && goWorkTime` and pass `onDayJobShift || onOfficialShift` at line 1092.

confirmed.title: Affair conception path creates ages 14-17 pregnancies without the documented youth-love gate
confirmed.evidence: lines 789-799: the affair branch gates only on `hasAffairPartner(entity, ctx.entityById) && entity.energy > ... && !isSpouseNearby(...)` and then rolls `if (Math.random() < HUMAN_DAILY_AFFAIR_PREGNANCY_CHANCE * fertility) {` (line 799). The youth branch directly above instead requires `entity.age >= HUMAN_FERTILITY_START && entity.age < HUMAN_YOUTH_FERTILITY_END` (lines 754-755).
confirmed.impact: isValidAffairTarget (line 622) admits targets from HUMAN_ADULT_MIN_AGE = 16, so a 16-17-year-old single settler can become an established affair partner through the daily owner. tryDailyConception is called for every non-prisoner player human (humanTick.ts:330), so that settler then rolls the full adult affair rate 0.14 x fertility (fertility = 1 up to age 35) - roughly 45x (age 17) to 60x (age 16) the youth-gate chance (0.0045 x 0.50 at 16) - with no mutual youth-love link and no age check, contradicting SIMULATION_AUTHORITY.md section 5: "At ages 14-17 it requires the documented mutual youth-love, nearby, energy, and reduced-probability gate".
confirmed.fix: Restrict the affair branch to adults, e.g. add `&& !(entity.age >= HUMAN_FERTILITY_START && entity.age < HUMAN_YOUTH_FERTILITY_END)` to the condition at line 789 (or require `entity.age >= HUMAN_YOUTH_FERTILITY_END`), so ages 14-17 can only conceive through the youth branch.
confirmed.verification: Verified in tryDailyConception: the affair branch (789-799) gates only on hasAffairPartner, energy, spouse distance and tryst site, then rolls HUMAN_DAILY_AFFAIR_PREGNANCY_CHANCE * fertility with no 14-17 restriction, whereas the youth branch above requires age 14-17 plus a mutual youth-love partner (753-786). isValidAffairTarget (617-627) admits targets from HUMAN_ADULT_MIN_AGE = 16 and tryDailyAffairEncounter (1339-1443) establishes mutual affairPartnerId for such a paramour, so a 16-17-year-old mother conceives once per colony day (humanTick.ts:330-331) at 0.14 x fertility instead of the ~0.00225 youth rate, contradicting SIMULATION_AUTHORITY section 5. Minimal fix: add `&& entity.age >= HUMAN_YOUTH_FERTILITY_END` (or an equivalent non-youth guard) to the affair branch.

confirmed.title: Commute path branch moves the entity and then the caller's single movement apply moves it again
confirmed.verification: Verified: steerWithPath documents 'path' as 'caller must not move it again' (pathfinding.ts:298-299) and itself applies `entity.x += entity.vx` (341-344), but commuteHumanToBuilding returns plain `false` for 'path' (150) and the humanTick commute callers ignore the return value (e.g. 768) while the loop-bottom integration `entity.x += entity.vx * roadMult` (1467) always runs — the only `continue`s are at lines 317-513, all before the commute block. Pathed commuters therefore integrate the same velocity twice per tick (~2x off-road; ~1.67x on road, not the cited ~2.1x). Minimal fix: return a tri-state and let the caller skip its integration, or zero vx/vy before returning false.

confirmed.title: Free-time civic petition is a per-day decision re-evaluated every tick while the settler stands near the hall
confirmed.impact: personDayRoll() hashes getAbsoluteCalendarDay(tick), so both the caller's roll (salt 841) and resolveCivicPetition's own guards (821/822-826) are constant for all 72 ticks of a day. A free-roaming settler parked at the hall (leisureKind 5 steers to `hall.y + hall.height + 6`, well inside the 40px/52px radii, for a whole 240-tick leisure slot) therefore calls resolveCivicPetition on every tick: officials gain 0.06 Official skill per tick (~14 skill per loiter window), addReputation(1) fires per tick until reputation saturates at 100 (simHelpers.ts:95), the aid_food branch subtracts food per tick, and the fall-through at townHall.ts:295 forces a chat phrase every tick. The declared intent ('At most one meaningful petition per person per few days') is not enforced by any state.
confirmed.fix: Make the call once per settler per day: record the absolute calendar day on success (e.g. `if (resolveCivicPetition(...).kind !== 'none') entity.lastCivicPetitionDay = getAbsoluteCalendarDay(state.tick);` and return early when it already equals today), or delete this realtime caller and let the existing daily owner townHall.ts:345 `tickTownHallAudiences` be the only petition path.
confirmed.verification: Verified: personDayRoll (humanSchedule.ts:98-107) hashes only entityId, absolute day and salt, so the caller's salt-841 roll (121) and resolveCivicPetition's internal rolls (townHall.ts:209 `821 + day`, 822-826) are constant for all 72 ticks, and no petition-day state exists anywhere (grep finds no such field). While a free-roaming settler sits at the hall (leisureKind 5 steers to `hall.y + hall.height + 6`, humanTick.ts:1344-1348, called every tick from 1102) the function therefore runs per tick, granting each hall occupant +0.06 Official skill on the 0-100 scale (townHall.ts:222-224), +1 reputation, food/gold aid, and a chat phrase. Minimal fix: record a per-settler 'last petition day' and return early when it equals today, or delete this realtime caller and keep tickTownHallAudiences as the only petition path.

confirmed.title: Silo spoilage clamp 0.01 defeats the formula's own 0.8% result
confirmed.evidence: L8 `export function updateStorageCaps(state: WorldState) {` ... L17 `gold: 20000,` ... L20 `state.foodSpoilageRate = Math.max(0.01, 0.02 - silos * 0.012);` — a repo-wide search for `updateStorageCaps` returns only this definition, `docs`-adjacent notes and tests/economyAudit.storageCaps.test.ts; no production path (tickDailyBuildingEconomy at dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:245-254, building completion at dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:166-201, demolition, upgrade, save load) ever calls it.
confirmed.impact: The only writer of `state.storageMax`/`state.foodSpoilageRate` after world creation never runs, so the caps stay at worldGen.ts:577 `{ wood: 1000, stone: 500, food: 1000, gold: 2000, iron: 500 }` and worldGen.ts:618 `foodSpoilageRate: 0.03` forever. Concrete: a new game's gold cap is 2000 instead of the designed 20000 (frontierCombat.ts:669 calls storageMax.gold 'effectively unlimited'), so gold gifts/taxes/rewards saturate 10x early; building a Wood Storehouse ('+800 wood storage', buildings.ts:231), Barn ('extends wood storage +300', buildings.ts:205) or Silo ('Passive food storage bonus', buildings.ts:218) changes nothing; spoilage stays 3%/day instead of the intended 2% (and a Silo's 0.8%/day, which tests/economyAudit.storageCaps.test.ts asserts). The existing passing test therefore verifies a function that is dead in the shipped game.
confirmed.fix: Call `updateStorageCaps(state)` from `tickDailyBuildingEconomy` (dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:245, before `tickBuildingProgress`) and/or from `tickBuildingProgress` when `completedAny`/demolition/upgrade changes building counts; since the function then writes `foodSpoilageRate` during a tick, add `'foodSpoilageRate'` to `SimPrepKeys` and to `extractSimPrep`/`applySimPrep` (simPrep.ts:10-87, 116-117) so the tick rollback restores it.
confirmed.verification: Verified in updateStorageCaps: `Math.max(0.01, 0.02 - silos * 0.012)` yields 0.01 with one silo rather than the 0.008 asserted by the 'cuts spoilage to 0.8%' test (economyAudit.storageCaps.test.ts:63-69), which passes only because toBeCloseTo's precision-2 tolerance is 0.005; two or more silos clamp back to 0.01. The deviation is 0.2 percentage points of spoilage (25% relative on that term) and silos still add +600 food storage, so this is a minor defect: low. Minimal fix: lower the floor (e.g. 0.005) so one silo gives 0.008, or remove the silo term and correct the test title.

confirmed.title: A continued food shortage re-notifies "Animal shortage" every colony day; the shortage marker is written but never read
confirmed.verification: Verified in tickAnimalCare: the shortage branch (96-103) writes FLAG_SHORTAGE_DAY but never clears FLAG_WARNING_DAY, and animal_care_shortage_day is declared at line 17 and read nowhere in the repo, so once `colonyDay - warningDay >= 2` holds it stays true and an identical 'Animal shortage' notification is appended on every unfed day (addNotification pushes unconditionally and shifts past 20, simEffects.ts:69-78); the early return at line 60 also lets a stale warning day survive zero-animal periods. The existing tests (animalCare.test.ts:60-89) only assert status transitions, so nothing locks the behaviour. Minimal fix: also require `(state.storyFlags?.[FLAG_SHORTAGE_DAY] ?? -1) < 0` before re-notifying.

confirmed.title: sufficientGrass can never be false, so the grass gate on prey respawn is dead
confirmed.evidence:
404:  const totalAvailableGrass = grassCount + (grassReplenished ? 98 : 0);
405:  const sufficientGrass = totalAvailableGrass >= 45;
confirmed.impact: grassReplenished is set exactly when grassCount < MIN_GRASS (65), so totalAvailableGrass is either grassCount+98 (>=98) or grassCount (>=65); both are >=45, so sufficientGrass can never be false. needsRabbits/needsDeer therefore reduce to `rabbits < 35` / `deer < 12` and the intended 'prey animals depend on grass' rule is inert: with grassCount = 0 (all grass eaten) the function still queues a full 55-rabbit / 20-deer refill because the +98 credit is a hard-coded estimate that no longer measures the resource it is compared against.
confirmed.fix: Recount grass after the spawnGrassPatch calls (e.g. const grassAfter = computeWildlifeCounts(state.entities).grass) and compare that real post-refill count to a threshold expressed against MIN_GRASS.
confirmed.verification: Verified: needsGrass is `grassCount < 65` and totalAvailableGrass is `grassCount + 98` when grass was just replenished, so sufficientGrass (`total >= 45`, line 405) is >= 98 in that branch and >= 65 otherwise — always true. The 'prey dependent on grass' gate in needsRabbits/needsDeer (408-409) is therefore dead and only the `rabbits < 4` / `deer < 2` fallbacks can trigger. Minimal fix: delete the gate or derive it from a real post-replenishment grass count.

confirmed.title: Storm damage heals any building that is already below the 20 HP floor and hides it from the storm damage report
confirmed.impact: Every other damage branch tests the stored radius (`dx*dx+dy*dy < radiusSq`: fire line 212, flood 232, tornado 245, plague 267), and the storm owner explicitly skips incomplete and rival buildings (line 116). The earthquake applies 15*resistMult damage to all buildings regardless of distance, completion or faction, so the x/y/radius pushed at lines 181-188 for the quake has no effect and a 'quake' anywhere damages distant rival structures.
confirmed.fix: Skip buildings outside the radius and non-player/incomplete ones the way the storm path does, e.g. compute dx/dy and `if (dx*dx + dy*dy >= radiusSq) continue;` (plus `if (!b.completed || b.faction === 'rival') continue;`) before applying damage.
confirmed.verification: Verified in applyStormDamageToBuildings: `b.health = Math.max(20, before - dmg)` (119) raises a building already below 20 HP, and buildings do sit there — raids floor at 5 (frontierCombat.ts:510) and fire/earthquake at 10 (worldEvents.ts:214, 258) — after which `b.health < before` (120) is false so the building is omitted from `damaged` and gets no 'Storm damage!' float and no notification (133-159). The existing test only pins 25 -> 20 (weatherConsequences.test.ts:66-70). Minimal fix: compute `b.health = Math.min(before, Math.max(20, before - dmg))`.

confirmed.title: Recurring world events reuse one constant GameEvent id, so dismissing one banner suppresses that event type for the rest of the save
confirmed.evidence: line 419 `id: `visitor_${kind}`,`; line 496 `id: 'rival_settlement',`; line 1721 `event: { id: 'wolf_migration', title: 'Wolf Pack Migration', ... }`
confirmed.impact: dismissActiveEvent permanently records event.id in world.dismissedActiveEventIds (useTransientGameFeedback.ts:277-279), and both the banner render (line 326 `!hiddenActiveEventIds.has(world.activeEvent.id)`) and the worker delta (simDelta.ts:462-464 preserveActiveEventDismissal) hide any later activeEvent carrying that id. Concrete: dismiss the year-0 first-week pilgrim banner (id `visitor_pilgrims`, line 419) and every later `pilgrim_caravan` yearly event — and every later first-week performer/pilgrim arrival after a save/load — never shows its banner again in that save, because the id is the same. The event still happens (groups spawn, toast still fires via addNotification), so the loss is silent: the player sees the effect with no banner explaining it.
confirmed.fix: Make the id instance-unique, e.g. line 419 `id: `visitor_${kind}_${state.tick}``, line 496 `id: `rival_settlement_${state.tick}``, and each rollYearlyWorldEvent case `event: { id: `wolf_migration_${state.tick}`, ... }`; keep the `visitor_` prefix (the hook's startsWith check at useTransientGameFeedback.ts:255 still works) and prune ids that are no longer in use from dismissedActiveEventIds, which stays bounded today only because ids repeat.
confirmed.verification: Verified: recurring events return constant ids (`visitor_${kind}` at 419, 'rival_settlement' at 496, and one constant per rollYearlyWorldEvent case at 1721-1796), while dismissActiveEvent permanently records that id in session.dismissedActiveEventIds (useTransientGameFeedback.ts:276-291; persisted per saveSchema.ts:22 and reseeded on load at line 312) and preserveActiveEventDismissal (simBuffers/simDelta.ts:29-36, applied at 462-465) plus the banner memo (useTransientGameFeedback.ts:325-330) hide any later activeEvent carrying that id. So dismissing the year-0 pilgrim banner suppresses all later pilgrim-caravan banners in that save even though the group still spawns and the toast still fires. Minimal fix: make ids instance-unique (e.g. `visitor_${kind}_${state.tick}`) and prune stale entries.

confirmed.title: Rival-owned watchtowers count as player early-warning towers and reveal their own raiders
confirmed.verification: Verified: detectRaidersFromWatchtowers filters only `b.completed && b.type === Watchtower` (15), unlike countCompletedDefenseBuildings which excludes `faction === 'rival'` (defenseStructures.ts:54-56), and rival camps do build completed faction-'rival' Watchtowers (createRivalBuilding, groupEvents.ts:308-324; picked for competitive/tense camps in rivalEvents.ts:107-114) in slots within ~90px of their own camp (rivalEvents.ts:35-44). The daily scan (dailyWorldEvents.ts:134) therefore clears hiddenFromPlayer and sets detectedByPatrol for the camp's own marching war-band (36-41), which entityCache.ts:86 renders and humanTick.ts:472 keeps sticky, giving free player early warning while the test only uses a faction-less tower. Minimal fix: add `&& b.faction !== 'rival'`.

confirmed.title: tickMoonHowlerCycle's injectable rng is not forwarded to the church rite or the flavour picks
confirmed.evidence:
moonHowler.ts:1044  `  const dawnCures = tryMoonHowlerChurchCures(state, aliveEntities, buildings, colonyDay, hourOfDay, entityById);`
(compared with moonHowler.ts:952 `  rng: () => number = Math.random,` and moonHowler.ts:642 `  rng: () => number = Math.random,`)
confirmed.impact: tickMoonHowlerCycle accepts an injected `rng` but only uses it for the replacement roll (line 1016). The rite path opened here falls back to the default Math.random for the weighted cure/kill/flee roll (line 743), the per-guard save rolls (line 780), the flee-position jitter (line 827) and the four WEREWOLF_*_LINES picks (lines 990, 1030, 1034, 1048). A caller that injects a deterministic stream to make a full-moon cycle reproducible (the seam documented in SIMULATION_AUTHORITY §11 step 4 and in CHANGELOG.md:626-628, and used by tests/moonHowler.rare.test.ts:164-213) cannot control whether the priest is cured or killed, so the 'deterministic full moon' guarantee only covers the replacement roll.
confirmed.fix: Forward the stream: `const dawnCures = tryMoonHowlerChurchCures(state, aliveEntities, buildings, colonyDay, hourOfDay, entityById, rng);` and replace the `Math.random()` line picks at 990/1030/1034/1048 with `rng()`.
confirmed.verification: Verified: tickMoonHowlerCycle accepts `rng` (952) but uses it only for the replacement roll (1016/1018); tryMoonHowlerChurchCures is called without it (1044) even though that function is fully injectable internally (its rng is used at 743, 752, 780, 797, 827), and the WEREWOLF_* line picks use Math.random directly (990, 1030, 1034, 1048). The existing rare-cycle tests pass `[]` buildings so the cure path never runs, and the production caller (tickLayerRealtime.ts:97) passes no rng, so the only impact is the documented deterministic-test seam (SIMULATION_AUTHORITY section 11 step 4). Minimal fix: forward `rng` to tryMoonHowlerChurchCures and use it for the line picks.

confirmed.lines: 1012-1020 | 891-900 (with 902-905 as the only place that schedules an election; caller src/game/dailyWorldEvents.ts:230)
confirmed.title: Load reconciliation schedules a vacancy election but leaves a dead villageLeaderId in place
confirmed.impact: When the leader dies (or is otherwise non-acting) and every remaining adult is ineligible (e.g. the only other adult is serving a scandal sentence, or only juveniles remain - isEligibleForLeadership requires alive/Human/player/adult/not imprisoned), this branch nulls villageLeaderId and returns WITHOUT setting pendingElectionYear. Every later daily call then returns at the `leaderId == null` guard, so the vacancy-election schedule is never re-established even after settlers grow up or are released from prison: the colony has no head, no 'leadership vacancy' notice (focusHints.ts:109 and getElectionCeremonyStatus both require pendingElectionYear != null), and only reaches a leader again at the next even-year term election (tryStartTermElectionCeremony requires year % 2 === 0) - up to 2 game years with no election, while the leader invariant check (simulationInvariants.ts:271) is silently skipped because villageLeaderId is null. tickLeaderVacancy is also the only scheduler of pendingElectionYear besides save-load (validateVillageLeaderOnLoad:1019), so this state survives until the player reloads.
confirmed.fix: Schedule the vacancy election in this branch instead of only clearing the office, i.e. replace the early `return null` with the same `state.pendingElectionYear = state.year + (state.dayInYear ?? 0) / DAYS_PER_YEAR + VACANCY_ELECTION_DELAY_YEARS` write used below (keeping the office cleared and logging the vacancy), or re-arm when `state.villageLeaderId == null && state.pendingElectionYear == null && state.lastElectionYear !== 0`.
confirmed.verification: Verified in validateVillageLeaderOnLoad: when getVillageLeader returns null it schedules pendingElectionYear (1018-1019) without clearing state.villageLeaderId, unlike the daily owner tickLeaderVacancy which nulls it (905) — and tickLeaderVacancy returns early while pendingElectionYear != null (889), so the stale id survives the whole vacancy. collectSimulationInvariantErrors then flags it every dev daily pulse (simulationInvariants.ts:271-276, asserted as a genuine error case in tests/simulation.invariants.test.ts:298), and raw readers compare against it (workforce.ts:683). Minimal fix: set `state.villageLeaderId = null;` immediately before scheduling the election.

confirmed.title: selectRivalDailyAction offers 'fortify' at 8 wood while applyRivalDailyAction requires 12, so a shelter-priority rival silently wastes its action day
confirmed.evidence: 74: `if (profile.priority === 'shelter' && ledger.wood >= 8) return 'fortify';` versus 105: `if (ledger.wood < 12) return { changed: false, summary: 'not enough wood to fortify' };` (the comparable security branch at 71 correctly requires wood >= 12).
confirmed.impact: A shelter-priority rival holding 8-11 wood selects 'fortify' every action day — the branch is evaluated before the 'gather' fallback at 75 — applyRivalDailyAction then refuses it without mutating any ledger value, and rivalEvents.ts:233 records `profile.lastAction = 'none'`. Because nothing is ever spent or gathered the ledger stays in the 8-11 window, so that rival's economy stops permanently: no gathers, no recovery, no trades, and the UI reports 'Quiet at camp' (rivalPresence.ts:23/34) forever.
confirmed.fix: Match the select threshold to the cost: `if (profile.priority === 'shelter' && ledger.wood >= 12) return 'fortify';`, mirroring the security branch on line 71.
confirmed.verification: Verified: selectRivalDailyAction returns 'fortify' for the 'shelter' priority whenever `ledger.wood >= 8` (74), while applyRivalDailyAction's fortify case requires wood >= 12 (105); every other branch matches its applier. In rivalEvents.ts:227-237 daysUntilAction is reset to 45-89 before the action is applied, so with wood in [8,12) the failed action sets lastAction='none', logs nothing, and the rival loses that action day. Minimal fix: raise the selection threshold to 12 (or lower the fortify cost to 8 consistently).

confirmed.title: Prep backup shallow-clones entities, so nested fields survive a failed-command rollback
confirmed.evidence: L102-103: `// Clone entity objects shallowly to decouple from in-place property mutations` / `entities: (state.entities ?? []).map((e) => ({ ...e })),`
confirmed.impact: The backup shares every nested object with the live world, so in-place nested mutations are not rolled back: `ensureEntitySkills(human)[job] = ...` (workforce.ts:211 and 264, skills.ts:37, apprenticeships.ts:95) mutates the shared `skills` map, `parent.childrenIds.push(childId)` (humanLifecycle.ts:40) the shared array, and moon-howler save/restore rewrites the shared `moonHowlerSaved`. gameWorker.ts:222-233 then rolls back via `applySimPrep` and answers `commandResult ok:false` with `safeExtractCommandDelta`, so the surviving mutations are shipped to the main thread as authoritative. The same O(entities) backup is also taken on every tick (gameWorker.ts:314) even though a tick error always ends the worker session (GameLoop.fallbackFromWorker), so the tick-path backup never changes the outcome.
confirmed.fix: Also copy the mutable nested fields in the entity clone, e.g. `({ ...e, skills: e.skills ? { ...e.skills } : e.skills, childrenIds: e.childrenIds ? [...e.childrenIds] : e.childrenIds, moonHowlerSaved: e.moonHowlerSaved ? { ...e.moonHowlerSaved } : e.moonHowlerSaved })`.
confirmed.verification: Verified the code fact: extractSimPrep maps entities with `{ ...e }` (103) and only deep-copies buildings' occupants/hotelGuestIds (106-110), so nested entity objects (skills, childrenIds, moonHowlerSaved) are shared, and the cited in-place writers exist (ensureEntitySkills in skills.ts:36-37, childrenIds pushes in humanLifecycle). The described harm is not demonstrated, though: every command that reaches those helpers deep-clones the world first via structuredClone (e.g. buildingStaffingActions.ts:119/216, settlerInteractionActions.ts:69), the in-place routed commands touch only top-level state (guidedCampaign.ts:109-130, visitorQuest.ts:53-64), and a tick error discards the worker entirely (gameWorker.ts:355-356 -> GameLoop.fallbackFromWorker, gameLoop.ts:348-351, 385-404), so the per-tick backup at gameWorker.ts:314 is indeed wasted work. Minimal fix for robustness: copy the mutable nested fields in the clone, or drop the tick-path backup.

confirmed.title: `avoidTreeId` retry loop can never run (no caller supplies it) and, if wired, its stride can be a no-op
confirmed.evidence: L288-293: `if (avoidTreeId && usePool.length > 1) { for (let attempt = 0; attempt < usePool.length && tree.id === avoidTreeId; attempt++) { index = (index + 5 + entityId) % usePool.length; tree = usePool[index]!; } }` — the only producer of `ChatPickOptions` is `chatHintsFromWorld` (humanChat.ts:94-101), which returns only `{ season, weather, festivalActive, foodLow }`, so `options.avoidTreeId` is always `undefined` at both pass-through sites (humanChat.ts:354, 391).
confirmed.impact: The repetition-avoidance feature is inert dead code: an entity whose formula picks the same tree twice in a row (same `entityId`/pool) repeats the line, and the guard's name/parameter promises otherwise. Separately, if the field were ever populated, the stride `5 + entityId` is `0 mod usePool.length` whenever `pool.length` divides `5 + entityId`, so all `usePool.length` attempts land on the avoided tree and the loop returns it anyway (bounded, but a silent no-op).
confirmed.fix: Either delete the parameter and block, or make progress guaranteed: `index = (index + 1) % usePool.length;` inside the loop (and set `avoidTreeId` at a call site if repetition avoidance is actually wanted).
confirmed.verification: Verified: the avoidTreeId parameter (263) and retry block (288-293) are inert because the only producer of ChatPickOptions, chatHintsFromWorld (humanChat.ts:94-101), returns just season/weather/festivalActive/foodLow, and the two pass-through call sites (humanChat.ts:354, 391) forward an always-undefined field; grep finds no other assignment. The stride `(index + 5 + entityId) % usePool.length` is also a no-op whenever the pool length divides 5 + entityId, so a wired feature could still return the avoided tree. Minimal fix: delete the parameter/block, or advance by 1 per attempt and set avoidTreeId at a call site.

confirmed.title: LifetimeStats.totalHumansDied counts dead entities in state.entities, which never contains dead entities
confirmed.evidence:
stats.ts:104 `humans: entities.filter(e => e.type === ET.Human && !e.alive && e.age > 0).length - (prevYearStats?.deaths.humans || 0),`
stats.ts:107 `).length - (prevYearStats?.deaths.animals || 0),`
stats.ts:132 `s.totalHumansDied = state.entities.filter(e => e.type === ET.Human && !e.alive).length;`
gameTick.ts:206-208 `const allAlive: Entity[] = [];` / `for (const e of aliveEntities) {` / `if (e.alive) allAlive.push(e);` then gameTick.ts:234 `state.entities = allAlive;`
confirmed.impact: gameTick rebuilds `state.entities` from alive entities only, so by the time `recordYearlyStats` runs at the year-rollover tick (gameTick.ts:83) the world array contains no `!alive` entity. `YearlyStats.deaths.humans`/`deaths.animals` are therefore always 0 and `lifetimeStats.totalHumansDied` is always 0, which is what StatisticsPanel.tsx:43 renders as "Humans Died" — the lifetime records panel reports 0 deaths forever. (Line 104 also subtracts the previous year's *delta* from a cumulative-looking count; both sides are 0 today, so the unit mismatch is currently masked.) The same alive-only snapshot makes `births.humans` (line 70) miss any child who died in its birth year.
confirmed.fix: Record deaths where they happen: increment a persistent counter at the death owner (e.g. in killHuman / the animal death helper) and derive both the per-year value and `totalHumansDied` from that counter (deltas), instead of scanning `state.entities` for `!e.alive`; e.g. in `updateLifetimeStats` replace line 132 with `s.totalHumansDied += latestYear?.deaths.humans ?? 0;` once the yearly value comes from the counter.
confirmed.verification: updateLifetimeStats (stats.ts:128-132) does filter `!e.alive`, but state.entities never holds dead entities: gameTick.ts:234 rewrites it to `allAlive` every tick, and the display copy is rebuilt the same way in simDelta.ts:498 (`world.entities = deltaClone(delta.aliveEntities)`, with the explicit garbage-collection note at 495-497). The call sits at gameTick.ts:86, i.e. before any death in that tick, so the count is always 0 and StatisticsPanel.tsx:43 shows "Humans Died" 0 forever. Minimal fix: keep a monotonic counter written by the death owner (e.g. increment alongside killHuman/humanLifecycleCleanup.ts) instead of re-deriving it; note recordYearlyStats' deaths.humans (stats.ts:104) makes the same dead-entity assumption and is also broken, so fix both together.

confirmed.title: clampToMapBounds lets NaN positions through unclamped
confirmed.verification: The code fact is exact: mapBounds.ts:17-20 uses only `< 0` / `> width` comparisons, which are false for NaN, and it is the last statement of both position-advancing paths (humanTick.ts:1467-1470, tickLayerSystems.ts:679). But no NaN producer exists in the repo (every `dx/dist` site I checked guards the divisor), so the described failure is latent; additionally simInvariants.ts:20 already detects non-finite positions and logs them, so this is a hardening gap in the last line of defence rather than a live defect. A minimal cheap guard (`if (!Number.isFinite(entity.x)) entity.x = 0;`) is still worthwhile.

confirmed.title: An escaped prisoner is never removed from prison.occupants and keeps prisonSentenceCrime
confirmed.evidence: L60-61: "escapee.prisonBuildingId = undefined;\n      escapee.prisonerUntilTick = undefined;" — no `prison.occupants` update and no `escapee.prisonSentenceCrime = undefined`, unlike the other release paths (workforce.releasePrisoners L670-677; buildingMaintenanceActions.ts L171-174).
confirmed.impact: tickPrisonGuardDuty runs from tickDailyWorldEvents.ts:129, after tickDailyBuildingEconomy's assignMissingWorkers has just rebuilt `prison.occupants` to include the escapee; nothing re-syncs afterwards in that tick, so the dev invariant pulse (gameTick.ts:277-286) reports "human N in prison #P is neither prisoner (prisonBuildingId) nor guard (homeBuildingId)" (simulationInvariants.ts:141-145). The Prison panel keeps listing the free settler as a prisoner until the next assign pulse (≤18 ticks), and `prisonSentenceCrime: 'scandal'` is carried in the save forever, unlike every other release path that clears it.
confirmed.fix: After L61 add: `prison.occupants = prison.occupants.filter((id) => id !== escapee.id);` and `escapee.prisonSentenceCrime = undefined;`
confirmed.verification: The escape branch (prisonGuardDuty.ts:60-61) really does clear only prisonBuildingId/prisonerUntilTick while the sibling release path (workforce.ts:670-677) also filters prison.occupants and clears prisonSentenceCrime, so the escape site is asymmetric. However "never removed" is wrong: syncJobBuildingOccupants (workforce.ts:301-311) rebuilds prison.occupants from scratch on every assign pulse (tickLayerAssign.ts:37, LAYER_ASSIGN_INTERVAL=18), so the stale id self-heals within 18 ticks and saveLoad.ts:487 repairs it on load; the invariant warning at the escape tick (gameTick.ts:282, dev builds only) is transient, and the stale prisonSentenceCrime is only ever read when prisonBuildingId != null (humanRelationships.ts:1180-1183), so it has no effect. Minimal fix: mirror the release path — drop the id from prison.occupants and clear prisonSentenceCrime at prisonGuardDuty.ts:60-61.

confirmed.title: removeStaffWorkerFromBuilding never validates that the human belongs to the building
confirmed.evidence:
L322-330: "return building.occupants.length < cap && state.entities.some(
      (entity) =>
        isPlayerHuman(entity)
        && entity.alive
        && !entity.isJuvenile
        && !entity.pregnant
        && !building.occupants.includes(entity.id)
        && !isOnConstructionCrew(state, entity.id, building.id),
    );" — the mutation path it gates requires `!hasWorkAssignment(entity)` (L92) and the shared predicate L58-68 does too.
confirmed.impact: In a village where every adult already holds a job, canAssignWorkerToBuilding returns true for an unfinished building, so App.tsx:1790 enables the "+ Fill builders" button (SelectedBuildingPanel.tsx:673); clicking sends `assignWorker` (App.tsx:1754) into _applyBuilderAssignmentMut, which finds no builder (`!hasWorkAssignment`), assigns nobody and floats "No idle settlers!" (L97-100). The player is offered an action that can never succeed. The same function is the auto-play bot's eligibility test (virtualPlayer.ts:373).
confirmed.fix: Add `&& !hasWorkAssignment(entity)` to the builder-branch filter (L324-329) so it mirrors _applyBuilderAssignmentMut and isEligibleIdleWorker.
confirmed.verification: removeStaffWorkerFromBuilding (buildingStaffingActions.ts:285-290) only checks existence and residence-role, then calls removeWorkerTransition(human, state.buildings), which strips that human's id from every building's occupants list (workforce.ts:219-229) — it never consults `building` or `human.homeBuildingId`, unlike the residence counterpart (buildingResidencyActions.ts:82) and unlike assignWorkerTransition's homeBuildingId guard (workforce.ts:203); the worker validator only checks shape (simWorker/commands.ts:227-228, not 231 as cited). Both real callers pass an id that belonged to the building (App.tsx:1761, virtualPlayer.ts:970), so a mismatch needs a stale display copy, and the freed settler is still the one the player named, which keeps the impact minor. Minimal fix: `if (human.homeBuildingId !== buildingId && !building.occupants.includes(humanId)) return state;` before mutating.

confirmed.title: Exported UNBUILDABLE_TERRAIN is a second, unread copy of a rule that lives in placementUtils (and a third in terrainGen)
confirmed.evidence: lines 25-32 `export const UNBUILDABLE_TERRAIN = new Set<TerrainType>([...])` plus line 34 `export { isFootprintOnBuildableTerrain, isFootprintWithinMapBounds } from './placementUtils';`; the same set is defined privately at placementUtils.ts:10-17 (used by `isUnbuildableTerrainType`, line 25) and a third time at terrainGen.ts:113. Nothing imports the exported set — the only other references are the pass-through re-exports in buildingActions.ts:19 and gameEngine.ts:245.
confirmed.impact: The authoritative terrain rule lives in placementUtils (`UNBUILDABLE_TERRAIN` + `isUnbuildableTerrainType`), so a new unbuildable terrain type added there will not affect this file's copy or terrainGen's, and the public façade advertises a stale second source of truth for placement legality. Any future caller that imports `UNBUILDABLE_TERRAIN` from buildingActions/gameEngine gets one of the copies rather than the owner's predicate.
confirmed.fix: Delete lines 25-32 and the `UNBUILDABLE_TERRAIN` entry in the buildingActions/gameEngine re-export lists, and import `isUnbuildableTerrainType` from placementUtils where a membership test is needed.
confirmed.verification: buildingPlacementActions.ts:25-32 defines and exports the set; a workspace-wide search finds only the re-exports at buildingActions.ts:19 and gameEngine.ts:245 and no reader, while the live rule is placementUtils.ts:10-27 (used at 112/114 and by renderer/grid.ts:173 via isUnbuildableTerrainType) and terrainGen.ts:113 is a third copy. The impact statement is accurate — editing the exported set changes nothing — so this is a duplicated-source-of-truth/dead-export defect, not a runtime bug. Minimal fix: delete the literal and re-export isUnbuildableTerrainType from placementUtils for external callers.

confirmed.title: Unused grid API: forEachNeighborCell, ensurePresent, hasEntity, distSq, buildGrassGrid, buildMobileGrid
confirmed.evidence: 340: `forEachNeighborCell(` / 191: `ensurePresent(entity: Entity): void {` / 227: `hasEntity(id: number): boolean {` / 70: `export function distSq(ax: number, ay: number, bx: number, by: number): number {` / 465: `export function buildGrassGrid(` / 795: `export function buildMobileGrid(` — a repo-wide search (src, tests, scripts) finds no call site for any of them.
confirmed.impact: A 30-line 3x3 neighbourhood walker plus two index helpers and two grid builders are carried as if they were part of the public grid contract but are never exercised, so they can silently drift from the invariants the grid enforces — forEachNeighborCell already disagrees with cellCoords (123-128): it returns false for out-of-map coordinates instead of clamping, so a caller written against cellCoords' semantics would get 'no neighbours' at map edges. The project's own CHANGELOG records removing exactly this class of dead spatial alias (forEachEntityInRadius, generateHumanSprites).
confirmed.fix: Delete the six unused members (or, if forEachNeighborCell is intended as public API, add a focused grid test that pins its edge behaviour).
confirmed.verification: A repo-wide search (src, tests, scripts) finds exactly one occurrence of each name — its own declaration — for distSq (spatialGrid.ts:70), ensurePresent (191), hasEntity (227), forEachNeighborCell (340) and the two builders buildGrassGrid (465) / buildMobileGrid (795); the other `distSq` hits are unrelated locals. The semantic drift claim also holds: forEachNeighborCell returns false for out-of-range coordinates (spatialGrid.ts:347-349) while cellCoords clamps (123-128), so the two public walkers disagree at map edges. This is real dead code (maintainability only, zero simulation impact), so the minimal fix is deletion or a focused test pinning edge behaviour.

confirmed.title: Two conflicting juvenile thresholds: the factory halves `size` below age 16 while dayCycle immediately recomputes isJuvenile at age 12
confirmed.evidence: entityFactory.ts:66 `isJuvenile ?? (isHuman && opts?.ageYears !== undefined ? opts.ageYears < HUMAN_ADULT_MIN_AGE : false);` with `HUMAN_ADULT_MIN_AGE = 16` (dayCycleConstants.ts:12), used at entityFactory.ts:110 `size: effectiveJuvenile ? config.size * 0.5 : config.size,`; but the same function then calls entityFactory.ts:159 `setHumanBirthFromAge(entity, opts.ageYears, opts.colonyDay ?? 0);`, which recomputes the flag with a different threshold — dayCycle.ts:212 `entity.isJuvenile = entity.age < HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS;` (HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS = 12, dayCycle.ts:126), and `syncHumanAgeFromCalendar` (dayCycle.ts:246) uses 12 as well.
confirmed.impact: For any caller that passes `ageYears` without an explicit `isJuvenile` (the exported factory API and the branch the code was written for), an entity aged 12–15 is created with `isJuvenile === false` but `size === config.size * 0.5`; `tryGraduateHumanChild` (dayCycle.ts:135 `if (!entity.isJuvenile || entity.age < HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS) return false;`) then refuses to promote it, so the settler renders at half size for life while every age-gated rule treats them as an adult. Today's in-repo callers all pass `isJuvenile` explicitly (worldGen.ts:499/510/539/770/781, groupEvents.ts:284, settlerInteractionActions.ts:91) so the path is latent, not live.
confirmed.fix: Use the dayCycle owner's threshold for the auto-detect branch (`opts.ageYears < HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS`) so `size` and `isJuvenile` agree after `setHumanBirthFromAge`, or drop the auto-detect branch and require the caller's `isJuvenile` argument.
confirmed.verification: createEntity computes effectiveJuvenile with HUMAN_ADULT_MIN_AGE=16 (entityFactory.ts:66) and halves size from it (line 110), then calls setHumanBirthFromAge (line 159), which overwrites entity.isJuvenile with `age < HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS` (=12, dayCycle.ts:212), so an ageYears 12-15 entity created without an explicit isJuvenile ends half-sized and non-juvenile, and tryGraduateHumanChild (dayCycle.ts:135) would never promote it. Every in-repo caller passes isJuvenile=false plus an age >= 16 (worldGen.ts:499/510/539/770/781, groupEvents.ts:278-285, settlerInteractionActions.ts:85-92), so it is latent, as the finding itself notes. Minimal fix: use the dayCycle owner's threshold in the auto-detect branch (`opts.ageYears < HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS`).

confirmed.title: A pregnant prisoner's pregnancy is frozen: the prisoner branch `continue`s before the pregnancy-progress gate, so the term is extended by the whole sentence
confirmed.evidence: humanTick.ts:388-403 `if (isPrisoner) { ... syncEntityGrids(ctx, entity); continue; }` exits the iteration before humanTick.ts:794-801 `if (isPlayerHuman(entity) && entity.gender === 'female' && entity.pregnant && !conceivedToday && entity.pregnancyProgress !== undefined) { tickPregnancyAndBirth(state, ctx, entity, { livingHumanAt }); }`. Pregnancy can coexist with imprisonment: arrest happens in exposeAffair -> arrestForScandal (humanRelationships.ts:1149-1152, 1203) and the daily gossip path only excludes a pregnancy fathered by the lover (humanRelationships.ts:313-318 `if ((entity.pregnant && entity.pregnantById === lover.id) || ...) return;`), so a married woman pregnant by her husband can be arrested as 'caught'.
confirmed.impact: While imprisoned, `pregnancyProgress` never advances (and the mother also takes no energy loss and no meal), so the term silently stretches by the 2.5-6 day sentence; if a save is taken during that window the progress field and the birth date the player sees diverge from the declared 24-day pregnancy. Any invariant/test that expects a pregnancy to advance every tick while `entity.pregnant` holds is violated for this edge case.
confirmed.fix: Move the pregnancy gate above the prisoner branch (or run it for prisoners before `continue`), i.e. advance existing pregnancy for imprisoned pregnant settlers while still skipping movement/needs.
confirmed.verification: The prisoner branch ends in `continue` (humanTick.ts:401-402), which skips the only tickPregnancyAndBirth call site (humanTick.ts:794-801), so pregnancyProgress stops advancing while imprisoned (it is also the only caller — humanLifecycle.ts:54 is otherwise uncalled from the sim). Pregnancy and imprisonment can coexist: arrestForScandal (humanRelationships.ts:1164-1205) needs only a married offender and a staffed prison, and tryDailyAffairGossip skips only a pregnancy fathered by the lover (humanRelationships.ts:313-318). Impact is limited (progress resumes on release, invariants still hold because pregnancyDueProgress stays valid), so low. Minimal fix: hoist the pregnancy gate above the prisoner branch and run it before `continue`.

confirmed.title: steerVisitorToHotel moves a pathing visitor twice per tick
confirmed.evidence: 234: `visitor.x += visitor.vx;` / 235: `visitor.y += visitor.vy;` immediately after the steerWithPath call whose documented contract (pathfinding.ts:298) is "'path': entity was moved along waypoints (caller must not move it again)"
confirmed.impact: On the branch this call exists for (camp-to-hotel walk crossing water/mountain), `steerWithPath` already applies `entity.x += entity.vx; entity.y += entity.vy` (pathfinding.ts:343-344) and then the visitor is advanced a second time by the same velocity, so lodging visitors travel at double the intended 0.7x speed and skip waypoint checks; the 'direct' branch below sets velocity itself and moves once, so the two branches have inconsistent movement semantics. humanMovement.ts:150 handles the same return value correctly (returns false without moving).
confirmed.fix: On `handled === 'path'` just `return true;` — delete lines 234-235 so the movement already performed by steerWithPath is the only one.
confirmed.verification: steerWithPath documents "'path': entity was moved along waypoints (caller must not move it again)" (pathfinding.ts:298) and really does apply `entity.x += entity.vx` before returning 'path' (pathfinding.ts:341-346); hotelStay.ts:233-236 then adds vx/vy a second time, while humanMovement.ts:142-150 handles the same return value correctly. The defect is real but cosmetic — hotel-bound visitors cover ~1.4x their intended speed and can step past waypoints; there is no state corruption. Minimal fix: on `handled === 'path'` just `return true;` and delete lines 234-235.

confirmed.title: isValidHuntingSpotPrey uses `in`, so Object.prototype keys validate as prey ids
confirmed.evidence:
huntingSpots.ts:34:
  return typeof value === 'string' && value in PREY_OPTIONS_MAP;
confirmed.impact: PREY_OPTIONS_MAP is a plain object literal, so `'toString' in PREY_OPTIONS_MAP`, `'constructor' in ...` and `'__proto__' in ...` are all true. The worker command boundary uses this as its only guard (simWorker/commands.ts:237 `return isFiniteNumber(cmd.buildingId) && isValidHuntingSpotPrey(cmd.prey);`), so a crafted `setHuntingSpotPrey` command carrying `prey: 'toString'` is accepted and stored on the building via buildingConfigurationActions.ts:109; dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:380 then compares `building.huntingSpotPrey ?? 'auto'` against real prey types, so the post silently harvests nothing, and getHuntingSpotPreyOption('constructor') returns Object.prototype.constructor (UI reads `.label`/`.hint` as undefined).
confirmed.fix: Use an own-property check: `return typeof value === 'string' && Object.hasOwn(PREY_OPTIONS_MAP, value);` (or `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(PREY_OPTIONS_MAP, value)`).
confirmed.verification: huntingSpots.ts:34 is `typeof value === 'string' && value in PREY_OPTIONS_MAP`, and `in` walks the prototype chain, so 'toString'/'constructor' pass, and getHuntingSpotPreyOption would then return the inherited function (line 29's `??` does not catch it). It is the command-channel validator (simWorker/commands.ts:237) while the domain transition rejects the same value (buildingConfigurationActions.ts:99 against VALID_PREY_IDS, lines 15-17), so validation and execution disagree — but the command is simply discarded, hence low. Minimal fix: `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(PREY_OPTIONS_MAP, value)`.

confirmed.title: Town Hall daily pulse is fed from state.entities, so settlers who died earlier in the same tick are counted
confirmed.evidence: L767 `const villagers = state.entities.filter(isPlayerHuman);` L768 `tickTownHallCivic(state, building, villagers);` L769 `tickTownHallAudiences(state, building, villagers);` — `isPlayerHuman` (playerHuman.ts:12-17) does not test `alive`, and gameTick only prunes `state.entities` at the very end of the tick (gameTick.ts:234 `state.entities = allAlive;`), after the daily layer at gameTick.ts:220-222. The same function already has an alive-filtered list in scope: L292 `const playerWorkers = allAlive.filter(isPlayerHuman);`.
confirmed.impact: A settler killed earlier in the same tick (predator, illness, old age) is still a Human with `alive === false` in `state.entities` during the daily layer, so `tickTownHallCivic` counts them in `const adults = playerHumans.filter((h) => !h.isJuvenile).length;` (townHall.ts:88) and pays `adults * 0.4` extra tax gold for that pulse; the dead entity is also handed to `tickTownHallAudiences`. tickTownHallAudiences happens to re-filter `h.alive` (townHall.ts:352), so the visible damage is limited to the tax count, but the module mixes two different population sources in one function.
confirmed.fix: Pass the already-built alive-filtered list: `const villagers = playerWorkers;` (or `ctx.playerHumans`) at L767 instead of re-filtering `state.entities`.
confirmed.verification: The Town Hall pulse re-filters state.entities (dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:767), and isPlayerHuman (playerHuman.ts:12-17) does not test `alive`, while state.entities is only pruned at the very end of the tick (gameTick.ts:234) — so a settler killed in this tick's realtime/systems layers is still present when the daily layer runs (tickLayerDaily.ts:79). tickTownHallCivic counts such a settler in `adults` (townHall.ts:88-89), inflating that pulse's tax by a fraction of a gold piece; tickTownHallAudiences re-filters `h.alive` (townHall.ts:352), so nothing else is affected. Minimal fix: pass the already-built alive-filtered list (`playerWorkers`, dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:292) instead of re-filtering state.entities.

confirmed.title: getGrazerDailyDemand is exported but never called, so the winter penalty is never applied to grazing demand
confirmed.evidence: grassEcology.ts:91-94 `export function getGrazerDailyDemand(type: GrazerType, season: Season): number { const meta = GRAZER_METABOLISM[type]; const penalty = getWinterEnergyPenalty(season); return grazerGrassEnergyDemandPerDay(meta.energyLossPerTick, meta.grassEnergyGain, penalty); }` — while the only production consumer passes a literal 0: ecosystemPressure.ts:68 `grazerGrassEnergyDemandPerDay(GRAZER_METABOLISM.deer.energyLossPerTick, GRAZER_METABOLISM.deer.grassEnergyGain, 0) * deerCount`.
confirmed.impact: A repo-wide grep finds no caller of `getGrazerDailyDemand` (only its definition), so grazing demand is always computed with `winterPenalty = 0`. In winter the report understates demand by the winter term, the sole helper that encodes that term is dead, and the seasonal-penalty rule has no effective owner.
confirmed.fix: Either call `getGrazerDailyDemand('deer', state.season)` etc. from getGrazingPressureReport (passing the season through) or delete `getGrazerDailyDemand` and `GrazerType` so the winter-penalty rule has one owner.
confirmed.verification: getGrazerDailyDemand (grassEcology.ts:91-95) is the only helper that routes getWinterEnergyPenalty into grazing demand, and a repo-wide search finds no caller — its sole production consumer, getGrazingPressureReport, passes a literal 0 for the penalty at ecosystemPressure.ts:68-70. The consequence is a UI/report understatement of winter demand rather than a simulation change (the report is diagnostic), so this is a dead-helper / one-owner gap. Minimal fix: call getGrazerDailyDemand(type, state.season) from the report, or delete the helper and GrazerType so the rule has one owner.

confirmed.title: replenishDepletedWildlife final 'nothing happened' guard can never fire
confirmed.evidence: 457:  if (!wildlifeSpawned && !grassReplenished) return false;
confirmed.impact: Line 422 already returns when `!needsWildlife && !grassReplenished`, and every needsX block (427-455) sets wildlifeSpawned = true, so needsWildlife implies wildlifeSpawned and the condition at 457 is always false (unreachable return). The function therefore always reports true once line 422 passes, even if spawnWildlifeRing placed no animal at all — the boolean reads as 'a refill happened' when it only means 'a refill was attempted'. (No production caller consumes the return value today: dailyWorldEvents.ts:142 discards it, so this is a latent trap for the next caller.)
confirmed.fix: Remove the dead guard, or make the function return whether anything was actually placed (e.g. track spawns inside spawnWildlifeRing/spawnGrassPatch and return `placedCount > 0`).
confirmed.verification: Line 422 already returns when `!needsWildlife && !grassReplenished`, and each branch that feeds needsWildlife (needsRabbits/needsDeer/needsFoxes/needsWolves at worldGen.ts:408-418) sets `wildlifeSpawned = true` unconditionally (427-455), so the guard at 457 is unreachable — the function always reports true once line 422 passes, even if spawnWildlifeRing placed nothing. No production caller consumes the return value (dailyWorldEvents.ts:142 discards it), so impact is latent only. Minimal fix: delete the dead guard or track an actual placed count.

confirmed.title: Earthquake branch ignores the disaster's own x/y/radius and hits every building on the map
confirmed.impact: Every other damage branch tests the stored radius (`dx*dx+dy*dy < radiusSq`: fire line 212, flood 232, tornado 245, plague 267), and the storm owner explicitly skips incomplete and rival buildings (line 116). The earthquake applies 15*resistMult damage to all buildings regardless of distance, completion or faction, so the x/y/radius pushed at lines 181-188 for the quake has no effect and a 'quake' anywhere damages distant rival structures.
confirmed.fix: Skip buildings outside the radius and non-player/incomplete ones the way the storm path does, e.g. compute dx/dy and `if (dx*dx + dy*dy >= radiusSq) continue;` (plus `if (!b.completed || b.faction === 'rival') continue;`) before applying damage.
confirmed.verification: The earthquake branch (worldEvents.ts:253-259) loops all buildings and applies 15*resistMult damage with no distance, completion or faction test, unlike fire (212), flood (232) and plague (267) which compare against radiusSq from the disaster record pushed at 176-188, and unlike the storm owner which skips incomplete/rival buildings (116). Damage is floored at 10 HP so nothing is destroyed, but the pushed quake radius has no effect and distant rival/incomplete structures take damage, so the area filter looks omitted. Minimal fix: reuse the sibling pattern (`const dx = b.x - x; ...; if (dx*dx+dy*dy >= radiusSq) continue;` plus the completed/faction guard).

confirmed.title: counter_attack research effects stack across tiers, so the chance reaches 1.0 and a counter-attack can never fail
confirmed.impact: Whenever Iron Spears has been forged (or Iron Swords researched), both nodes are researched, so researchedEffect(...,'add') returns 0.45 + 0.55 = 1.0 and this function returns 1.0. rollCounterAttack (combat.ts:157-159) computes roll = (hash % 1000)/1000 in [0, 0.999] and returns roll < chance, so it is always true: in tickLayerSystems.ts:394-403 every predator contact (Wolf, Fox, and the cursed Moon Howler) kills the predator instead of the settler, making predator deaths of settlers impossible late game. The explicit 0.55 / 0.45 fallback on line 133 is unreachable. getPredatorBlockChance (117-122) accumulates the same way (0.35 + 0.6 + 0.72 = 1.67); its Math.min(0.85, chance) cap masks the sum and makes the tier Math.max chance,0.72/0.6/0.35 branches dead, so the applied block rate is the cap rather than the researched tier.
confirmed.fix: Treat these as tier effects, not additive stacks: resolve the highest researched tier (e.g. if (hasIronSwords(state)) return 0.55; if (hasIronSpears(state)) return 0.45;) and keep any researched-effect override capped, e.g. return Math.min(0.85, add). Re-check getPredatorBlockChance after the same change.
confirmed.verification: researchedEffect sums every same-target `add` (combat.ts:38-51), defense_4 carries `counter_attack add 0.45` and defense_8 `counter_attack add 0.55` with defense_4 as a prerequisite (gameTypes.ts:925 and 929), so getCounterAttackChance returns 1.0 once Iron Swords is researched; rollCounterAttack's roll is `(hash % 1000)/1000` in [0,0.999] (combat.ts:157-158), so it is always true and the pre-awarded branch in tickLayerSystems.ts:394-405 kills every predator on contact — wolf, fox and Moon Howler can no longer kill a settler late game, and the explicit 0.45/0.55 fallback at line 133 is unreachable. The same accumulation makes getPredatorBlockChance 0.95 (0.35+0.6, and 1.67 with scale mail), which is then clamped to 0.85 (combat.ts:117-122), so the per-tier Math.max values are dead too. Minimal fix: resolve the highest researched tier for counter_attack (and re-check predator_block), or cap the accumulated value.

confirmed.title: Injected rng is not forwarded to the church exorcism, so the cure outcome ignores it
confirmed.evidence:
moonHowler.ts:1044  `  const dawnCures = tryMoonHowlerChurchCures(state, aliveEntities, buildings, colonyDay, hourOfDay, entityById);`
(compared with moonHowler.ts:952 `  rng: () => number = Math.random,` and moonHowler.ts:642 `  rng: () => number = Math.random,`)
confirmed.impact: tickMoonHowlerCycle accepts an injected `rng` but only uses it for the replacement roll (line 1016). The rite path opened here falls back to the default Math.random for the weighted cure/kill/flee roll (line 743), the per-guard save rolls (line 780), the flee-position jitter (line 827) and the four WEREWOLF_*_LINES picks (lines 990, 1030, 1034, 1048). A caller that injects a deterministic stream to make a full-moon cycle reproducible (the seam documented in SIMULATION_AUTHORITY §11 step 4 and in CHANGELOG.md:626-628, and used by tests/moonHowler.rare.test.ts:164-213) cannot control whether the priest is cured or killed, so the 'deterministic full moon' guarantee only covers the replacement roll.
confirmed.fix: Forward the stream: `const dawnCures = tryMoonHowlerChurchCures(state, aliveEntities, buildings, colonyDay, hourOfDay, entityById, rng);` and replace the `Math.random()` line picks at 990/1030/1034/1048 with `rng()`.
confirmed.verification: tickMoonHowlerCycle forwards its rng only to shouldApplyNewMoonHowlerCurse (moonHowler.ts:1016) and calls tryMoonHowlerChurchCures without it (line 1044), so that function keeps its `rng = Math.random` default (line 642) for the rite roll (680-681, 743), the guard-save roll and the flee jitter; the announcement/flavour picks at 990, 1030, 1034 and 1048 also bypass the injected stream. The tests that rely on injection only cover the curse path (tests/moonHowler.rare.test.ts:158-219), so the module header's injectability claim and SIMULATION_AUTHORITY §11 step 4 are only half satisfied — a testability defect with no player-visible simulation effect (Math.random is the seeded global in the main-thread path). Minimal fix: pass `rng` at line 1044 and use `rng()` at 990/1030/1034/1048.

confirmed.title: The 0.25-year vacancy campaign is only evaluated on a year rollover, so the real delay is 0.25-1.25 years while the UI reports 3 months
confirmed.evidence:
const electionYear = currentFraction + VACANCY_ELECTION_DELAY_YEARS;
  state.pendingElectionYear = electionYear;   // ... while the only caller is: if (yearRollover) { const vacancyCeremony = tryStartVacancyElectionCeremony(state, state.year, state.dayInYear); }
confirmed.impact: tryStartVacancyElectionCeremony takes dayInYear and compares the full fractional date (`if (currentFraction < state.pendingElectionYear) return false;`), but its only caller sits inside `if (yearRollover)` in dailyWorldEvents.ts, so it is invoked with dayInYear === 0 once per year. A leader who dies on, say, day 20 of year 3 gets pendingElectionYear = 3.06, but the ceremony cannot start until tick 0 of year 4 (about a 0.95-year wait instead of the declared 3 months); the ceremony then never happens mid-year, so the effective delay is uniformly 0.25-1.25 years. getVillageCeremonyStatus/formatElectionDelay keep telling the player 'No village head - merit election in 3 months (Year 4)' and then 'Leadership election imminent - settlers will gather soon.' for up to nine more months, and focusHints reports '0.25 years'.
confirmed.fix: Call `tryStartVacancyElectionCeremony(state, state.year, state.dayInYear)` from the daily path unconditionally (next to `tickLeaderVacancy`, outside the yearRollover block) - the function is already idempotent (it bails on a null pendingElectionYear, an active ceremony, or a future date) - or change the schedule to a whole year boundary so the displayed delay matches the actual one.
confirmed.verification: tickLeaderVacancy stores `currentFraction + VACANCY_ELECTION_DELAY_YEARS` (=0.25, villageLeadership.ts:30, 902-904), but its sole scheduler is inside `if (yearRollover)` (dailyWorldEvents.ts:223-232), so tryStartVacancyElectionCeremony is only ever invoked with dayInYear === 0 while comparing the full fractional date (villageLeadership.ts:931-934) — a death on day 20 of year 3 waits until tick 0 of year 4, an effective delay of 0.25-1.25 years. Meanwhile the player is told "merit election in 3 months" (focusHints.ts:114, villageLeadership.ts:484) and the panel text promises a 3-month election (VillageLeadershipPanel.tsx:25). Minimal fix: call tryStartVacancyElectionCeremony unconditionally from the daily path (it already bails on a null pendingElectionYear, an active ceremony, or a future date).

confirmed.title: availableScripts reads the 40 OLDEST event-log entries instead of the 40 most recent
confirmed.evidence: 62: `const recent = state.eventLog.slice(-40);` with the local named `recent` and the module comment promising 'script selection from real history' (line 4). eventLog is newest-first: eventLog.ts:23 `state.eventLog.unshift({...})`, and simDelta.ts:236 takes `world.eventLog.slice(0, EVENT_LOG_DELTA_TAIL_MAX)` as the recent tail. `slice(-40)` therefore returns the last 40 entries of the array, i.e. the colony's oldest recorded events.
confirmed.impact: The theatre only becomes eligible at colony day 50-110 (MIN_DAY 50 + seeded window, line 23/54) by which time the 2000-entry log holds far more than 40 entries, so the offered plays (and the /foot/i famine detection at 75) are decided by the first days of the colony and freeze permanently — new disasters/combats/scandals can no longer unlock a script. If those oldest entries yield no script, the function returns at 89 without setting any flag and retries the same dead history every day, so the story never starts.
confirmed.fix: `const recent = state.eventLog.slice(0, 40);`
confirmed.verification: availableScripts uses `state.eventLog.slice(-40)` (travelingTheatre.ts:62) on an array that is newest-first — logEvent unshifts (eventLog.ts:23) and trims with pop (line 33) — so the slice returns the oldest surviving entries, which is also how simDelta.ts:236 defines the recent tail (`slice(0, EVENT_LOG_DELTA_TAIL_MAX)`). The script choice (and the /foot/i famine check at line 75) is therefore driven by early-colony history and drifts only as the 2000-entry cap pushes the oldest entries out, so recent disasters/combats/scandals cannot unlock a script. Minimal fix: `const recent = state.eventLog.slice(0, 40);`.

confirmed.title: Rollback snapshot shallow-copies object slices that the sim mutates in place, so applySimPrep cannot restore them
confirmed.evidence: simPrep.ts:102-103 `// Clone entity objects shallowly to decouple from in-place property mutations` / `entities: (state.entities ?? []).map((e) => ({ ...e })),` (the occupant array of buildings is explicitly isolated at line 108, but entity nested state is not)
confirmed.impact: Nested objects keep the same reference between the backup and the live world, so gameWorker.ts:228/360 `applySimPrep(world, prepBackup)` restores only top-level properties. In-place nested writers during ticks/commands include skills.ts:37 `skills[job] = ...`, humanLifecycle.ts:40 `parent.childrenIds.push(childId)`, relationships.ts:108 `a.friendships[friendKey(b.id)] = next`, groupEvents.ts:516 `group.daysLeft--`, rivalProfiles.ts:89 `ledger.food -= 5`, and renffrOmen.letters. If a tick or command throws after one of these (e.g. a birth is rolled back at entity level but the parent's `childrenIds` still lists the removed child), the authoritative worker world stays mutated although the tick/command is reported failed; the next delta ships the 'failed' change to the player, or a retry applies it twice.
confirmed.fix: Deep-copy the backed-up slices: `entities: structuredClone(state.entities ?? [])` (or clone the nested fields skills/childrenIds/friendships/feuds explicitly) and clone element objects of visitorGroups/rivalSettlements (e.g. `.map(g => ({...g}))`) in extractSimPrep.
confirmed.verification: The snapshot really does only copy the arrays for visitorGroups, rivalSettlements, tradeRoutes, the three pending*Event lists and disasters (simPrep.ts:141-150) while cloning entities/buildings per object, and the tick path mutates those elements in place (e.g. tickTradeCaravans, tradeCaravans.ts:240-256), so applySimPrep after a thrown tick or buffer exhaustion (gameWorker.ts:339/345/355) cannot restore them. The command-path half of the claim is wrong, however: the cited owners deep-clone before mutating (cloneWorldStateForAction = structuredClone, groupEvents.ts:204-206; establishTradeRoute, tradeCaravans.ts:158), so a throwing command discards its clone and leaks nothing, and the failure needs an exceptional error path. Minimal fix: structuredClone the element slices in extractSimPrep (and use `playerWorkers`-style alive lists where applicable).

confirmed.title: Legacy combat-kind fallback is applied to every chronicle line and classifies any message containing "raid" as a combat event
confirmed.evidence: L50: `const msg = evt.message.toLowerCase();`  L53: `if (msg.includes('raid')) {`  L60: `return 'incoming_raid';` — the function never checks `evt.type`, and its caller passes the whole log: villagePortrait.ts:83-90 `const eventLog = state.eventLog ?? []; ... const kind = resolveCombatLogKind(eventLog[i]); if (kind === 'outgoing_raid') outgoingRaids++; else if (kind === 'defense' || kind === 'repelled' || kind === 'incoming_raid') defenses++;`
confirmed.impact: `groupEvents.ts:818` (also 1110, 1125) logs `logEvent(state, 'event', 'Raid called off — truce with ' + rival.name, rival.name)` with no `combatKind`; the heuristic matches `'raid'`, fails the 'raid on the village'/' raid on ' tests and returns `'incoming_raid'`. Every peace treaty therefore increments `defenses` in villagePortrait, which both misreports the village's history and can silently delete the `+10` war-score bonus (`villagePortrait.ts:97 (defenses > 0 && outgoingRaids >= defenses ? 10 : 0)`), moving the portrait's war label across its 25/50 thresholds.
confirmed.fix: Add a type guard as the first line after the kind fast-path: `if (evt.type !== 'combat') return null;` (combat writers always pass a kind, so this only removes false positives).
confirmed.verification: resolveCombatLogKind falls through to the text heuristic whenever combatKind is absent (eventLog.ts:48-62), and villagePortrait.ts:84-92 runs it over the entire log; non-combat 'event' lines therefore get a kind — "Raid called off — truce with …" (groupEvents.ts:818) and "… led the raid against …" (frontierCombat.ts:487-492) both hit the final `return 'incoming_raid'` at line 60 — inflating `defenses` and suppressing the `outgoingRaids >= defenses ? 10 : 0` war term (villagePortrait.ts:94-99). summarizeCombatEvents is safe only because CombatLogPanel pre-filters to type 'combat' (CombatLogPanel.tsx:23-32). Minimal fix: gate the text fallback on `evt.type === 'combat'` (or fold it into a caller that already filters).

refuted.title: Stepping down a leader in cursed werewolf form leaves the Moon Howler snapshot saying 'leader', which restores a stale LEADER_OCCUPATION on revert
refuted.impact: transformToWerewolfForm snapshots `occupation` into human.moonHowlerSaved (moonHowler.ts:342) and leaves the live occupation as 'leader', so a sitting leader who loses an election or is replaced while in werewolf form is stepped down here only in live state. On the dawn revert, `were.occupation = saved?.occupation === LEADER_OCCUPATION ? LEADER_OCCUPATION : 'settler';` (moonHowler.ts:438) writes 'leader' back onto a settler who no longer holds villageLeaderId. Nothing repairs it: applyLeaderOccupation only ever steps down the id captured as `prevLeaderId` (null from now on), and workforce.ts:206/227/260 all preserve LEADER_OCCUPATION, so the ex-leader is permanently displayed as 💼 leader (SelectedEntityPanel.tsx:332, PopulationPanel.tsx:52) and prepareWorkforce (workforce.ts:464-481) permanently skips the stale-workplace repair for them. Reachable whenever a reveal lands inside a full-moon night (20:00-06:00, moonHowler.ts:219-226) for a cursed settler who is the incumbent.
refuted.fix: Clear the snapshot too when stepping down a transformed leader: `if (prev.moonHowlerSaved?.occupation === LEADER_OCCUPATION) prev.moonHowlerSaved.occupation = 'settler';` inside the existing step-down block.
refuted.verification: The code paths are as described (leaderHouse.ts:44-52 steps down only the live occupation, while transformToWerewolfForm snapshots it at moonHowler.ts:342 and revertToHumanForm restores LEADER_OCCUPATION at :438), but the trigger cannot occur. Both ceremony starts are inside the year-rollover daily block (dailyWorldEvents.ts:230-232) and I measured with real gameTick calls that the reveal fires exactly 4345 ticks later — tick 56185 in a run started at a year boundary, i.e. hour 8 (tickOfDay 25) — whereas shouldMoonHowlerTransform is true only during a full-moon night, 20:00-06:00 (moonHowler.ts:219-226, with syncMoonHowlerForms reverting at dawn), and isActingVillageHead deliberately keeps a transformed cursed leader in office (villageLeadership.ts:357-360) so no vacancy step-down happens at night either. Corrected severity low: the suggested one-line snapshot clear is harmless hardening, but no reachable state produces it today.

refuted.title: birthsCompletedThisInterval is recorded before the outcome branches, so stillbirths count as completed births
refuted.evidence: 90: `recordRelationshipDiagnostic('birthsCompletedThisInterval');` — recorded before the Wildkin branch (103-115, returns at 114) and before the stillborn branch (118-127, returns at 126)
refuted.impact: The diagnostics contract says this counter "increments only at a completed birth" (relationshipDiagnostics.ts:5-19 and the header of tests/relationshipDiagnostics.test.ts:10-12), and §5 requires diagnostics to distinguish completed births. A stillbirth creates no child and is logged as a death, yet it increments the birth counter; the same happens for a Wildkin birth. Per-day birth rates read high, and a run of stillbirths looks like live human births to anyone consuming the flush snapshot (Objective 8 truth rule). The existing test only covers the successful human-birth path, so nothing locks this in.
refuted.fix: Move the `recordRelationshipDiagnostic('birthsCompletedThisInterval')` call into the human-birth branch after line 129 (and decide explicitly whether a Wildkin counts as a completed birth rather than inheriting it by placement).
refuted.verification: The record call does sit in the shared delivery-recovery block (line 90, before the wildkin return at 114 and the stillborn return at 127), but that placement matches the counter's documented meaning: CHANGELOG.md:46 states the scope of the conception-labelling fix is the label only and that `birthsCompletedThisInterval` "always counted deliveries", and the wildkin outcome (105) creates a Wildkin, not a human child, yet is also a completed delivery. The counter is a diagnostics-only value with no gameplay consumer that distinguishes a live birth from a delivery (relationshipDiagnostics.ts is its only reader), and the interval funnel it feeds is a delivery funnel, so no simulation outcome is wrong; at most the name invites a different reading. Refuted as a logic defect, not a player-visible bug.

refuted.title: releasePrisoners runs full housing + workforce reconciliation from the realtime layer
refuted.evidence: L697-698: "assignMissingResidences(villagers, state.buildings, state.entities);\n    assignMissingWorkers(villagers, state.buildings);" inside releasePrisoners, which tickLayerRealtime.ts:72 calls on every realtime tick (`releasePrisoners(state);`).
refuted.impact: The two heaviest full-population scans (the up-to-24-pass residence reconciliation and the workforce rebalance/soft-steal pass) are executed on whatever realtime tick a prison sentence expires instead of in the assignment cadence owned by tickLayerAssign, and the authority table lists immediate reconciliation only for place/recruit/death/divorce/arrest. §9's checklist item "No new full-population scan was added to a realtime path" is violated; the release decision itself is cheap but silently drags an assignment-cadence decision into realtime.
refuted.fix: Let releasePrisoners only free the prisoner and clear the prison fields (plus the occupants entry), and rely on the next tickLayerAssign pulse for re-housing/re-staffing — or invoke it from tickLayerAssign next to the other immediate triggers.
refuted.verification: The calls are exactly where the finding says (workforce.ts:697-698, invoked from tickLayerRealtime.ts:72), but they sit inside `if (released)` at line 693, so the two reconciliation passes run once per actual release event rather than on every realtime tick, and they are the assignment owner's own transitions (assignMissingResidences / assignMissingWorkers), not a second rules engine. Release is the symmetric counterpart of the documented immediate 'arrest' trigger in the housing/residency row of SIMULATION_AUTHORITY §3, and no player-visible outcome depends on the timing. The only measurable divergence I found is that the optional venue-schedule argument is omitted (assignMissingWorkers(villagers, state.buildings) vs tickLayerAssign.ts:37 passing `world`), which the next assign pulse (~18 ticks) overwrites — a preference note, not a defect.

refuted.title: Ledger/foodHistory are outside the worker rollback snapshot, so a reverted tick double-counts in the ledger
refuted.verification: The omission is real — simWorker/simPrep.ts:10-87 lists neither economyLedger nor foodHistory, and applySimPrep restores resources without them — but the stated consequence is unreachable in production. A throwing gameTick or an exhausted render-buffer pool posts a 'tick' error (gameWorker.ts:339-356) which GameWorkerHost turns into onWorkerFault (GameWorkerHost.ts:492-505) and the loop answers with fallbackFromWorker, which disposes the worker (gameLoop.ts:348-351, 385-404), and the main-thread world's ledger is only ever written by simDelta fields from successful ticks (simDelta.ts:340-353, 482-493) — so no tick is retried against the half-written ledger. The command-failure rollback keeps the worker alive (gameWorker.ts:222-223) but no worker command writes the ledger (recordFoodProduced/recordFoodConsumed are called only from the daily layer, dailyChallenges and tryEatColonyMeal), so this is an incompleteness in the snapshot with no observable effect.

refuted.lines: 206-212, 224-234 | 206-234 (entity commit at 234; offending spawn write at src/game/tradeCaravans.ts:246)
refuted.title: Entities that die inside the daily layer after its prune stay in `state.entities` as dead for up to a full day
refuted.evidence: gameTick.ts:105 `const aliveEntities = state.entities.filter((e) => e.alive);` then 206-212 build `allAlive` from that pre-tick snapshot plus `newEntities`, and 234 `state.entities = allAlive;`. `spawnCaravan` (called from the systems layer via tickLayerSystems.ts:142 -> tickTradeCaravans -> spawnCaravan) instead does tradeCaravans.ts:246 `state.entities.push(carrier);` (plus `indexLivingEntity`), which is in neither list. gameTick.ts:224-226 documents the contract: 'Daily systems may append authoritative entities through ctx.newEntities'.
refuted.impact: `state.entities = allAlive` silently deletes the carrier at the end of the departure tick, so `hasActiveCarrier` (tradeCaravans.ts:256-259, `state.entities.some(...)`) is false on the very next systems pulse; because `spawnCaravan` returned true, `route.nextDepartureTick` was cleared (tradeCaravans.ts:275-277), so the route re-schedules a fresh departure ~8 days later (`scheduleTradeRouteDeparture`, EVENT_INTERVAL.tradeRoute). Every departure first calls `deductExports(state, route)` (tradeCaravans.ts:231) after `canAffordExports`, so the colony loses the route's wood/stone/food/gold every 8 days forever: no carrier ever walks, `applyImports` (tradeCaravans.ts:336) never runs, `caravansCompleted`/`tradeCaravansCompleted`/`goldFromTradeRoutes` never increase, and no refund is possible. `getCaravanMoveTarget`/`tryAdvanceCaravanLeg` (humanTick.ts:445) are dead code as a result.
refuted.fix: Spawn the carrier through the documented tick-layer contract: give `tickTradeCaravans(state, ctx)` and `spawnCaravan(state, ctx, route)` the TickContext and replace `state.entities.push(carrier); indexLivingEntity(state, carrier);` with `pushNewEntity(state, ctx, carrier);` (simulationEntities.ts:17-27 already registers entityById/grids; keep `indexLivingEntity` if the persistent index is still needed). Alternatively, make gameTick preserve untracked in-tick spawns, but the ctx.newEntities path is the one every other spawner uses (simulationEntities.ts:26, dailyPopulation.ts:112-114, tickLayerSystems.ts:133).
refuted.verification: The claim's central fact is wrong: gameTick.ts:105 rebuilds `aliveEntities` from `state.entities.filter((e) => e.alive)` on every tick, so a body left in `allAlive` at line 234 is dropped at the start of the very next tick (retention = the remainder of the dying tick, not 72 ticks). The suggested `state.entities = allAlive.filter((e) => e.alive)` would also break simInvariants.ts check #4, whose `allIds` set is built from `state.entities` and runs in the same tick's dev pulse: a living human whose partner died in that daily layer would be reported as 'partnerId missing'. The observation that the dying tick's array still holds the body is accurate, but the described failure (day-long corpses, saves carrying them) is not reachable.

refuted.title: birthsCompletedThisInterval also counts stillbirths and Wildkin births
refuted.evidence: 90: `recordRelationshipDiagnostic('birthsCompletedThisInterval');` — recorded before the Wildkin branch (103-115, returns at 114) and before the stillborn branch (118-127, returns at 126)
refuted.impact: The diagnostics contract says this counter "increments only at a completed birth" (relationshipDiagnostics.ts:5-19 and the header of tests/relationshipDiagnostics.test.ts:10-12), and §5 requires diagnostics to distinguish completed births. A stillbirth creates no child and is logged as a death, yet it increments the birth counter; the same happens for a Wildkin birth. The existing test only covers the successful human-birth path, so nothing locks this in.

CHANGELOG.md:46 states explicitly that `birthsCompletedThisInterval` 'always counted deliveries', and grep shows no consumer beyond the flush/dev log (relationshipDiagnostics.ts:118-144) derives human birth rates from it; stillbirth is 0.1% (LIFECYCLE_CONFIG.STILLBORN_CHANCE) anyway. refuted.title: Construction crew cap reuses maxOccupants, which for housing is the bed capacity, so a house site absorbs 6-12 builders by draining workplaces
