refuted.evidence: L396-397: "const cap = BUILDING_CONFIGS[building.type].maxOccupants;\n  if (building.occupants.length >= cap) return false;" plus the pass-2 loop L540-545 "while (assignBuilderInPlace(building, alive, buildings)) { // Fill crew capacity }" — while buildings.ts:129-136 documents maxOccupants as "Housing (House, Mansion, LeaderHouse): bed / resident capacity".
refuted.impact: staffConstructionCrews (called 4x/day from tickLayerAssign via assignMissingWorkers) fills every unfinished site to that number: a House site holds 6 builders, a Mansion 8, a Leader's House 12. Once no idle settler is left, assignBuilderInPlace's soft-steal (L417-451) takes the rest from completed non-manual workplaces, which can drop to zero workers (only Farm/Greenhouse are protected, L442); the stolen settlers are then excluded from job assignment by isOnConstructionCrew, so production buildings stand empty while the site builds and countWorkingAndIdleSettlers still reports the strippers as 'working'. Reproduce with an all-employed village plus one queued House: Quarry/Lumber Mill crews are moved onto the site.
refuted.fix: Use a dedicated crew limit instead of the role-overloaded field, e.g. `const cap = isResidenceBuildingType(building.type) ? MAX_CONSTRUCTION_BUILDERS : BUILDING_CONFIGS[building.type].maxOccupants;` with a small named constant.
refuted.verification: The 6-builder House site is designed, not accidental: the same cap is used by the manual assignment path (buildingStaffingActions.ts:83), the UI shows 'Builders: N / config.maxOccupants' (SelectedBuildingPanel.tsx:360), and buildings.ts:128-135 documents maxOccupants as a slot cap deliberately overloaded by role (for a site, the crew). The soft-steal priority (workforce.ts:438-446, Farm/Greenhouse protected at staffed<=1) is likewise the intended lower-priority-job rule, and countWorkingAndIdleSettlers counting crew members as working is consistent with that rule. A separate crew constant would be a balance change, not a correctness fix.

refuted.title: placeStripChain removes a replaced building itself, skipping every cleanup the removal owner performs, and pays an uncapped refund
refuted.evidence: line 274: `state.buildings = state.buildings.filter((building) => building.id !== replacementId);` followed by line 280 `refundHalfBuildingCost(state, existing.type);`, where line 180 is `state.resources.wood += Math.floor(config.cost.wood * 0.5);`. The authoritative removal path (`buildingMaintenanceActions.demolishBuilding`, lines 204-214) instead calls `unindexAdjacency(state, buildingId)`, sets `state.adjacency = undefined`, clears `roadAvoidance`/`roadAvoidanceStamp` for roads and decrements `state.totalBuildingsCompleted`; none of that happens here.
refuted.impact: A second owner of building removal exists. If a replaced Road/Barn/Market ever leaves state through this path, the live `AdjacencyIndex` keeps its bucket entry (the phantom source keeps granting +0.15 road / +0.35 barn / +0.25 market multipliers to neighbours, and the object is retained forever), `totalBuildingsCompleted` stays one too high until the next save/load recompute (saveLoad.ts:447), and the road-avoidance index keeps routing around a destroyed road. The refund also bypasses storage caps (it uses `+=` instead of `addResource`, which is what demolishBuilding uses), so a refund at a full wood/stone store can push stores above `storageMax` — the exact 'caps bypassed / ledger vs actual' split between two implementations of the same 50% rule (`BUILDING_REFUND_RATIO` at buildingMaintenanceActions.ts:12 vs the literal `0.5` here).
refuted.fix: Route the removal through one shared transition: extract demolishBuilding's cleanup block (unindexAdjacency + adjacency/roadAvoidance invalidation + counter decrement) into an exported helper such as `removeBuildingFromWorld(state, building)` and call it here instead of the raw `filter`, and make `refundHalfBuildingCost` use `addResource(state, 'wood', Math.floor(config.cost.wood * BUILDING_REFUND_RATIO))` for each resource.
refuted.verification: The cited lines do exactly what the auditor says, but the branch is unreachable: no code anywhere ever assigns StripPlacementPiece.replacesBuildingId (stripTopology.ts:131 and stripBuild.ts:29 only declare it; buildingPlacementActions.ts only reads it), resolveStripPlan/buildStripPlanFromDrag never set it, and buildStripPreview forwards the undefined value, so segment.replacesBuildingId is always undefined in production. Consequently no Road/Barn/Market can leave state through this path, and the += refund at 180-182 is equally dead. Routing it through a shared removal helper would be a reasonable cleanup but fixes no live defect.

refuted.title: placeStripChain indexes BUILDING_CONFIGS with the payload-supplied segment.placeType without a guard
refuted.evidence: lines 254-257: `const placeType = segment.placeType ?? type;` … `const config = BUILDING_CONFIGS[placeType];`, reached from commands.ts:326 (`return placeStripChain(world, cmd.type, cmd.segments, cmd.rotation ?? 0);`), where the only segment validation is commands.ts:199-203 `const seg = value as { x?: unknown; y?: unknown }; return isFiniteNumber(seg.x) && isFiniteNumber(seg.y);` — `placeType`, `valid` and `rotation` are never validated.
refuted.impact: A `placeStripChain` payload whose segment carries an unknown/removed `placeType` (a hand-built command, or a stale sender) makes `config` undefined and the next line `state.resources.wood < config.cost.wood` throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'cost')`. `applyWorkerCommand` has no try/catch (commands.ts:316-326), so the throw escapes the command boundary instead of being rejected like a malformed command, and the same unguarded read repeats in `buildStripPreview` (line 210).
refuted.fix: Guard the lookup: `const config = BUILDING_CONFIGS[placeType] ?? BUILDING_CONFIGS[type];` (or `if (!BUILDING_CONFIGS[placeType]) continue;`), and reject unknown `placeType` in commands.ts `isStripSegment` with `isBuildingType(seg.placeType)` when present.
refuted.verification: StripSegment.placeType is a required BuildingType (stripBuild.ts:19-30) and every producer of segments (resolveStripPlan/resolveRoadStripPlan/resolveWallStripPlan in stripTopology.ts) emits a real BuildingType, with commands built only from buildStripPreview segments (useCanvasInteractions.ts:157-174, virtualPlayer.ts:1103-1114), so no in-client path can supply an unknown placeType; only a hand-crafted command could, and the shape validator (commands.ts:199-203) is the only boundary. The cited companion claim is also inaccurate: buildStripPreview's line 210 uses piece.type from the plan, not a payload placeType. Adding isBuildingType(seg.placeType) would be harmless hardening, not a bug fix.

refuted.title: Naive radial scan lacks the grid's non-finite/negative radius guard, so grid and naive modes disagree for NaN inputs
refuted.verification: It is true that forEachInArrayRadius, naiveFindClosestInArray and simQueries' naive helpers omit the guard that spatialGrid.ts:297/377 applies, and that the naive path is live in production because the adaptive cost model may select it. However, every caller passes positive constant radii (SOCIAL_FRIENDSHIP_RADIUS 96, 150, 48/72/90/120) and entity coordinates, and simInvariants.ts:21 reports non-finite positions as an invariant violation, so the NaN/negative-input state required to make the two modes disagree cannot arise in play. Adding the same early return is reasonable defensive parity but fixes no reachable defect.

refuted.title: The commands decision declares `building.occupants` as its own write, duplicating the workforce owner
refuted.evidence: decisionRegistry.ts:283-286 `return ( cleanPermitted.includes(cleanField) || cleanField.includes(cleanPermitted) || permitted.toLowerCase().includes(cleanField) );` after line 278 strips only a leading `entity|human|building|residence.` prefix.
refuted.impact: The helper's contract ('Checks whether a specific property write is declared by a given subsystem') is not met: `isPropertyWritePermitted('production', 'age')` returns true because the permitted `'storageMax'` contains 'age', and any one-character field name (e.g. `'x'`) returns true for nearly every decision because some permitted string contains that letter ('human.relationshipStatus (expecting)'). An architecture linter built on this helper would silently accept an owner writing a field it does not declare — exactly the mutation-boundary check the registry exists to enforce. Additionally the `housing` row's `'residence building.occupants'` (line 84) never normalises because the prefix regex requires a dot after the word.
refuted.fix: Match field names exactly after normalisation (split the declaration on whitespace/commas and compare `===` against the cleaned field, or use a word-boundary regex), and drop the two `includes` directions.
refuted.verification: The duplicate listing is real but is the established pattern, not a commands-specific breach: 'building.occupants' is declared in five rows (workforce:69, construction:96, moonHowler:208, leadership:223, commands:237) as documentation that includes delegated writes, e.g. moonHowler's 'during transform/restore' and leadership's 'stale leader assignment only'. The advertised ownership check isPropertyWritePermitted has no callers anywhere in the repo, and no UI component writes occupants (commands.ts:326 routes to buildingActions, which uses workforce transitions), so no enforcement or mutation boundary is weakened. This is metadata tidying at most.

refuted.title: Defense research migration is a no-op: mergeCombatResearchNodes' return value is discarded
refuted.evidence: saveLoad.ts:531 `const clearedChurchSeats = clearAutoFilledChurches(world);` and saveLoad.ts:327-328 `if (human && human.alive && human.homeBuildingId === church.id) {` / `removeWorkerTransition(human, world.buildings);`
refuted.impact: In a current-version save a player Church can only be staffed by the manually chosen priest, and that priest is stored exactly the way the destructive branch detects: `assignIdleWorkerToBuilding` sets `occupants=[priestId]` + `homeBuildingId=church.id` + job Priest (tests/church.manualStaffing.test.ts:107-113, tests/workerCommand.roundtrip.test.ts:143-150). Because the call is unconditional and the same-version gate (saveLoad.ts:80-82) means no pre-0.6.4 save can reach it, every load of a save with a staffed Church empties the Church and resets the priest to settler (`removeWorkerTransition` clears homeBuildingId/job/occupation). The recorded migration id only dedupes the log line (applySaveMigration, saveLoad.ts:489-494), not the destructive clear, and `assignMissingWorkers` never refills a manual workplace, so the priest stays idle after every reload. Player-visible: the priest assignment is lost on each load/save cycle.
refuted.fix: Stop running the migration on load: delete the call at saveLoad.ts:531 (and the now-unreachable function) — or, if the migration must stay, gate it on a persisted one-time marker/legacy version instead of calling it for every 0.6.4 save.
refuted.verification: The call at saveLoad.ts:539 does discard the new array returned by the explicitly non-mutating combat.ts:441-459, so it is a genuine no-op — but its only purpose was repairing old saves and no loadable save can lack the defense nodes: parseSaveJson rejects every version except the current one (saveLoad.ts:74-88, pinned by tests/saveVersion.gate.test.ts), worldGen seeds researchNodes from createInitialResearchNodes() (gameTypes.ts:905-933, worldGen.ts:636) which already contains defense_1..defense_10 with defense_1 unlocked:true, and git shows those nodes predate the 0.6.4 version bump. Assigning the result would change nothing in play.

refuted.title: Birth outcomes draw from unseeded Math.random while the same birth creates the child from the seeded stream
refuted.evidence: 79: `const wildkinBirth = nearDeer && Math.random() < LIFECYCLE_CONFIG.WILDKIN_CHANCE;`, 118: `if (Math.random() < LIFECYCLE_CONFIG.STILLBORN_CHANCE) {`, 139: `const childGender ... Math.random() > 0.5 ? 'male' : 'female'`
refuted.impact: The run seed is the simulation's determinism contract (`setSimSeed`, `getSimRng`, `seededRandomForRun`; tests/deterministicSeed.test.ts asserts same-seed replay), and the child created two lines later comes from `createEntity`, which deliberately draws from `getSimRng('entityFactory')` (entityFactory.ts:15-18). Because the birth owner uses global Math.random for wildkin/stillborn/gender, a seeded replay diverges permanently at the first birth (different children, lineage, population) — a divergence the 100-tick determinism test never reaches, since pregnancy is 1728 ticks.
refuted.fix: Draw these three decisions from the sim RNG, e.g. `seededRandomForRun(`birth:${entity.id}:${state.tick}:wildkin`)` (context rolls, as humanChat/humanLeisureBehavior already do) or a dedicated `getSimRng('humanLifecycle')` stream.
refuted.verification: The Math.random calls exist as cited, but the premise that they are unseeded is wrong: initGame calls setSimSeed(seed) and enableSeededGlobalRandom() (worldGen.ts:568-570), which replaces Math.random with a seeded Mulberry32 stream for the whole main-thread session (simRng.ts:132-137), so a same-seed in-process replay (the path tests/deterministicSeed.test.ts exercises via initGame) reproduces these birth rolls rather than diverging. createEntity's getSimRng('entityFactory') stream is not more seeded than they are; the real (different) gap is that the sim worker never calls setSimSeed/initGame, so in the worker both Math.random and every getSimRng stream are unseeded/default-1 — a project-wide seed-propagation issue that this suggested three-line change would not fix.

crossFindings.title: The simulation worker never receives or installs the run seed, so the entire authoritative simulation ignores it
crossFindings.evidence: gameWorker.ts:152 `resetWorkerSession(msg.world);` and gameWorker.ts:118-124 `function resetWorkerSession(nextWorld: WorldState): void { // Rehydrate spatial and ID lookups on the incoming world  hydrateWorldRuntimeCaches(nextWorld);` — the only two setters, `setSimSeed(mapSeed);` / `enableSeededGlobalRandom();` (worldGen.ts:569-570), are called from `initGame` on the main thread only; `grep setSimSeed` matches nothing in src/game/simWorker/** and `importSave`/`syncWorld`/`init` all funnel through `resetWorkerSession`.
crossFindings.impact: The worker is the production owner (`isGameWorkerEnabled()` returns true by default, GameWorkerHost.ts:570-579; gameLoop.ts:216 uploads the world via `workerHost.importSave`). Inside that realm simRng keeps its module default `currentSeed = 1` (simRng.ts:4) and `Math.random` is native, so the run seed has no effect on the authoritative simulation: (a) all `getSimRng(owner)` streams collapse to seed 1, making entityFactory gender/age/`reproductionCooldown` (entityFactory.ts:61,104,113), migration edge (migration.ts:39), famine bite (famineDesperation.ts:68) and prison escapes (prisonGuardDuty.ts:55) identical across every new game; (b) every raw `Math.random()` gameplay roll becomes truly non-reproducible — grep finds 303 `Math.random` references under src (~296 in src/game, ~250 of them in modules reachable from gameTick, across ~27 simulation modules), including conception (humanRelationships.ts:736,777,799), birth/stillborn/gender (humanLifecycle.ts:118,139), old-age and illness death (humanRelationships.ts:828,842), weather (worldEvents.ts:72), wolf recruitment/breeding (tickLayerSystems.ts:104,109,575,706), daily festival/immigration (dailyWorldEvents.ts:71, dailyPopulation.ts:66) and group/rival event rolls (groupEvents.ts, rivalEvents.ts). The existing D1 test cannot catch this because it drives the main-thread path directly (tests/deterministicSeed.test.ts:29 `current = gameTick(current);`).
crossFindings.suggestedChange: In `resetWorkerSession` (gameWorker.ts:118) call `setSimSeed(nextWorld.worldMap?.seed ?? getSimSeed())` and `enableSeededGlobalRandom()` (import them from '../simRng'), so every `init`/`importSave`/`syncWorld` installs the run seed in the worker realm.

crossFindings.title: Seeded global Math.random is shared with the renderer/audio, so in the main-thread fallback the sim stream depends on frames rendered
crossFindings.evidence: simRng.ts:135 `Math.random = () => seededGlobalStream!();` (installed by `initGame`, worldGen.ts:570) while presentation code in the same realm draws from that same stream: renderer.ts:49 `ctx.translate((Math.random() - 0.5) * shake * 2, (Math.random() - 0.5) * shake * 2);` and renderer/weather.ts:36 `x: Math.random() * cw * 1.5 - cw * 0.25,` (weather rebuilds `WEATHER_CONFIGS[w].particleCount` particles and respawns them every frame, lines 34-41 and 52).
crossFindings.impact: When the worker is disabled or fails to start, gameLoop falls back to main-thread ticks (gameLoop.ts:198 `'[GameLoop] Worker init failed — falling back to main-thread ticks'`) and sim draws and frame draws interleave on one stream: `worldEvents.updateWeather` (worldEvents.ts:72), `humanLifecycle.tickPregnancyAndBirth` (humanLifecycle.ts:139) and the conception rolls (humanRelationships.ts:736) consume values whose position was advanced by particle churn, window size and screen-shake. The same seed therefore produces different worlds at 30 fps vs 144 fps, or after resizing. The deterministicSeed test only passes because rendering never runs under it.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Do not use the shared global hook for gameplay: keep `enableSeededGlobalRandom()` for the headless entry points only, and convert gameplay draws to explicit `getSimRng(owner)` streams (or give presentation its own unseeded generator).

crossFindings.title: Every injectable-RNG owner is called without its rng, so the seeded seam is dead in production
crossFindings.evidence: tickLayerRealtime.ts:97-105 `const moonResult = tickMoonHowlerCycle(state, aliveEntities, state.buildings, colonyDay, ctx.hourOfDay, ctx.entityById, ctx.byType,);` provides 7 arguments, so moonHowler.ts:952 `rng: () => number = Math.random,` applies; likewise moonHowler.ts:1044 `const dawnCures = tryMoonHowlerChurchCures(state, aliveEntities, buildings, colonyDay, hourOfDay, entityById);` omits the parameter defaulted at moonHowler.ts:642, and inside `tickMoonHowlerCycle` the decision uses `rng` (moonHowler.ts:1016) while the flavour lines use the global stream (moonHowler.ts:990 `WEREWOLF_TRANSFORM_LINES[Math.floor(Math.random() * ...)]`).
crossFindings.impact: The Moon Howler lifecycle rolls that were explicitly made injectable — `shouldApplyNewMoonHowlerCurse` (moonHowler.ts:163 `&& rng() < MOON_HOWLER_REPLACEMENT_CHANCE`) and the church rite `rollMoonHowlerRiteOutcome` (moonHowler.ts:127 `const r = rng();`) plus the guard-save roll (moonHowler.ts:780) — are drawn from the unseeded/global stream in production, so the one-Howler-cursed/replaced lifecycle is not reproducible and tests pass only because they inject stubs (tests/moonHowler.exorcism.test.ts:151 `() => 0.49`). The same omitted-rng pattern affects `tryDailyAmicableDivorce` (humanTick.ts:357 → default humanRelationships.ts:868), `tryFormSchoolyardBond` (humanTick.ts:373 → default humanRelationships.ts:389) and `advanceYouthLove` (tickLayerDaily.ts:53 → default humanRelationships.ts:536), i.e. youth-love breakups, schoolyard bonds and divorce are all on the global stream.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Thread one domain stream through, e.g. in tickLayerRealtime.ts:97 pass `getSimRng('moon-howler')` as the 8th argument, pass it on to `tryMoonHowlerChurchCures` at moonHowler.ts:1044, replace the `Math.random()` at moonHowler.ts:990/1030/1034/1048 with `rng()`, and pass dedicated streams at humanTick.ts:357/373 and tickLayerDaily.ts:53.

crossFindings.title: Loading a save never restores the colony seed, so the seed in the save file is ignored
crossFindings.evidence: saveLoad.ts:154 persists it (`seed: worldMap.seed,`) and saveLoad.ts:168-172 regenerates terrain with it (`return generateWorldMap(parsed.worldMap.size ?? 'medium', parsed.worldMap.preset ?? 'verdant', parsed.worldMap.seed);`) and assigns `worldMap: restoreWorldMapFromSave(parsed),` at saveLoad.ts:374, but the load path contains no `setSimSeed` call — repo-wide the only callers are worldGen.ts:569 and test files, and `loadGame()` (saveLoad.ts:592-601) and `applyLoadedSession` (App.tsx:953) only replace the world.
crossFindings.impact: `simRng.currentSeed` and the cached per-owner streams (simRng.ts:4-5, `streams`) keep the values of the session that happens to be running, so `seededRandomForRun`-based systems read the wrong seed after a load: chat and courtship lines (humanChat.ts:387,438,461,472,523; humanTick.ts:874,876), venue/work chat (humanVenueBehavior.ts:57) and leisure bubbles (humanLeisureBehavior.ts:100,122). The same save file therefore produces different social content depending on which run loaded it (and differs from the original run), while seed-derived systems such as renffrStar/electionPromises/inventionFair that read `state.worldMap.seed` (renffrStar.ts:46) stay correct — the two notions of "the run seed" disagree.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: At the end of `loadGameFromParsed` (after `world.worldMap` is set, saveLoad.ts:374) call `setSimSeed(world.worldMap?.seed ?? getSimSeed())` so currentSeed and all cached streams are rebuilt from the saved seed.

crossFindings.title: RNG stream position is not part of any rollback/save snapshot, so a resumed or retried world cannot reproduce its continuation
crossFindings.evidence: The full rollback key set is `type SimPrepKeys = | 'tick' | 'year' | 'dayInYear' | ...` (simPrep.ts:10-13) and contains no RNG entry, while the generators live in module state outside `WorldState` (simRng.ts:4-5 `let currentSeed = 1; const streams = new Map<string, RngStream>();`). The worker restores the world snapshot without touching that state: gameWorker.ts:222-223 `} catch (err) { applySimPrep(world, prepBackup);` and gameWorker.ts:355 `applySimPrep(world, prepBackup);`.
crossFindings.impact: Any rollback or resume continues from an advanced RNG position: (a) after a failed command/tick the world is reverted but the draws already consumed by the failed attempt are gone, so a retried command (or the next tick) yields different random outcomes than the un-failed run; (b) even if finding #4 is fixed by re-seeding on load, clearing the streams restarts entityFactory/migration/famine-desperation/prison-guard-duty at draw #1 while the world is at day N, so a save/load continuation diverges from the original run. Because none of this state is in the save, delta or prep payload, no code path can restore it.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Add RNG-state capture to the existing snapshot mechanism: export `captureSimRngState()`/`restoreSimRngState()` from simRng.ts (covering `currentSeed`, each stream's internal counter and `seededGlobalStream`), include it in `SimPrepPayload` and restore it in `applySimPrep`, and persist it in the save payload so a loaded colony resumes at the same stream position.

crossFindings.title: Conception and pregnancy duration — the invariant-critical reproductive owner — draw from raw Math.random instead of a domain stream
crossFindings.evidence: humanRelationships.ts:736 `if (Math.random() < baseChance * fertility * traitMultiplier(entity, 'lucky', 1.15)) {`, humanRelationships.ts:799 `if (Math.random() < HUMAN_DAILY_AFFAIR_PREGNANCY_CHANCE * fertility) {` (also :777), and the resulting due date is rolled raw at humanRelationships.ts:640 `entity.pregnancyDueProgress = Math.round(PREGNANCY_TICKS * (0.85 + Math.random() * 0.3));` (also :660, :676); sibling lifecycle owners do the same (humanLifecycle.ts:118 stillborn, :139 `const childGender: 'male' | 'female' = Math.random() > 0.5 ? 'male' : 'female';`, settlerTraits.ts:229 inheritance, nameLoader.ts:255 name pick).
crossFindings.impact: Which married/affair/youth couples conceive, and on which tick each child is born, depend on an unseeded global stream, so a run seed cannot reproduce the colony's demographic history (and after fixing #1 the worker would still draw these from native Math.random). It also means one shared stream is used by every raw-Math.random owner, so adding or removing a single `Math.random()` call anywhere in the sim (or a render particle draw, in fallback mode) silently shifts conception, birth, gender, mortality and trait inheritance outcomes — the exact class of drift the per-owner `getSimRng` design (simRng.ts:82-89) exists to prevent.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Give each owner a stream and use it for these rolls, e.g. `const rng = getSimRng('human-relationships')` for the conception gates and `getSimRng('human-lifecycle')` for birth/stillborn/gender, passing the same stream into `startMarriedPregnancy`/`startYouthPregnancy`/`startAffairPregnancy` for `pregnancyDueProgress`.

crossFindings.title: Off-screen wildlife throttle gate can never fire for 3/4 of entity ids (tick always a multiple of the layer interval)
crossFindings.evidence: 252-254: `const wildlifeInFocus = !focus || isInFocus(entity, focus);` / `const wildlifeActive =` / `wildlifeInFocus || (state.tick + entity.id) % OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE === 0;` — this code only ever runs inside `tickLayerSystems`, which gameTick calls only when `state.tick % LAYER_SYSTEMS_INTERVAL === 0` (gameTick.ts:198) and `LAYER_SYSTEMS_INTERVAL = WILDLIFE_LAYER_INTERVAL = 4` (tickLayerSystems.ts:70, simFocus.ts:32), while `OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE = 8` (simFocus.ts:26).
crossFindings.impact: Because `state.tick` is always a multiple of 4 at this point, `(state.tick + id) % 8 === 0` is satisfiable only when `id % 8` is 0 or 4 — i.e. only for entities whose id is a multiple of 4 (25%). For every other id (1,2,3,5,6,7 mod 8) the fallback throttle is never true, so out-of-focus fauna permanently skips the whole AI block (movement, grazing, hunting, mating, block 6-16) while still paying the per-pulse energy drain at line 242 (`entity.energy -= (config.energyLossPerTick * grazerEase + winterPenalty) * step;`), so they starve to death at line 244-249 without ever grazing. In production the worker passes the camera viewport as focus (gameLoop.ts:825 -> requestTick -> gameWorker.ts:317), and at the default zoom 1.45 the focus rect is only ~1122x736 px, so on Medium/Large/Huge maps a large band of the map is out of focus: e.g. a wolf spawned by `tickWolfRecruitment` at the map edge with id 11 walks nowhere and dies of starvation, and autumn migration herds / `replenishDepletedWildlife` arrivals freeze in place. The intended cadence of the constant ('every N wildlife-layer calls', simFocus.ts:25) is also not what the code implements even for the lucky ids: multiples of 4 are active once per 8 ticks, i.e. every 2 layer calls.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Evaluate the throttle on the layer pulse index instead of the raw tick: `const wildlifePulse = Math.floor(state.tick / WILDLIFE_LAYER_INTERVAL);` then `wildlifeInFocus || (wildlifePulse + entity.id) % OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE === 0;` — every id then gets full AI once per OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE layer calls (32 ticks), matching the constant's comment. (If 8 ticks was the intent, use `state.tick % OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE === 0 && entity.id % OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE === 0`-style staggering that cannot strand ids.)

crossFindings.lines: 206-234 (entity commit at 234; offending spawn write at src/game/tradeCaravans.ts:246)
crossFindings.title: gameTick's `state.entities = allAlive` destroys entities pushed directly onto state.entities during the tick — trade-caravan carriers never survive, so exports are deducted every 8 days with no delivery
crossFindings.evidence: gameTick.ts:105 `const aliveEntities = state.entities.filter((e) => e.alive);` then 206-212 build `allAlive` from that pre-tick snapshot plus `newEntities`, and 234 `state.entities = allAlive;`. `spawnCaravan` (called from the systems layer via tickLayerSystems.ts:142 -> tickTradeCaravans -> spawnCaravan) instead does tradeCaravans.ts:246 `state.entities.push(carrier);` (plus `indexLivingEntity`), which is in neither list. gameTick.ts:224-226 documents the contract: 'Daily systems may append authoritative entities through ctx.newEntities'.
crossFindings.impact: `state.entities = allAlive` silently deletes the carrier at the end of the departure tick, so `hasActiveCarrier` (tradeCaravans.ts:256-259, `state.entities.some(...)`) is false on the very next systems pulse; because `spawnCaravan` returned true, `route.nextDepartureTick` was cleared (tradeCaravans.ts:275-277), so the route re-schedules a fresh departure ~8 days later (`scheduleTradeRouteDeparture`, EVENT_INTERVAL.tradeRoute). Every departure first calls `deductExports(state, route)` (tradeCaravans.ts:231) after `canAffordExports`, so the colony loses the route's wood/stone/food/gold every 8 days forever: no carrier ever walks, `applyImports` (tradeCaravans.ts:336) never runs, `caravansCompleted`/`tradeCaravansCompleted`/`goldFromTradeRoutes` never increase, and no refund is possible. `getCaravanMoveTarget`/`tryAdvanceCaravanLeg` (humanTick.ts:445) are dead code as a result.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Spawn the carrier through the documented tick-layer contract: give `tickTradeCaravans(state, ctx)` and `spawnCaravan(state, ctx, route)` the TickContext and replace `state.entities.push(carrier); indexLivingEntity(state, carrier);` with `pushNewEntity(state, ctx, carrier);` (simulationEntities.ts:17-27 already registers entityById/grids; keep `indexLivingEntity` if the persistent index is still needed). Alternatively, make gameTick preserve untracked in-tick spawns, but the ctx.newEntities path is the one every other spawner uses (simulationEntities.ts:26, dailyPopulation.ts:112-114, tickLayerSystems.ts:133).

crossFindings.title: Realtime layer performs a full-population scan and rewrites residence `occupants` every tick while a Moon Howler is active
crossFindings.evidence: 117-123: `if (activeMoonHowler) { const occupants: Entity[] = []; for (const entity of aliveEntities) { if (isResidenceOccupantEntity(entity)) occupants.push(entity); } syncResidenceOccupants(occupants, ctx.updatedBuildings); }` — `aliveEntities` is the whole living-entity array and `syncResidenceOccupants` (residencyReconciliation.ts:113-119) rewrites `building.occupants` for every residence by filtering that array, so the cost is O(entities x residences) per tick.
crossFindings.impact: SIMULATION_AUTHORITY section 3 assigns residence occupancy writes to the `dayCycle.ts` residence functions scheduled from `tickLayerAssign` (4x/day) plus immediate entries on place/recruit/death/divorce/arrest (confirmed by decisionRegistry.ts:78-89, scheduledFrom 'tickLayerAssign.syncResidenceOccupants + assignMissingResidences'), and section 4/9 forbid full-population scans in the realtime path. This block adds a second, realtime schedule for that write on every tick of every full-moon night (~30 ticks), and it is redundant: the same reconciliation already runs at the form change itself (moonHowler.ts:971-974, 1025-1028, 1056-1059) and at each assign pulse, and a werewolf-form howler has `residenceBuildingId === undefined` (moonHowler.ts:382, forceMoonHowlerOutside line 303), so it can never contribute an occupant id — the write can only reproduce the current value while allocating a fresh `occupants` array per residence per tick (array-identity churn for UI/render memoization) and dirtying the authoritative worker state every tick.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Delete the `if (activeMoonHowler) { ... syncResidenceOccupants(...) }` block from tickLayerRealtime; if a repair is genuinely needed while a cursed settler is in werewolf form, make tickLayerAssign's `allHumans` include cursed werewolves (`world.entities.filter(isResidenceOccupantEntity)`) instead of re-scheduling the residence owner from the realtime layer.

crossFindings.title: Hour-granular full-moon gate is evaluated on all three ticks of hour 20 — replacement curse rolls 3x per full moon and the 'Full Moon!' announcement repeats 3x
crossFindings.evidence: moonHowler.ts:161 `&& hourOfDay === NIGHT_START` (inside shouldApplyNewMoonHowlerCurse) is reached from the realtime layer every tick: moonHowler.ts:1016 `if (shouldApplyNewMoonHowlerCurse(colonyDay, hourOfDay, humanPop, activeMoonCurses, rng)) {`. `getHourOfDay` = `Math.floor(getTickOfDay(tick) / TICKS_PER_HOUR)` (dayCycleClock.ts:19-21), so hour 20 covers tick-of-day 60, 61 and 62. Likewise moonHowler.ts:924 `nightFall: transformTick && (transformed.length > 0 || huntingTonight),` with `transformTick = isMoonHowlerTransformTick(...)` = `hourOfDay === NIGHT_START && isFullMoonDay(...)` (lines 224-226) is true on all three ticks, and it drives 983-986 `if (moonSync.nightFall) { addBigNews(state, '🌝 Full Moon!', ...)` (addBigNews has no dedup, simEffects.ts:96-111).
crossFindings.impact: With no active curse the realtime layer rolls `rng() < MOON_HOWLER_REPLACEMENT_CHANCE` (0.15) three times per full moon, so the effective per-full-moon replacement probability is 1 - 0.85^3 = 0.386 -- 2.6x the declared constant and far from the constant's own stated budget of '~1-2 replacements per year' (moonHowler.ts:77-84) and section 5's 'rare replacement roll'. Separately, whenever a cursed howler is active (huntingTonight true at ticks 61 and 62), the player receives three identical '🌝 Full Moon!' big-news cards and three event-log entries per full moon. The cure rite does not have this problem because it is rate-limited by `state.lastMoonHowlerExorcismTick` (lines 673-678).
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Restrict the nightfall decision to the first tick of the hour: in tickMoonHowlerCycle change line 1016 to `if (state.tick % TICKS_PER_HOUR === 0 && shouldApplyNewMoonHowlerCurse(colonyDay, hourOfDay, humanPop, activeMoonCurses, rng)) {`, and in syncMoonHowlerForms change line 924 to `nightFall: transformTick && (tick == null || tick % TICKS_PER_HOUR === 0) && (transformed.length > 0 || huntingTonight),` so the announcement fires once.

crossFindings.title: Per-tick full-population scans feed a decision that can only fire at nightfall on a full-moon day
crossFindings.evidence: 1014-1015: `const activeMoonCurses = countActiveMoonHowlerCurses(aliveEntities);` / `const humanPop = aliveEntities.filter((e) => e.alive && isPlayerHuman(e)).length;` (countActiveMoonHowlerCurses is itself an O(N) filter, moonHowler.ts:136-138), executed from tickLayerRealtime every tick of the year; the values are only used by `shouldApplyNewMoonHowlerCurse`, which additionally requires `hourOfDay === NIGHT_START` and `isFullMoonNight(colonyDay, hourOfDay)` (roughly 1 day in 14, one hour of it). syncMoonHowlerForms adds two more per-tick passes (`entities.filter((e) => e.alive && e.type === EntityType.Human)` line 894 and `entities.some((e) => isActiveMoonHowler(e))` line 919).
crossFindings.impact: Three O(N) scans plus two array allocations of length N run on every one of the 72 ticks/day in the realtime layer even though the curse decision needs them at most once per full-moon night, which is exactly what section 4 and the section 9 pre-merge checklist ('No new full-population scan was added to a realtime path') forbid. The maintainers already removed one per-tick O(N) rebuild from this function (tests/moonHowler.byTypeReuse.test.ts), so this is the same class of regression; the wasted work is proportional to the whole living-entity set and runs all year on every tick.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Compute the cure-roll inputs only inside the nightfall window, e.g. wrap lines 1014-1016 in `if (isFullMoonNight(colonyDay, hourOfDay)) { ... }`, and reuse `ctx.byType`/`state.entityByType` buckets instead of re-filtering `aliveEntities` in syncMoonHowlerForms (line 894).

crossFindings.title: Prison escape clears prisonBuildingId but leaves the id in prison.occupants
crossFindings.impact: tickPrisonGuardDuty runs inside the daily layer (dailyWorldEvents.ts:129 <- tickLayerDaily.ts:81), so at the collector run in the same tick the escaped settler is still listed in prison.occupants with prisonBuildingId undefined and homeBuildingId undefined (arrestForScandal cleared it, humanRelationships.ts:1192). simulationInvariants.ts:139-145 therefore reports 'human N in prison #M is neither prisoner (prisonBuildingId) nor guard (homeBuildingId)' — §5's occupants-vs-ownership invariant is false until the next assign pulse (up to 18 ticks, 6 in-game hours) rebuilds the list via workforce.syncJobBuildingOccupants. Same missing cleanup as the 'stale id left in building.occupants' class the audit targets.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: After line 61 add the removal through the prison owner's list: `prison.occupants = prison.occupants.filter((id) => id !== escapee.id);` (best: extract one named release/escape transition shared by this file and workforce.releasePrisoners, which does the removal at line 672).

crossFindings.title: spawnCaravan's carrier entity is discarded by the end-of-tick entity swap, so exports are spent and imports never arrive
crossFindings.evidence:
deductExports(state, route);            // line 231 — goods reserved
  ...
  state.entities.push(carrier);           // line 246 — never ctx.newEntities / allAlive
  indexLivingEntity(state, carrier);
  route.caravanCarrierId = carrier.id;    // line 248 — stale id
crossFindings.impact: spawnCaravan is reached from tickTradeCaravans (tickLayerSystems.ts:142), i.e. during a tick, but gameTick.ts:234 unconditionally does `state.entities = allAlive`, and allAlive (gameTick.ts:206-212) contains only the pre-tick aliveEntities plus ctx.newEntities. The carrier is in neither, so it is dropped the same tick; it is never processed by humanTick (humanTick.ts:445-456) and never reaches applyImports (line 336). The deducted export goods are lost, route.caravanCarrierId is left pointing at an entity no longer in state.entities (cleared only by the next systems pulse, hasActiveCarrier line 258), and every departure pushes one more permanent ghost into state.entityById (indexLivingEntity -> ensureEntityByIdMap is cached, killHuman/removeCarrier never see it) — a per-departure leak. This is exactly the mechanism the codebase already documented and fixed for the autumn herd (migration.ts:56-57 'BUG-12: gameTick replaces state.entities with allAlive ... pushing into state.entities would discard the herd'). Net effect: no trade caravan ever completes a round trip (caravansCompleted / Trade Empire victory unreachable).
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Thread the TickContext into tickTradeCaravans/spawnCaravan and create the carrier through `pushNewEntity(state, ctx, carrier)` (which appends to ctx.newEntities) instead of `state.entities.push(carrier)`; alternatively pass the daily-layer `allAlive`-equivalent array the way migration.spawnHerdAtEdge does.

crossFindings.title: Newborn gets residenceBuildingId but is invisible to the assign layer, so a birth on a daily tick leaves residents/occupants inconsistent
crossFindings.evidence: child.residenceBuildingId = entity.residenceBuildingId;   // line 154
crossFindings.impact: tickPregnancyAndBirth runs in the realtime layer (humanTick.ts:801) and only appends the child to ctx.newEntities, so it is absent from state.entities, ctx.byType and ctx.playerHumans for the rest of the tick. tickLayerAssign then rebuilds the residence lists from the stale bucket: tickLayerAssign.ts:30-35 `const humanBucket = byType[EntityType.Human]; ... syncResidenceOccupants(allHumans, updatedBuildings)` replaces every residence occupants array (residencyReconciliation.ts:116) with a list that cannot contain the newborn. On a tick that is also a daily boundary (state.tick % 72 === 0 — the assign interval is 18, so it always coincides) the daily collector sees the child in state.entities with residenceBuildingId set but missing from that residence's occupants and reports 'human N residenceBuildingId B missing from that residence's occupants' (simulationInvariants.ts:191-195). The mismatch persists until the next assign pulse (up to 18 ticks) and also hides the baby from occupants consumers (housingDiagnostics, night effects, resident panels).
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Make same-tick newborns visible to the residence owner before the daily invariant pulse: in gameTick after `state.entities = allAlive` (line 234) call `syncResidenceOccupants(allAlive, updatedBuildings)`, or have tickLayerAssign build its human list from `world.entities` plus `ctx.newEntities` rather than `ctx.byType`.

crossFindings.title: Death cleanup never clears the survivor's youthLovePartnerId, leaving a one-sided youth-love link at the daily collector
crossFindings.evidence:
if (survivor.pregnantById === removedId) survivor.pregnantById = undefined;   // line 164
    if (survivor.childrenIds?.includes(removedId)) { ... }                          // lines 165-167 — no youthLovePartnerId case
crossFindings.impact: Neither finalizeHumanDeath (lines 42-98) nor reconcileFamilyReferencesAfterRemoval (lines 145-169) clears `youthLovePartnerId`, and killHuman (line 182) calls both. When a 12-17 year old is killed inside the daily layer after advanceYouthLove has already run (tickLayerDaily.ts:53 does the reconciliation, line 81 tickDailyWorldEvents kills: raids via frontierCombat.ts:570 from tickPendingRaidEvents, disasters via worldEvents.ts:272), the surviving sweetheart keeps `youthLovePartnerId = <dead id>`. The dead settler is pruned from state.entities at gameTick.ts:234 while youthLovePartnerId is not, so the collector reports 'human B youthLovePartnerId A references a missing or invalid settler' (simulationInvariants.ts:216-224) — §5's 'a youth-love link joins two living colony settlers' is false until the next day's advanceYouthLove reconciliation.

crossFindings.title: Leader-residency check has no exemption for the leader's temporary Moon Howler form
crossFindings.evidence:
if (manor && leader.prisonBuildingId == null && leader.residenceBuildingId !== manor.id) {   // line 284
        errors.push(`leader ${leader.id} not residing in the Leader's House (#${manor.id})`);
crossFindings.impact: transformToWerewolfForm clears `human.residenceBuildingId = undefined` (moonHowler.ts:381-383) and isActingVillageHead deliberately accepts a cursed werewolf as acting head (villageLeadership.ts:357-359, covered by the test at simulation.invariants.test.ts:288). The daily boundary tick is hour 0, and isFullMoonNight(colonyDay, 0) is true for the morning after a full-moon day (dayCycleConstants.ts:28-34), so a cursed leader is still transformed when the collector runs (transform at hour 20 of day D, revert at hour 6 of D+1). leader.prisonBuildingId is also cleared by the transform, so the guard at line 284 does not exempt it and the collector reports a false 'not residing in the Leader's House' violation for a fully legal state; the turn-around sync (tickLayerDaily.ts:59 -> leaderHouse.collectLeaderHousehold, which requires type Human) cannot repair it while the leader is a werewolf.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Exempt the temporary form in the check: `if (manor && leader.prisonBuildingId == null && leader.moonHowlerSaved == null && leader.residenceBuildingId !== manor.id)` (equivalently `leader.type !== EntityType.Werewolf`).

crossFindings.title: Debug curse command can create a second living cursed Moon Howler
crossFindings.evidence:
const candidates = state.entities.filter((entity) => entity.alive && canMoonHowlerCurse(entity));   // line 110
  ...
  if (pick) {
    ...
    curseMoonHowler(pick);   // line 115 — no active-curse gate
crossFindings.impact: canMoonHowlerCurse (moonHowler.ts:253-263) only checks the target, never the colony, so `spawnMoonHowlerDebug` (registered as a production command op in simWorker/commands.ts:99/416 and wired to the UI in App.tsx:1942) curses a second settler while a curse is already live. §5 states there is at most one living cursed Moon Howler, and the daily collector reports 'multiple living Moon Howlers: 2' (simulationInvariants.ts:262-267); the replacement owner in moonHowler.ts:1016 explicitly requires `activeCursed === 0`, so the command is a second, ungated owner of the same decision (the second path at line 129 spawns a cursed settler for a similar effect).
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Guard the command with the same owner rule, e.g. `if (countActiveMoonHowlerCurses(state.entities) > 0) return state;` at the top of spawnMoonHowlerDebug (or move the one-curse gate into curseMoonHowler so no caller can bypass it).

crossFindings.title: Manual builder assignment omits the pregnancy/alive checks its sibling paths enforce
crossFindings.evidence:
(entity) =>
      isPlayerHuman(entity)
      && !entity.isJuvenile
      && !hasWorkAssignment(entity)      // lines 88-91 — no `entity.alive`, no `!entity.pregnant`
      && !isImprisoned(entity)
crossFindings.impact: isPlayerHuman (playerHuman.ts:12-17) is a type/faction predicate and does not test `alive` or `pregnant`. Every other crew/job path excludes pregnancy — workforce.isEligibleIdleWorker (workforce.ts:58-68), assignWorkerTransition (workforce.ts:202) and assignBuilderInPlace (workforce.ts:399-409) — and addToConstructionCrew itself does not check pregnancy (workforce.ts:234-242), so the manual 'assign builder' command (assignBuilderToBuilding -> _applyBuilderAssignmentMut) can put a pregnant settler on a construction crew where auto-staffing never would. The same filter gap can select a dead settler: addToConstructionCrew returns false silently (workforce.ts:236) while lines 103-109 still announce 'Builder Assigned'.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Match the sibling filters: add `&& entity.alive && !entity.pregnant` to the pickAdultSettler predicate at lines 88-95 (or enforce both inside addToConstructionCrew and return a status the caller checks before notifying).

crossFindings.title: pruneDeadBarracksOccupants is never called and would break the reverse occupants invariant if it were
crossFindings.impact: No module calls this function (verified by repo-wide grep: only the definition matches), so the intended barracks-occupant pruning never runs — it is dead repair code. Worse, if it were called it would remove any barracks occupant who is not currently a non-imprisoned Soldier (e.g. a just-conscripted settler, or a Soldier serving a prison sentence whose homeBuildingId still points at the barracks) from `b.occupants` while leaving `homeBuildingId` set, which is precisely the mismatch simulationInvariants.ts:174-178 reports as 'homeBuildingId ... missing from that workplace's occupants'.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Delete the function (workforce.syncJobBuildingOccupants already rebuilds barracks occupants from homeBuildingId), or if it is meant to run, call it from prepareWorkforce and clear `human.homeBuildingId`/job for every dropped occupant through removeWorkerTransition.

crossFindings.title: syncGrassRenderGrid never refreshes a reusable grid, but the render-SoA caller relies on it rebuilding every tick
crossFindings.impact: In the default worker path (isGameWorkerEnabled() returns true unless VITE_USE_GAME_WORKER is off, GameWorkerHost.ts:570-579) the render grass index is frozen at the first rendered tick for the whole session: resolveSpatialGrid returns the same instance, so `grid !== existing` is false and rebuild is skipped, yet `grassGridTick = tick` claims freshness. Renderer draws grass exclusively from this grid (renderer/entityCache.ts:189-201 passes `[]` as the fallback list), so grass that spawns later (dailyGrassEcology.ts:57-65, groupEvents.ts:1744-1748) is never drawn, and grass that dies later keeps being drawn forever because the retained tick-1 shims were built with `let flags = RENDER_FLAG_ALIVE` (packRenderSoA.ts:48) and are never refreshed. Player-visible: permanent ghost grass / missing new grass after the first frame.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Have the render path force a refresh: in syncGrassRenderGridFromSoA call `syncGrassRenderGrid(undefined, ...)` (or add a `forceRebuild` parameter, or call `grassRenderGrid.reconcile(grassEntities, isGrassGridEntity)` when layout matches), so the tick-keyed cache actually updates its contents each tick.

crossFindings.title: Tree and grass sim grids are never reconciled, so mid-run spawns are invisible and dead trees are retained
crossFindings.impact: update()/reconcile() are only ever driven by syncSpatialGridEntity (grass + mobile) and by syncMobileSimGrid/syncHumanSocialGrid; tickLayerRealtime.ts:148-158 calls syncGrassRenderGrid/syncTreeGrid with a reusable instance, which no-ops. Therefore: (a) the 15 trees and 30 grass spawned by the yearly 'nature_boom' event (groupEvents.ts:1738-1748 push straight into allAlive, bypassing pushNewEntity) never enter treeGrid/grassGrid, and since findClosestInEntityGrid ignores its fallback array whenever the grid is non-null (simQueries.ts:113-117), grazers (tickLayerSystems.ts:540-548) cannot find the new grass and settlers cannot visit the new trees (humanTick.ts:1403-1412) for the rest of the session; (b) trees killed by clearTreesUnderFootprint when a building is placed (buildingPlacementActions.ts:95-98) are never removed from treeGrid, retaining one dead Entity per chopped tree for the session and tripping EntitySpatialGrid.validateInvariant ('stale dead entity') — which is never run for treeGrid because assertSpatialGridInvariants only validates grassGrid and mobileGrid (spatialGrid.ts:819-829).
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Reconcile instead of skip: `else grid.reconcile(entities, filter)` in syncTreeGrid, and add a treeGrid parameter to syncSpatialGridEntity so pushNewEntity/kill paths index trees like grass.

crossFindings.title: extractSimPrep shallow-clones entities, so nested mutable state is aliased and applySimPrep does not actually roll back
crossFindings.evidence:
entities: (state.entities ?? []).map((e) => ({ ...e })),
(contrast line 106-110, where buildings deliberately isolate `occupants` and `hotelGuestIds`)
crossFindings.impact: Entity `skills`, `friendships`, `feuds`, `childrenIds`, `childhoodFriendsIds` are mutated in place during a tick (skills.ts:37 `skills[job] = ...`, relationships.ts:105-109, residencySelection.ts:215) and are shared with the backup object, so a rollback restore keeps them. The same aliasing applies to object-valued arrays that are copied shallowly: `tradeRoutes: [...(state.tradeRoutes ?? [])]` (line 149) while tradeCaravans.ts:287-305 mutates `route.caravanLeg`/`caravanWaitTicks`/`caravansCompleted` in place, `disasters: [...(state.disasters ?? [])]` (line 150) while worldEvents.ts:299 does `d.progress++`, plus visitorGroups/rivalSettlements. Concrete path: gameWorker.ts:343-350 calls applySimPrep after a *successful* gameTick when the render buffer pool is exhausted; `state.tick`/`nextEntityId` are restored, so the next tick re-runs the same tick number and the same in-place skill/relationship gains are applied a second time (skills.ts:37 has no idempotence guard).
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Deep-clone the mutable nested fields in extractSimPrep, e.g. map entities with `({ ...e, skills: e.skills ? { ...e.skills } : undefined, friendships: e.friendships ? { ...e.friendships } : undefined, feuds: e.feuds ? { ...e.feuds } : undefined, childrenIds: e.childrenIds ? [...e.childrenIds] : undefined, childhoodFriendsIds: e.childhoodFriendsIds ? [...e.childhoodFriendsIds] : undefined })`, and use structuredClone for tradeRoutes/disasters/visitorGroups/rivalSettlements.

crossFindings.title: SimPrepKeys omits simulation state that a tick writes (yearlyStats, lifetimeStats, populationHistory)
crossFindings.impact: applySimPrep restores only its own key list, so the worker's rollback path (gameWorker.ts:339, 345, 355 — e.g. render-buffer-pool exhaustion after a completed gameTick) leaves the failed tick's year-rollover effects in place while state.tick is rewound. When the restored tick is re-run it crosses the same year boundary again, pushing a duplicate YearlyStats entry (and running the >50 shift twice) and double-counting lifetimeStats; populationHistory also gains a second sample for the same tick number. simDelta.ts:317-318 already ships yearlyStats/lifetimeStats to the main thread, so the field list exists — only the rollback backup is missing them.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Add 'yearlyStats' | 'lifetimeStats' | 'populationHistory' (and 'huntVisuals') to SimPrepKeys, extract them with structuredClone/deep copies in extractSimPrep, and assign them back in applySimPrep.

crossFindings.title: Wildkin reproduces but is absent from REPRO_WILDLIFE_TYPES, so its population cap and scarcity boost are computed from a permanently zero count
crossFindings.impact: Wildkin passes the reproduction gate (WILDLIFE_TICK_TYPES includes it, tickLayerSystems.ts:78; speciesConfig.ts:190-192 gives reproductionCooldown cd(288), threshold 200, chance 0.008) but wildlifeTypePopulation() returns 0 + 0 - 0 for it forever, so capacityFactor is always 1.0 and scarcityBoost is always the 1.55 scarcity multiplier: the intended `maxPop = 35` fallback cap never binds and wildkin breed at a permanently boosted rate once two are within 80px, growing without bound (matching the pattern the comment 'Keep the buffer bounded' style guards elsewhere exist for).
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Add EntityType.Wildkin to REPRO_WILDLIFE_TYPES (or, if wildkin is meant to be sterile, add `entity.type !== EntityType.Wildkin` to the reproduction gate and set its reproductionChance to 0).

crossFindings.title: Worker tick delta carries neither huntVisuals nor chronicleChapters, so worker-authored state never reaches the display world
crossFindings.evidence: The SimTickDelta interface lists populationHistory/yearlyStats/lifetimeStats (lines 113-115) but has no huntVisuals or chronicleChapters field; grep for those names in simDelta.ts returns nothing, and applySimTickDelta (lines 373-523) assigns no such fields.
crossFindings.impact: huntVisuals is written by sim code that runs in the worker (huntvisuals.ts:61 `state.huntVisuals.unshift(entry)` from dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:412 and humanHuntingBehavior.ts:125) and read by the renderer through RenderSnapshot.huntVisuals (renderSnapshot.ts:112 → renderer/humans.ts:353, drawn unconditionally from entityComposite.ts:42). Because the delta never carries it and GameWorkerHost applies only deltas plus invalidate/hydrate (GameWorkerHost.ts:546-548), the display world's huntVisuals stays at its last full-load value, so the hunting arrow that BUG_REPORTS/2026-08-28-hunting-projectile-visual.md was resolved for only appears in non-worker mode. chronicleChapters has the same shape: advanceValleyChronicle writes it daily in the worker (tickLayerDaily.ts:65, valleyChronicle.ts:89) but neither extract/apply delta nor prep reference it, so ValleyChroniclePanel.tsx:6 and useTransientGameFeedback.ts:83-144 (chapter moments) never see a completion until a save reload.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Add `huntVisuals` and `chronicleChapters` to SimTickDelta, copy them in extractSimTickDelta, and assign them in applySimTickDelta (and add both to SimPrepKeys for rollback symmetry).

crossFindings.title: Church 'one-time' migration runs on every load and unassigns the player's priest
crossFindings.evidence: saveLoad.ts:531 `const clearedChurchSeats = clearAutoFilledChurches(world);` and saveLoad.ts:327-328 `if (human && human.alive && human.homeBuildingId === church.id) {` / `removeWorkerTransition(human, world.buildings);`
crossFindings.impact: In a current-version save a player Church can only be staffed by the manually chosen priest, and that priest is stored exactly the way the destructive branch detects: `assignIdleWorkerToBuilding` sets `occupants=[priestId]` + `homeBuildingId=church.id` + job Priest (tests/church.manualStaffing.test.ts:107-113, tests/workerCommand.roundtrip.test.ts:143-150). Because the call is unconditional and the same-version gate (saveLoad.ts:80-82) means no pre-0.6.4 save can reach it, every load of a save with a staffed Church empties the Church and resets the priest to settler (`removeWorkerTransition` clears homeBuildingId/job/occupation). The recorded migration id only dedupes the log line (applySaveMigration, saveLoad.ts:489-494), not the destructive clear, and `assignMissingWorkers` never refills a manual workplace, so the priest stays idle after every reload. Player-visible: the priest assignment is lost on each load/save cycle.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Stop running the migration on load: delete the call at saveLoad.ts:531 (and the now-unreachable function) — or, if the migration must stay, gate it on a persisted one-time marker/legacy version instead of calling it for every 0.6.4 save.

crossFindings.title: visitorQuest is written by the sim but carried by neither the save allow-list nor the worker delta
crossFindings.evidence: visitorQuest.ts:34 `state.visitorQuest = {` ; saveLoad.ts:67-69 `for (const key of WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS) {` / `if (key in parsed) (out as Record<string, unknown>)[key] = parsed[key];` ; saveSchema.ts:16 `'visitorGroups', 'activeVillageRequest', 'villageRequestCooldownUntilDay', 'villageRequestHistory',` (no `visitorQuest` entry anywhere in the list, lines 4-26)
crossFindings.impact: The traveling-smith quest is created inside the sim (groupEvents.ts:416 -> maybeStartVisitorQuest) and expires day-by-day (visitorQuest.ts:43-50). It is not in the save payload, so saving during an active quest silently deletes it: the card (App.tsx:1545 `const q = getVisitorQuest(world);`) disappears and a later `deliverVisitorQuest` command returns false (visitorQuest.ts:55) with a valid payment in store. It is also absent from every SimTickDelta field (simDelta.ts:52-139), so in worker mode the authoritative quest never reaches the main-thread world at all: the card cannot appear and virtualPlayer's quest step (virtualPlayer.ts:847) can never fire, until the next full-world export (which only happens on save, gameLoop.ts:654-683). Same class as the documented whitelist-miss bug in tests/saveMigration.roundtrip.test.ts.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Add `visitorQuest` to WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS (the `if (key in world)` guard tolerates undefined) and add `visitorQuest?: WorldState['visitorQuest']` to SimTickDelta plus its extract/apply lines in simDelta.ts.

crossFindings.title: Compact worldMap save discards in-play terrain edits, so building efficiency changes across a reload
crossFindings.evidence: saveLoad.ts:153-159 `return {` / `seed: worldMap.seed,` ... `_compact: true as const,` and buildingPlacementActions.ts:111 `tile.type = TerrainType.Grassland;`
crossFindings.impact: Every placement mutates authoritative terrain: `clearTreesUnderFootprint` converts Forest/DarkForest to Grassland under each footprint (buildingPlacementActions.ts:100-114, called from startBuilding:162 and placeStripChain:300). The save keeps only seed/preset/size, and restoreWorldMapFromSave regenerates pristine tiles from the seed (saveLoad.ts:168-172), so those edits are lost. `getTerrainEfficiencyMultiplier` reads the tile under the building (terrainSystems.ts:59-75) and is used for production (dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:314, workshopEconomy.ts:48): a Farm on a cleared forest tile drops 1.4 -> 0.8 and a LumberMill rises 0.9 -> 1.5 after a save/load, so the same colony produces different output before and after reloading (and forest art returns under the village).
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Persist the terrain deltas (e.g. a `clearedTiles: [tx,ty][]` array in the compact worldMap payload) and re-apply them in restoreWorldMapFromSave after generateWorldMap.

crossFindings.title: Moon Howler exorcism cooldown and priest-flee deadline are never persisted
crossFindings.evidence: moonHowler.ts:693 `state.lastMoonHowlerExorcismTick = state.tick;` and moonHowler.ts:812 `state.moonHowlerPriestsFleeUntil = state.tick + MOON_HOWLER_EXORCISM_INTERVAL_HOURS * TICKS_PER_HOUR;` — neither key appears in WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS (saveSchema.ts:4-26) or in SimPrepKeys (simPrep.ts:10-87).
crossFindings.impact: Both are tick deadlines read by later decisions: `const last = state.lastMoonHowlerExorcismTick ?? -9999;` (moonHowler.ts:673) rate-limits the rite, and `state.tick < (state.moonHowlerPriestsFleeUntil ?? -1)` suppresses it when priests fled (moonHowler.ts:659, humanTick.ts:609). Saving and reloading on a full-moon night therefore resets the cooldown so the Church rite can be re-attempted immediately on the same night (save-scumming re-rolls `rollMoonHowlerRiteOutcome`, can kill/cure repeatedly), and a priest who just watched a colleague die stops being scared after a reload. Being absent from simPrep, they also survive a failed tick/command rollback.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Add 'lastMoonHowlerExorcismTick' and 'moonHowlerPriestsFleeUntil' to WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS and to SimPrepKeys/extractSimPrep/applySimPrep.

crossFindings.title: Workforce/mood HUD fields written every tick are never transferred to the main thread
crossFindings.evidence: gameTick.ts:243-244 `state.workingSettlers = workforceCounts.working;` / `state.idleSettlers = workforceCounts.idle;` and simDelta.ts:62-63 `humanPopulation: number;` / `maxHumanPopulation: number;` (the neighbouring derived counts exist, but no workingSettlers/idleSettlers/villageHappiness/villageCanHeat anywhere in SimTickDelta, lines 52-139)
crossFindings.impact: In worker mode the main thread's world is only advanced by applySimTickDelta (gameLoop.ts:546), so these fields keep their creation values forever: worldGen.ts:605-606 sets workingSettlers/idleSettlers to 0 and villageHappiness is undefined. PopulationPanel.tsx:110-111 (`const working = state.workingSettlers; const idle = state.idleSettlers;`) shows 0 working / 0 idle and line 154 renders village mood as `Math.round(state.villageHappiness ?? 50)` = 50 permanently; citizenOverview.ts:171 reads `world.villageCanHeat !== false` = true regardless of the worker's winter heating result (dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:111). They are in simPrep (rollback) but in no save key and no delta, so only a save-time full export refreshes them.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Add workingSettlers, idleSettlers, villageHappiness and villageCanHeat to the SimTickDelta interface and to extractSimTickDelta/applySimTickDelta (all are cheap scalars already present in simPrep).

crossFindings.title: chronicleChapters and huntVisuals are written in the worker but omitted from the tick delta
crossFindings.evidence: valleyChronicle.ts:89 `state.chronicleChapters = [...(state.chronicleChapters ?? []), ch.id];` and huntvisuals.ts:61 `state.huntVisuals.unshift(entry);` — neither field exists in SimTickDelta (simDelta.ts:52-139); chronicleChapters is in WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS (saveSchema.ts:15) but huntVisuals is in neither save list.
crossFindings.impact: Both are produced only inside the sim (valleyChronicle from the daily layer; addHuntVisual from humanHuntingBehavior.ts:125 / dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:412, pruned at tickLayerRealtime.ts:238) but are read from the main-thread world: ValleyChroniclePanel.tsx:6 and useTransientGameFeedback.ts:83 (`world.chronicleChapters`) and the renderer via renderSnapshot.ts:112 `huntVisuals: world.huntVisuals` built from `this.world` at gameLoop.ts:943. With the worker active (the default, isGameWorkerEnabled) new chronicle chapters and hunt arrow visuals never reach the UI: the chronicle panel/chapter moments stay empty and hunt animations never draw until a save exports the whole world.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Add `chronicleChapters?: string[]` and `huntVisuals?: WorldState['huntVisuals']` to SimTickDelta and populate/apply them, or document explicitly that they are main-thread-only and rebuild them on the main thread.

crossFindings.title: extractSimPrep shallow-copies entities/elements, so rollback cannot undo nested mutations
crossFindings.evidence: simPrep.ts:102-103 `// Clone entity objects shallowly to decouple from in-place property mutations` / `entities: (state.entities ?? []).map((e) => ({ ...e })),` (the occupant array of buildings is explicitly isolated at line 108, but entity nested state is not)
crossFindings.impact: Nested objects keep the same reference between the backup and the live world, so gameWorker.ts:228/360 `applySimPrep(world, prepBackup)` restores only top-level properties. In-place nested writers during ticks/commands include skills.ts:37 `skills[job] = ...`, humanLifecycle.ts:40 `parent.childrenIds.push(childId)`, relationships.ts:108 `a.friendships[friendKey(b.id)] = next`, groupEvents.ts:516 `group.daysLeft--`, rivalProfiles.ts:89 `ledger.food -= 5`, and renffrOmen.letters. If a tick or command throws after one of these (e.g. a birth is rolled back at entity level but the parent's `childrenIds` still lists the removed child), the authoritative worker world stays mutated although the tick/command is reported failed; the next delta ships the 'failed' change to the player, or a retry applies it twice.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Deep-copy the backed-up slices: `entities: structuredClone(state.entities ?? [])` (or clone the nested fields skills/childrenIds/friendships/feuds explicitly) and clone element objects of visitorGroups/rivalSettlements (e.g. `.map(g => ({...g}))`) in extractSimPrep.

crossFindings.title: simPrep omits fields the tick writes, so a failed tick is only partially rolled back
crossFindings.evidence: gameTick.ts:84-86 `state.yearlyStats.push(yearlyStat);` / `if (state.yearlyStats.length > 50) state.yearlyStats.shift();` / `state.lifetimeStats = updateLifetimeStats(state, state.lifetimeStats);` and tickLayerRealtime.ts:204 `state.populationHistory.push(snapshot);` — SimPrepKeys (simPrep.ts:10-87) contains none of yearlyStats, lifetimeStats, populationHistory, activeEvent, notifications, bigNews, chronicleChapters, economyLedger, foodHistory or appliedSaveMigrations.
crossFindings.impact: The declared purpose of extractSimPrep is failure recovery (simPrep.ts:7-9), but a tick that throws after the year-rollover block is only partially restored: `tick`/`dayInYear` come back (they are in the list) while yearlyStats/lifetimeStats keep the first application. The tick error then falls back to main-thread ticks (gameLoop.ts:385-404 via GameWorkerHost.handleMessage -> onWorkerFault), the next gameTick re-crosses the same day boundary and re-runs recordYearlyStats/updateLifetimeStats, so the year is recorded twice and lifetime birth/death/marriage totals are double-counted. The spurious populationHistory sample survives too and is shipped to the player because populationHistory is in the delta.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Add at least populationHistory, yearlyStats, lifetimeStats, activeEvent, notifications, chronicleChapters and bigNews to SimPrepKeys and to the extractSimPrep/applySimPrep bodies (copy the arrays, e.g. `[...(state.yearlyStats ?? [])]`).

crossFindings.title: All legacy save-migration branches are unreachable behind the exact-version gate
crossFindings.evidence: saveLoad.ts:80-81 `if (parsed._version !== GAME_VERSION) { return { valid: false }; }` versus saveLoad.ts:478 `const forceAgeMigration = saveVersion === '0.4' || saveVersion === '0.4.1';` and the `saveVersion === '0.4' ... '0.5.0'` blocks at lines 496-537
crossFindings.impact: parseSaveJson rejects every save whose `_version` is not 0.6.4 (a policy pinned by tests/saveVersion.gate.test.ts:19-23), so loadGameFromParsed can only ever see `saveVersion === GAME_VERSION`: forceAgeMigration is always false, the v0.4/v0.4.1/v0.4.2/v0.5.0/v0.5.1 applySaveMigration branches and the legacy `clearAutoFilledChurches` call can never apply to a real save. This is dead code that hides the fact that the only remaining same-version repairs are the iron backfills at lines 460-466, and it is the reason the destructive Church block above runs unconditionally instead of behind its version check.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Delete the unreachable legacy branches (and the forceAgeMigration/saveVersion comparisons), or replace them with an explicit, documented same-version backfill list; keep only migrations that can apply to a GAME_VERSION payload.

crossFindings.title: Missing _ticksPerDay defaults to the legacy 24-tick day and rescales every tick deadline 3x
crossFindings.evidence: saveLoad.ts:344-346 `const savedTicksPerDay = typeof parsed._ticksPerDay === 'number' && parsed._ticksPerDay > 0` / `? (parsed._ticksPerDay as number)` / `: LEGACY_TICKS_PER_DAY;`
crossFindings.impact: The version gate and the cadence field are validated separately: parseSaveJson accepts a payload that has the right `_version` but no `_ticksPerDay` (exactly the minimal object used in tests/saveVersion.gate.test.ts:15), and loadGameFromParsed then treats it as a 24-tick legacy save, multiplying `world.tick` and every absolute deadline by TICKS_PER_DAY/24 = 3 in migrateTickTimeline (world.tick:226, pregnancyProgress:245, prisonerUntilTick/scandalCooldownUntilTick/griefUntilTick/hotelStayUntilTick:238-241, raid/diplomacy/festival/election expiries:260-287). A hand-edited or partially-written same-version file therefore loads with a tripled calendar and pregnancies/prison sentences three times too long instead of being rejected.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Require the cadence for a GAME_VERSION payload: reject when `typeof parsed._ticksPerDay !== 'number'` (or derive the scale from `_version` and only use LEGACY_TICKS_PER_DAY for explicitly legacy versions).

crossFindings.title: updateStorageCaps is never called: live storage caps and food spoilage never recompute (Barn/Silo/Wood Storehouse deliver nothing)
crossFindings.evidence: src/game/economy.ts:8 `export function updateStorageCaps(state: WorldState) {` — its only other mention in all of src is a doc string (`src/game/simulation/decisionRegistry.ts:103 ... economy.ts — addResource, applyFoodSpoilage, updateStorageCaps`), and its only caller anywhere is `tests/economyAudit.storageCaps.test.ts:44 updateStorageCaps(w);`. Live caps therefore come from `src/game/worldGen.ts:577 const storageMax = { wood: 1000, stone: 500, food: 1000, gold: 2000, iron: 500 };` and `src/game/worldGen.ts:618 foodSpoilageRate: 0.03,` (only saves/simPrep/simDelta carry these fields afterwards).
crossFindings.impact: As §6 forbids duplicate rules and the decision registry lists `storageMax`/`foodSpoilageRate` as daily production writes, the game runs on frozen world-gen values: Barns (`src/game/buildings.ts:205 '... extends wood storage +300'`), Siloes (`buildings.ts:218 'Passive food storage bonus.'`) and Wood Storehouses (`buildings.ts:231 '+800 wood storage'`) add no storage at all, spoilage stays 3% instead of the audited 2% (and never drops to 0.8% with a Silo), and gold stays capped at 2000 (shown in `src/components/GameHeader.tsx:315`) instead of 20000 — exactly the numbers the passing test asserts but nothing produces.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Call `updateStorageCaps(state)` from the daily economy owner — first statement of `tickStaticDaily` (src/game/dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:238-242, beside `applyFoodSpoilage`) — which `decisionRegistry.ts:113` already documents as `scheduledFrom: 'tickLayerDaily'`.

crossFindings.title: Second Moon Howler spawn path: the debug command curses a settler even while a cursed Howler already exists
crossFindings.evidence: src/game/settlerInteractionActions.ts:110-115 `const candidates = state.entities.filter((entity) => entity.alive && canMoonHowlerCurse(entity)); const pick = candidates[Math.floor(Math.random() * candidates.length)]; if (pick) { ... curseMoonHowler(pick);` — no `countActiveMoonHowlerCurses`/`activeCursed === 0` gate, unlike the sole owner `src/game/moonHowler.ts:158-164 ... activeCursed === 0 && humanCount > 5 && hourOfDay === NIGHT_START && isFullMoonNight(...) && rng() < MOON_HOWLER_REPLACEMENT_CHANCE`. It is a shipped worker op (`src/game/simWorker/commands.ts:416-417 case 'spawnMoonHowlerDebug': return spawnMoonHowlerDebug(world);`) driven by an unconditional UI button (`src/components/tabPanels/MoreTabPanel.tsx:225-231`, wired at `src/App.tsx:1942`).
crossFindings.impact: Because `canMoonHowlerCurse` (moonHowler.ts:253-263) only rejects the already-cursed settler, pressing the button while one cursed Howler lives curses a second living settler, breaking §5 'There is at most one living cursed Moon Howler' (detected by `src/game/simulation/simulationInvariants.ts:250-258`) and §3's single owner for curse/spawn (moonHowler.ts). It also ignores the §4 `full-moon-event` cadence — a Howler can be created at any hour of any day.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Add the debug entry point to `moonHowler.ts` as a named transition that returns early when `countActiveMoonHowlerCurses(state.entities) > 0` (and gate it on `import.meta.env.DEV`), then have `spawnMoonHowlerDebug` delegate to it.

crossFindings.title: Hand-rolled storage-cap clamps instead of addCappedResource: raid spoils go negative and subtract resources when stock is above the cap
crossFindings.evidence: src/game/frontierCombat.ts:682-689 `const room = state.storageMax.food - state.resources.food; gained.food = Math.min(room, spoils.food); state.resources.food += gained.food;` (identical shape for wood at 686-689 / stone at 691-695), where the declared owner clamps headroom at zero: `src/game/resourceUtils.ts:43 const headroom = Number.isFinite(max) ? Math.max(0, max - current) : amount;` in `addCappedResource` (:38-48). The same hand-rolled rule recurs at `src/game/groupEvents.ts:525-526, 543, 549, 1220, 1236, 1247, 1787, 1794` (e.g. `:549 state.resources.wood = Math.min(state.storageMax.wood, state.resources.wood + wood);`), `src/game/rivalEvents.ts:244`, `src/game/visitorQuest.ts:61` and `src/game/tradeCaravans.ts:85-86`.
crossFindings.impact: Stock legitimately exceeds the cap because `src/game/buildingPlacementActions.ts:180-182 refundHalfBuildingCost` adds wood/stone/gold with no cap check (called on strip-build replacement at line 280). With `resources.wood` above `storageMax.wood`, `room` is negative, `gained.wood = Math.min(negative, spoils.wood)` is negative, and `state.resources.wood += gained.wood` therefore DELETES wood on a successful raid while `formatLootParts(gained)` (line 1167) logs a negative haul — the opposite of the comment `/** Add spoils ... (respects storage caps). */`. The `Math.min` variants silently destroy the same excess instead of leaving it untouched.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Use the owner helper in all these sites: `gained.wood = addCappedResource(state, 'wood', spoils.wood)` and `addCappedResource(state, key, amount)` in groupEvents/rivalEvents/visitorQuest (import from './resourceUtils').

crossFindings.title: groupEvents privately re-implements the affordability, deduction and storage-headroom rules with weaker guards
crossFindings.evidence: src/game/groupEvents.ts:1313-1315 `function storageRoom(state: WorldState, type: keyof WorldState['resources']): number { return Math.max(0, (state.storageMax[type] as number) - (state.resources[type] as number)); }` vs `src/game/resourceUtils.ts:24-28 getAvailableStorageHeadroom`; src/game/groupEvents.ts:1321-1326 `canPayTradeCost` vs `src/game/resourceUtils.ts:65-73 canAfford`; src/game/groupEvents.ts:1328-1334 `applyTradeCost` vs `src/game/resourceUtils.ts:76-84 consumeResources`. The module already imports the owner helper: `src/game/groupEvents.ts:19 import { addCappedResource } from './resourceUtils';`.
crossFindings.impact: Two owners for one economy rule, and the private copies lack the `?? 0` guards: `canPayTradeCost` tests `(state.resources[key] as number) < cost`, so a missing key passes (undefined < n is false) and `applyTradeCost` then writes `Math.max(0, (state.resources[key] as number) - cost)` = NaN into `state.resources[key]`; `storageRoom` returns NaN for a missing `storageMax[type]`, so the village-request gate at line 184 (`storageRoom(state, 'food') < VILLAGE_REQUEST_PROVISIONS_FOOD`) is false and an unaffordable/over-cap accept can pass. `canAfford`/`deductResource` cannot do either.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Delete `storageRoom`, `canFitPurchase`, `canPayTradeCost`, `applyTradeCost` and import `getAvailableStorageHeadroom`, `canAfford`, `deductResource` from './resourceUtils'.

crossFindings.title: assignAllWorkers: dead second auto-staffing entry point that also fills manual-staff buildings
crossFindings.evidence: src/game/workforce.ts:580-584 `export function assignAllWorkers(humans: Entity[], buildings: Building[]): void { const alive = prepareWorkforce(humans, buildings); staffConstructionCrews(alive, buildings); staffJobBuildings(alive, buildings, true, undefined); }` — the only live entry point is `src/game/workforce.ts:570-578 assignMissingWorkers(... staffJobBuildings(alive, buildings, false, venueSchedules))`. `assignAllWorkers` is referenced nowhere except the barrel: `src/game/gameEngine.ts:113 assignAllWorkers,` (verified across all of src and tests).
crossFindings.impact: `includeManualStaff = true` skips the guard `src/game/workforce.ts:558 if (!includeManualStaff && isManualStaffingBuilding(building)) continue;`, so this path would generically auto-fill manual buildings (the Church priest selection §5 protects) and it passes `venueSchedules = undefined`, bypassing the Tavern/Hotel auto-staff targets. It is a second workforce rule exposed on the public barrel with no caller.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Delete `assignAllWorkers` and its `gameEngine.ts:113` re-export, leaving `assignMissingWorkers` as the sole auto-staffing entry point.

crossFindings.title: Seven unreferenced legacy chat/courtship implementations survive the social-feel extraction
crossFindings.evidence: Across all src/*.ts, src/*.tsx and tests/*.ts the following names have exactly one occurrence (their own definition): `startHumanChat` (src/game/humanChat.ts:343), `maybeHumanChat` (:485), `maybeHousemateChat` (:509), `startPairedHumanChat` (:529), `pickCourtshipPair` (:541), `pickChatPhrase` (:546), `truncateChatForBubble` (:556). `pickCourtshipPair` also discards both parameters: `:541-543 export function pickCourtshipPair(_entityId: number, _tick: number): readonly [string, string] { return ['Walk with me?', 'Gladly.']; }`. The live owner path is `maybeDialogueChat`, used by the extracted social-feel owner `src/game/simulation/humanSocial.ts:7 (import) / :28 maybeDialogueChat(...)`.
crossFindings.impact: A second, parallel chat/courtship-phrase implementation (hardcoded pairs, legacy `_legacyDurationTicks`/`_durationTicks` knobs, `@deprecated` banners) remains exported, so a future caller can bypass the dialogue-tree owner and its `isDialogueBusy`/duration bookkeeping; the underscore parameters hide that the courtship pair is no longer chosen from a table.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Delete the seven deprecated functions from src/game/humanChat.ts (no importers exist anywhere).

crossFindings.title: isLivingMarriagePartner duplicates moonHowler.isSettlerRelationshipEntity verbatim (with a third variant elsewhere)
