crossFindings.evidence: src/game/humanLifecycleCleanup.ts:189-193 `function isLivingMarriagePartner(entity: Entity | undefined): boolean { if (!entity?.alive) return false; if (entity.type === EntityType.Human) return true; return entity.type === EntityType.Werewolf && !!entity.moonHowlerCursed; }` is the same rule as `src/game/moonHowler.ts:270-274 export function isSettlerRelationshipEntity(entity: Entity | undefined): entity is Entity { ... }` (used at src/game/humanTick.ts:227 and :265); a third copy lives at `src/game/residencyReconciliation.ts:105-109 isResidenceOccupantEntity` (same plus `!entity.faction`). The file already imports from the owner: `src/game/humanLifecycleCleanup.ts:3 import { finalizeMoonHowlerDeath } from './moonHowler';`.
crossFindings.impact: The 'a cursed settler still counts as a marriage/social partner' rule has three owners. If the Moon Howler form rules change (e.g. aligning with `isActiveMoonHowler`, which also requires `alive`), `isLivingMarriagePartner` will not follow, and `reconcileOrphanedMarriages` (:205) can start clearing or keeping marriages differently from the social lookups it mirrors (a §5-adjacent marriage/pregnancy state divergence).
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Delete `isLivingMarriagePartner` and use the imported `isSettlerRelationshipEntity` from './moonHowler'.

crossFindings.title: countArmedMilitia: dead militia-count rule that disagrees with the militia owner
crossFindings.evidence: src/game/frontierCombat.ts:193-197 `export function countArmedMilitia(state: WorldState, entities: Entity[]): number { const armed = hasIronSpears(state) || hasStoneSpears(state); if (!armed) return 0; return entities.filter((e) => e.alive && isPlayerHuman(e) && !e.isJuvenile).length; }` — its only other occurrence is the barrel `src/game/gameEngine.ts:152 countArmedMilitia,`; the live owner is `src/game/militiaBalance.ts:91-93 countAdultSettlers` reached via `src/game/frontierCombat.ts:199-201 getMilitiaStrength → computeMilitiaBreakdown`, whose tier ladder handles swords: `src/game/militiaBalance.ts:147 if (spearTier === 'sword') {` (and `:118 getMilitiaSpearTier`, `:120 getMilitiaSpearMultiplier`).
crossFindings.impact: This second militia rule is both unreachable and wrong: with iron swords researched (`hasIronSpears`/`hasStoneSpears` at combat.ts:119 terms) it returns 0 militia for a fully armed village, and it counts prisoners/children-free adults with no shields, guards or barricades. Reusing the exported name (it is on the public barrel) would feed raid math a number the owner never produced.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Delete `countArmedMilitia` and its `gameEngine.ts:152` re-export; use `computeMilitiaBreakdown(...).adultCount` where a raw count is needed.

crossFindings.title: Second calendar definition: DAYS_PER_YEAR / MONTHS_PER_YEAR / DAYS_PER_MONTH re-declared locally
crossFindings.evidence: src/game/villageLeadership.ts:34-36 `export const DAYS_PER_MONTH = 30; export const MONTHS_PER_YEAR = 12; export const DAYS_PER_YEAR = DAYS_PER_MONTH * MONTHS_PER_YEAR; // 360 days` shadows the canonical `src/game/gameConstants.ts:82 export const DAYS_PER_YEAR = Time.DAYS_PER_YEAR;` / `src/game/dayCycleClock.ts:6 export const DAYS_PER_YEAR = Time?.DAYS_PER_YEAR ?? 360;`, re-exported through `src/game/dayCycle.ts:13`. The local copy drives election timing: `src/game/villageLeadership.ts:46 return GOSSIP_MONTHS * DAYS_PER_MONTH * TICKS_PER_DAY;` and `:385 state.year + (state.dayInYear ?? 0) / DAYS_PER_YEAR`.
crossFindings.impact: Election campaign length and the years-until-election figure derive from a private 30×12 calendar, so retuning `Time.DAYS_PER_YEAR`/`DAYS_PER_SEASON` in the declared single source (gameConstants.ts) would silently desync elections from the world calendar. No test imports this constant, so the drift would be invisible.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Import `DAYS_PER_YEAR` from './dayCycle' and declare the month pair once (or derive `MONTHS_PER_YEAR = DAYS_PER_YEAR / DAYS_PER_MONTH`).

crossFindings.title: Dead/duplicated Moon Howler window helpers (next-full-moon, cure tick, transform, revert)
crossFindings.evidence: No reference exists anywhere in src/ or tests/ for `src/game/moonHowler.ts:140 export function daysUntilNextFullMoon(colonyDay: number): number {` or `:245 export function isMoonHowlerCureTick(colonyDay: number, hourOfDay: number): boolean { return isMoonHowlerCureWindow(colonyDay, hourOfDay); }`; `isMoonHowlerCureWindow` (:240-242) and `shouldMoonHowlerTransform` (:219-221) have identical bodies `return isFullMoonNight(colonyDay, hourOfDay);`, and `isMoonHowlerRevertTick` (:232-234) is referenced only by `tests/moonHowler.cureWindow.test.ts:45` (production `syncMoonHowlerForms` at :881-916 uses the window, never the revert hour).
crossFindings.impact: Four exported names encode one full-moon window rule, so a reader cannot tell which is authoritative; the deprecated alias can drift from `isMoonHowlerCureWindow`, and the test pins a `isMoonHowlerRevertTick(6)` contract that the simulation does not actually call (reverts happen through `shouldMoonHowlerTransform`). This is a §3 'one owner per decision' smell inside the declared owner module.
crossFindings.suggestedChange: Delete `daysUntilNextFullMoon`, `isMoonHowlerCureTick` and `isMoonHowlerRevertTick`; keep one window predicate (`isMoonHowlerCureWindow`) and have the test assert `shouldMoonHowlerTransform`/`isMoonHowlerCureWindow`.

groupNotes.notes:
VERDICT PER FILE
- src/game/gameTick.ts — layer order/cadence matches SIMULATION_AUTHORITY §4 and tests/gameTick.layerOrder.test.ts (72/4/18/72, realtime first); calendar rollover, deathsThisTick/untracked-spawn cache invalidation and the entityByType rebuild conditions verified correct. Only the winter-heating persistence gap (F1) and a no-op scan (notes) found.
- src/game/tickLayerRealtime.ts — grid sync order, moon-howler byType/playerHumans/predator refresh, bounded populationHistory/particle/text buffers all consistent; no finding (the Moon-Howler gated residence re-sync is discussed below).
- src/game/tickLayerSystems.ts — multi-tick step scaling is correct for energy, flash, combatTicks, reproduction cooldown, breeding probability and wander probability; predation/counter-attack/forgiveness paths unindex and grid-sync their casualties. Findings F2 (off-screen throttle) and F5 (unreachable growth branch).
- src/game/tickLayerAssign.ts — 18-tick = 4x/day cadence correct; filters dead entities via prepareWorkforce/assignMissingResidences internals; passes playerHumans as assignees and all Humans as genealogy; no finding.
- src/game/tickLayerDaily.ts — composition is once-per-day and does not duplicate another owner (friendships/feuds in relationships.ts, youth love and conception in humanRelationships.ts, leadership in leaderHouse/villageLeadership, requests in groupEvents via dailyWorldEvents). Finding F6 (dead guards only).
- src/game/simFocus.ts — focus math, EntityType bucketing and draw-bucket construction are correct and total over EntityType; only the OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE unit mismatch (half of F2).
- src/game/simHelpers.ts — getSeason/seasonBlendForDay/getMultiplier/addReputation/getPollutionProductionMultiplier match their documented formulas and clamps; no finding.
- src/game/gameLoop.ts — worker protocol, optimistic-command replacement/revert and worker-authoritative delta handling match the §2 amendment; findings F3, F4, F7.
- src/game/gameEngine.ts — pure compatibility barrel; verified the re-exported modules/symbols exist and the docstring matches intent. No findings (it does publish tickWildlife/tickGrassDaily as public entry points — see below).

DID NOT RUN VERIFICATION: this was a read-only audit; I did not execute the test suite, typecheck or a build, so no pass/fail claim is made. Every claim above is from reading the code and its call sites; the tests listed in filesReviewed were read only to identify intentional behavior (notably tests/gameTick.layerOrder.test.ts, which locks 72/4/18 and the four-layer order, and tests/dayCycle.cadence.test.ts, which locks OFFSCREEN_HUMAN_THROTTLE = 8*TICKS_PER_HOUR).

UNRESOLVED / DESIGN QUESTIONS
1. Worker mode loses seeded determinism. Only worldGen.initGame calls setSimSeed + enableSeededGlobalRandom (worldGen.ts:568-570) and src/game/simWorker/** contains no simRng reference. Because the worker only ever receives a world via importSave/syncWorld, every Math.random() in tickLayerSystems (wolf recruitment line 104, breeding 706/720, wander 575-576, howl lines 474/521) and tickMoonHowlerCycle is the unseeded native generator in production worker mode, while the same code is seeded in main-thread mode and in tests/deterministicSeed.test.ts. Needs an owner decision (seed the worker on 'init' with the world seed) — reported as a note because the fix belongs to the worker entry point, not to this group's files.
2. tickLayerRealtime.ts:117-123 re-derives every residence's occupants from residenceBuildingId on every tick while a Moon Howler is in werewolf form (an O(population) scan in the realtime path). I could not find a case where the assign layer actually leaves it stale for a transformed howler (transformToWerewolfForm clears residenceBuildingId, and moonHowler itself re-syncs on transform/revert/cure), except a legacy save loaded mid-full-moon-night where migrateLegacyMoonHowler leaves a cursed Werewolf holding a residenceBuildingId; in that case this block is the only repair because tickLayerAssign's bucket is Humans-only. Confirm whether that legacy repair is the intent (if not, the block is redundant per-tick assignment work).
3. gameTick.ts:107-111 re-derives entity.age for cursed humans on every tick (full alive scan) although humanTick.ts:292-303 is the daily age owner and, for the adults that can be cursed (canMoonHowlerCurse requires age >= 18), the school-age multiplier it drops cannot apply, so the write is numerically a no-op. Not reported as a finding (no behavioural difference found), but it looks like leftover code from an older form-swap bug and could be deleted or scoped to the transformed entity.
4. gameLoop.applyAction's closure branch (gameLoop.ts:601-626) is unreachable from shipped UI: every applyGameAction call site passes a WorkerCommand (all 40+ in App.tsx, plus useVirtualPlayer). With a worker active it is rejected with a console error, so the legacy path is effectively dead; and isSimWorkerBooting() (gameLoop.ts:410) has no consumer, which is what makes finding F4 reachable.
5. simWorker/simPrep.ts does not back up populationHistory or yearlyStats/lifetimeStats, so a rolled-back worker tick keeps a spurious population sample and (at a year boundary) a duplicated yearly stat. Not reported because a tick fault leads GameLoop to dispose the worker and re-authoritative from the main-thread world, so the half-rolled-back worker state is discarded; worth a defensive addition if rollback is ever used to keep the worker alive.
6. Question of intent for simFocus.seasonBlendForDay: the `until <= 0` skip means the exact season-boundary day returns null (no blend) even though it is 'within blendDays' of the boundary; the renderer (renderer/terrain.ts:130-132) then bakes the pure new-season palette, which is visually continuous, so I treated it as intentional.

NO ISSUES FOUND (verified, worth recording): the byType WeakMap cache cannot go stale across command/delta boundaries (all command implementations structuredClone the world, and gameTick rebuilds on death/spawn/type-change/day); killHuman/death cleanup keeps occupants, partnerId and childrenIds consistent with the fact that gameTick drops dead entities from state.entities each tick; workforce/residence helpers all re-filter `alive` so the tick-start playerHumans snapshot used by the assign layer cannot assign a corpse; road/bridge/well/hospital flags only count completed, non-rival buildings; markWildlifeDead splices byType and grid entries so the hunt/mate/graze queries cannot pick a corpse.

UNRESOLVED / NEEDS A DESIGN DECISION
1. Who owns the per-tick position integration for pathing entities? `steerWithPath` both moves the entity and leaves vx/vy set (pathfinding.ts:341-346) while its own docstring (line 298) tells callers not to move it again. humanMovement.ts:150 returns false on 'path' and humanTick.ts:1467 then integrates vx/vy again (road multiplier included), so commuting settlers also advance ~2x on blocked routes; hotelStay adds an explicit third move. I reported only the hotelStay instance (unambiguous inside one function); the humanMovement/humanTick half needs one decision: make steerWithPath set velocity only, or zero vx/vy after a 'path' result.
2. moonHowlerSaved omits pregnancyDueProgress (moonHowler.ts:336-361, restored at 422-424), so a cursed pregnant settler returns pregnant with no due date. Which owner repairs it (howler snapshot vs pregnancy owner) is a design call; I reported the humanLifecycle fallback because that line is in this group, but the root cause is outside it.
3. hospitalCare.findStaffedHospital (hospitalCare.ts:13-21) has no importer anywhere in src/ or tests/; humanTick builds its staffedHospitals list inline (humanTick.ts:248-252). Dead export — delete it or route humanTick through it.
4. Whether a stillbirth or a Wildkin birth should count in birthsCompletedThisInterval is a diagnostics/product decision (my finding 7 assumes the documented "only at a completed birth" reading).
5. Doctor treatment cadence needs a designer decision: is treatment a continuous per-tick effect (then scale it by PER_TICK_RATE_SCALE) or a per-hour action (then gate it on isStartOfClockHour)?
6. Not reported: `apprenticeships` clears master.apprenticeId when the apprentice is missing, but the existing-apprentice path (lines 62-66) never re-checks ownership, so a pair whose owner-side link was cleared can be taught by two masters; and an apprentice who turns adult is still taught forever. Not reachable from current writers (apprenticeId/apprenticeOfId are only set together), so I left it out. Likewise skills.getWorkerSkillMultiplier divides by the raw occupants length, so stale ids dilute the average, and settlerTraits.pickTrait falls back to the male-leaning weight set when gender is undefined (never called that way today).

SAVE PERSISTENCE: no gap found for this group. Entities and buildings are persisted whole (WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS 'entities'/'buildings'), so friendships/feuds/traits/schoolDays/schoolTicksToday/educated/apprenticeId(+OfId)/hotelGuestIds/hotelStayBuildingId survive; the tick-valued fields these files write (griefUntilTick, hotelStayUntilTick, pregnancyProgress inside moonHowlerSaved) are scaled by migrateTickTimeline (saveLoad.ts:236-252); simDelta sends full aliveEntities (simDelta.ts:286), so those entity fields reach the main thread.

PER-FILE VERDICT
- simulation/humanLifecycle.ts — the birth owner is well structured and clears pregnancy state correctly, but I found the posthumous-bastard mislabel, the unsynced newborn residence, the misplaced births diagnostic, the due-progress fallback and unseeded birth rolls.
- simulation/humanMovement.ts — deterministic helpers; movement math correct; only the cross-file 'path' integration question (notes 1) remains.
- simulation/humanNeeds.ts — meal rule, exhaustion death, hunt yield and energy-loss modifiers all behave as their comments promise; no findings.
- simulation/humanSocial.ts — correct; lower-id pair roll prevents same-tick double fire; no findings.
- humanLifecycleCleanup.ts — death cleanup is otherwise sound (occupants, widowing, grief, orphan adoption); the reconcileOrphanedMarriages guard cannot repair the 'married' + no-partner state, and reconcileFamilyReferencesAfterRemoval erases an unborn child's father id.
- relationships.ts — daily pulse respects the documented pair budget and is symmetric; friendships are never pruned, so dead friends keep buffing energy.
- socialLife.ts — opinionated but internally consistent per-person day rolls; no findings.
- relationshipDiagnostics.ts — counters/snapshot semantics match the documented truth rule; module-global state is worker-local and unused by src consumers; no findings.
- humanStatus.ts — read-only projection, no sim writes, no findings.
- citizenId.ts — no findings.
- citizenOverview.ts — presentation-only aggregation; no findings.
- familyTree.ts — pure reads; no findings.

Unresolved / design questions:
1. All authored stories share one flaw: storyEvents.tickPendingStoryEvents (storyEvents.ts:155-160) silently drops an expired card, while weddingDiplomacy stamps FLAG_OFFERED at offer time (line 101) and only pushes stage 2 when FLAG_STATUS is gift_sent/declined (line 258). An unanswered stage-1 card therefore consumes the one-time story slot forever, and an unanswered stage-2 card leaves FLAG_STATUS = gift_sent permanently. This is systemic across the authored-story family, so I did not raise it as a group finding; it needs a product decision (resolve-with-default on expiry vs. re-offer).
2. getWeddingDiplomacyChoiceEligibility is status-blind: it gates choice ids by resource without checking FLAG_STATUS, while resolveWeddingDiplomacy routes by status, so it can report ok:false for an answer the resolver would accept (stage-1 id while in stage 2) and ok:true for a stage-2 id that resolveStage1 would treat as 'decline'. Only reachable through a consumer that sends off-card ids (the bot uses card choices), so I left it out; a `storyFlag(state, FLAG_STATUS)` switch would make the mirrored contract exact.
3. Dead/unused API in this group: getActiveElectionPromises and PromiseDetail-style progress (electionPromises.ts:161) and isElectionCeremonyActive (villageLeadership.ts:418) have no consumers anywhere in src/ or tests/, and setNewLeaderPromise (villageLeadership.ts:1026) is an unreferenced legacy hook - the promise progress is never shown to the player even though promises are recorded and evaluated. 4. tickElectionPromises is invoked three times per colony day (tickLayerDaily.ts:62, dailyWorldEvents.ts:100 via tickLeaderPromise, dailyWorldEvents.ts:131). It is idempotent (the evaluated flag short-circuits), so this is redundant rather than wrong, but the triple wiring is easy to get out of sync.

CHANGELOG.md:468-476 states the 7 files "now form the only dialogue bank", so I treated the exclusion as intentional and did not file it — but 41 authored trees (incl. all pregnancy/family content) are unreachable; please confirm these are retired rather than accidentally orphaned.
2. `recordGuidedCampaignChoice` (guidedCampaign.ts:120) is dispatched and validated (commands.ts:267, 368) but no component ever sends it — I grepped `choiceId` across src and only the story/raid/diplomacy handlers and `virtualPlayer.ts` (which does not use it) appear. So `GuidedCampaignState.choices` is always empty and the journal's choice records are a prepared-but-unwired path; treated as a missing feature, not a finding.
3. `winter_watch` uses `dayInYear >= 250` while winter starts at `DAYS_PER_SEASON * 3 = 270` (simHelpers.ts:11-14). 'Prepare for winter' firing in late autumn looks deliberate and tests/tutorialCampaign.test.ts:92 locks the 250 threshold, so I did not file it — confirm 250 is the intended trigger.
4. `downloadTextFile` (eventLogExport.ts:56) calls `URL.revokeObjectURL(url)` synchronously right after `anchor.click()`. This is the common pattern and I have no evidence of a real failure, so it is noted only; if downloads ever silently fail in a target browser, revoking inside a `setTimeout` is the usual fix.
5. Preference plumbing is split: `eventLogExport.ts:105` owns its own `wilderfolk_export_chronicle_on_save` key with raw `localStorage`, and `useGameShellState.ts:24-25` still reads the tutorial-done/build-panel keys directly, bypassing `preferences.ts`/`getStorage()`. No behavioural bug found (all sites catch), but it weakens the single-source-of-truth rule from AGENTS.md §5.2.
6. `resetPreferencesCache` (preferences.ts:121) has no callers, so the juice-effects cache is never reset between sessions; harmless today (the only writer updates the cache), noted for completeness.
7. `resolveCombatLogKind`'s string heuristic exists for "saves logged before combatKind existed", but saveLoad rejects any other `_version` (documented beta save policy) and all current combat writers pass a kind, so that heuristic is effectively unreachable for current-version data; my finding 3 concerns the false positives it produces for non-combat entries, not its legacy purpose.

NOTES ON METHOD: no files were modified; verification was static (read + grep + a read-only PowerShell JSON consistency check over src/game/data). I did not run the test suite, so all findings are code-path arguments, each with the exact reachable call chain quoted above.

Per-file verdicts (read in full): dayCycle.ts — mostly sound constants/formulas; one unreachable-transition bug (finding 1); dead month/day branch in setHumanBirthFromAge is unreachable from all 5 call sites (entityFactory.ts:159/190, dayCycle.ts:375, humanLifecycle.ts:155, settlerInteractionActions.ts:128 all pass 3 args) and lines 360-382 duplicate what setHumanBirthFromAge already set. dayCycleClock.ts — no finding: TICKS_PER_DAY/TICKS_PER_HOUR, weekday, nextTickAtClockHour (handles fromTick===target), isNewCalendarDayTick (lastProcessedCalendarDay is persisted in saveLoad.ts:360/420, simPrep.ts:174, simDelta.ts:333/477) and isProductionTick all behave as documented; the `Math.max(1, Math.round(interval/TICKS_PER_DAY))` day quantisation is lossless for every current caller (all intervals are whole days: PRODUCTION_INTERVAL, EVENT_INTERVAL). residencyOccupancy.ts — no finding (occupancyMove's fromId===toId guard, residenceRoomFor's self-decrement, and the id-0 comment are all consistent with call sites; getResidenceCapacity's `level || 1` also absorbs undefined/NaN). residencyReconciliation.ts — findings 3-5. residencySelection.ts — finding 2; the scoring constants/ties are deterministic (id-ordered, stable sort) and `Math.abs(child.id*7919)%n` is used instead of Math.random, so no determinism defect; auditHousingSharingIssues/isUnnecessarilySharingHousing (lines 487-518) have no production or test caller (only the dayCycle.ts re-export) — unused exported audit helper, not reported as a finding. householdComposition.ts — no finding; collectOwnHousehold/collectFamilyMembers/getChildCustodian/isMinorChild match their comments, and no caller array is mutated (sort calls are on locally filtered copies). housingDiagnostics.ts — finding 6; also note collectHousingDiagnostics runs `state.entities.find` per occupant id inside a per-render memo in VillageTabPanel.tsx:34 (O(entities x occupants) per render) — performance only, no correctness claim, so not reported.

Unresolved / for a design decision: (1) `tickLayerRealtime.ts:117-122` calls `syncResidenceOccupants` on a full `aliveEntities` scan every tick while a Moon Howler is active, i.e. residence sync outside the assign cadence named in SIMULATION_AUTHORITY.md §3. I traced why it exists (moonHowler.ts:971/1025 sync only Human-typed entities, and tickLayerAssign.ts:31-35 syncs from byType[Human], so a settler in werewolf form is dropped from its residence occupants for one tick) and the daily layer's assignMissingResidences(aliveEntities) repairs it at day boundaries, so it looks like a deliberate exception rather than a defect — but it is a second scheduling site for the residence owner and worth a documented decision. (2) `tickLayerDaily` indirectly runs `assignMissingResidences` via leaderHouse.ts:119 and dailyPopulation.ts:124, a third cadence (daily) for a decision the authority table lists as assign-cadence; tickLayerDaily.ts:59 documents the leader-house case, dailyPopulation.ts:124 does not. Is this sanctioned 'daily maintenance'? (3) rebuildChildrenIds (residencyReconciliation.ts:50-53) uses truthy id checks (`if (child.motherId)`) while the rest of the residency code deliberately uses `!= null` for id 0 (residencyOccupancy.ts:31). It is only safe because worldGen.ts:691-695 always spawns grass first, so entity id 0 is grass and no living human can hold id 0; if the id allocator ever changes, motherId/fatherId 0 links would be silently dropped. (4) Housing capacity is not in SIMULATION_AUTHORITY.md §5, yet findings 3 and 6 both hinge on it being a real invariant rather than a diagnostics warning — worth stating explicitly in the contract.

Method notes: this was a read-only audit; no files were created, modified or deleted and no test/build command was run (running vitest would write cache artifacts), so every claim above is from static reading of the quoted lines plus grep-verified call sites. METHOD: every file was read in full (321/217/92/195/200/120/260/385 lines) and each function, including unexported helpers, was traced to its call sites with grep. No test in C:\Wilderfolk\tests references these eight modules by name (grep for stripTopology|stripJunction|stripBuild|adjacencyIndex|placementUtils|buildingRotation|buildingPlacementActions|buildingMaintenanceActions in tests/ = 0 matches), so nothing here is test-locked except the one item noted below.

ONE-LINE VERDICT PER FILE
- src/game/buildingPlacementActions.ts — one real logic error (footprint-clearing region vs the placement gate, finding 1) plus a second removal owner with no cap-aware refund (finding 2); startBuilding itself is otherwise sound (affordability checked before any deduction, unique/research/terrain/bounds order correct).
- src/game/buildingMaintenanceActions.ts — no cadence or ownership violation, and its own cleanup is complete for the fields it owns (homeBuildingId/residenceBuildingId/prison* chain, `totalBuildingsCompleted` matching the load-time recompute at saveLoad.ts:447, `unindexAdjacency` + `state.adjacency = undefined` which tests/demolition.adjacencyHydration.test.ts:58 deliberately locks in); gaps are the missing rival guard (finding 4) and the refund message (finding 7).
- src/game/buildingRotation.ts — no logic error in the functions themselves; the repo carries two different `BuildingRotation` types (`buildings.ts:79` = 0|90|180|270 for `Building['rotation']`, `buildingRotation.ts:4` = 0|90) and only 0/90 ever reach `createBuilding` because both callers normalize, so the 180/270 corner angles in `structures.ts` doc comment are latent, not live; Fence is missing from both metadata sets (finding 5).
- src/game/placementUtils.ts — clean. `canPlaceBuildingSnapshot` duplicates the domain gate in the same branch order and is currently equivalent to `getPlaceBuildingFailureReason` (the duplication is acknowledged in its comment at line 174); the flood-free tile indexing and the strict-inequality overlap test (edge-touching allowed) are correct; bridge/fishing branches are internally consistent with their comments.
- src/game/adjacencyIndex.ts — clean. Self-adjacency is correctly impossible by construction (Farm/Greenhouse are never in barnMap, the road query explicitly skips Roads, Store/Workshop are never in marketMap), the cell-radius scan cannot miss a source inside the radius (80*ceil(r/80) >= r), bucket/`idToCell`/`indexedIds` are all pruned, `rebuild` clears before inserting, and `syncAdjacency`'s early return for a never-completed non-source is correct. The only hazard is external (finding 2: a removal path that skips `unindexAdjacency`).
- src/game/stripBuild.ts — arithmetic clean (pitch>0 guard, `MAX_STRIP_SEGMENTS-1` + `<=` yields exactly 72 centres, direction preserved via stepDir, negative/zero drag collapses to one segment); its only issue is the `replacesBuildingId` field it advertises (finding 6).
- src/game/stripJunction.ts — classification arithmetic is sound for the shapes it is actually used on (road elbows/tees/crosses: worked through the L-corner case and `cornerRotationFromConnections` returns the matching 270/0/180 frames); two dead-code items (findings 8, 9). Worth noting: `detectBuildingJunction` is called only with family 'road' (renderer/buildings.ts:49), so the wall-junction path of this module — and `stripRender.drawProceduralWallJunction`/`drawProceduralWallCorner`/`cornerArms` — have no caller at all, which is also why `resolveWallStripPlan` never emits `junctionInfo`.
- src/game/stripTopology.ts — the wall-plan existing-piece skip is asymmetric (finding 3); `findEnclosedWallAreas` is sound in effect (the raw flat-index neighbour arithmetic at lines 335-343 can wrap at column 0/cols-1, but a wrap can only ever involve a border or blocked cell, and component cells can be neither, so it is unreachable rather than harmful).

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS (need an owner's decision, not a code fact I can settle)
1. Building anchor convention is not settled repo-wide and is the one thing that could flip finding 1's direction. `getBuildingCenter` (simulation/humanRelationships.ts:223-225), residencyOccupancy.ts:53, beautyGrid.ts:31, hotelStay.ts:224, hospitalCare.ts and ~100 other sites compute the centre as `building.x + building.width / 2`, and rivalEvents.ts:130 explicitly converts a camp centre to a top-left x (`rival.campX + slot.dx - config.width / 2`) — all of which imply building.x,y is TOP-LEFT. But the placement subsystem (placementUtils bounds/terrain/overlap, useCanvasInteractions.findBuildingAt:51-54, the build ghost at renderer/grid.ts:378-381 and the strip preview at grid.ts:335-336) treats it as the CENTRE, and MAP_EDGE_INSET's comment ('so sprites are not clipped') plus the centre-anchored sprite draw (spriteDrawing.ts:73) and centred procedural strip draw match that reading. Whichever is authoritative, finding 1 stands as an internal contradiction (a tree/terrain edit applied to a region the gate never validated), but the correct global fix is a design decision for the simulation owner.
2. `resolveRoadStripPlan` deliberately has no existing-piece skip, unlike the wall plan, so a road drag that crosses an existing road emits a piece on the occupied cell, the UI's all-segments-valid gate refuses the entire chain, and crossing/joining roads cannot be laid in one drag. `detectBuildingJunction`/`drawProceduralRoadJunction` exist to draw exactly those crossings, so this looks like a gap rather than intent — but it is a behaviour/design choice, so it is reported here rather than as a finding.
3. Is the wall corner/junction feature meant to be live? `stripJunction` computes it, `resolveWallStripPlan` discards it, and `stripRender`'s wall junction/corner renderers have no caller. Additionally, completed Fences are drawn by the `isDecorType` branch (renderer/buildings.ts:146) because `BUILDING_CONFIGS[Fence].decor === true` (buildings.ts:678), so `drawProceduralFence`/rotation is only ever used for ghosts and construction sites — a presentational inconsistency that follows from Fence being in `STRIP_BUILD_TYPES` (stripBuild.ts:14) while being configured as decor.
4. `placementUtils.isFootprintOnBuildableTerrain`'s fishing branch rejects RiverBank tiles (RiverBank is in UNBUILDABLE_TERRAIN but not WATER_TERRAIN, so the line-112 test reduces to 'RiverBank OR Mountains OR Snow') although the comment says only mountains/snow are refused and the building is described as a 'Riverside fishing post' — a dock can therefore never sit on the bank. This may be intended; it is recorded as a question.
5. `isBuildingTechUnlocked` requires BOTH `unlockedTechs.includes(id)` AND `node.researched`, while `notifyBuildingLocked` (research.ts:77) returns silently when only `unlockedTechs` contains the id. `syncResearchUnlocks` keeps the two in step for normal play, so the divergence is only reachable from a hand-edited/legacy save, where a click on a locked building would produce no feedback at all. Not reported as a finding because I could not show a reachable path.

VERDICT PER FILE
- src/game/pathfinding.ts — UNSOUND: two independent high-severity defects break path following (origin-seeking waypoint loop; double position integration), plus the sampling cap that can miss blocked tiles. The A* core itself (heap, octile heuristic, corner guard, path reconstruction) is correct and deterministic, and tests/pathfinding.test.ts only covers findPath/getPathGrid/lineCrossesBlocked, never steerWithPath.
- src/game/spatialGrid.ts — Mostly sound: swap-remove, insert/update, radial and rect bounds, reconciles, road index dedup (lastAvoidQueryId) and computeRoadLayoutStamp all check out. Two gaps: syncTreeGrid never reconciles, and a block of unused API.
- src/game/adaptiveSpatialQuery.ts — Sound; cost model and both routing paths agree with the grid helpers. No finding: only latent edge-case/perf notes below.
- src/game/spatialQueryMetrics.ts — Sound and internally consistent (category list is the single source of truth; flush/zero logic correct for the per-tick flush performed by gameTick.ts:71/270).
- src/game/scentGrid.ts — Sound: decay-then-deposit cadence is per-tick/realtime, values clamped to [0,255], NaN-tolerant sampling/reader, sidecar header indices match SCENT_HEADER_WORDS=6. No finding.
- src/game/simQueries.ts — Sound: resident/occupant index, naive vs grid query parity, and the grass/wildlife snapshot bookkeeping (absorbedEntityIds, bornAfterSnapshot, self-spawn subtraction) are consistent with their callers in tickLayerSystems/simulationEntities/dailyGrassEcology. No finding.
- src/game/beautyGrid.ts — Functionally correct (stamp falloff, clamps and test-locked behaviour verified numerically against tests/beauty.decor.test.ts), but the happiness input set and its save round-trip are both wrong.

UNRESOLVED / DESIGN QUESTIONS
1. syncTreeGrid: the fix depends on whether mid-game trees are supposed to exist at all. Today the only mid-game tree spawn, groupEvents.ts:1688-1693 (nature_boom), pushes its trees into `allAlive` + `entityById` only — never into `state.entities` — so those 15 trees are visible for one tick and then silently missing from the world and from `byType`. That is a cross-group defect (groupEvents/entityIndex, not A6) and it currently masks the tree-grid staleness. Whoever fixes nature_boom should add the reconcile line in the same change, otherwise newly spawned trees become invisible to every tree query.
2. Should `steerWithPath` own the integration at all? The JSDoc says it does, the two callers act as if it does not. I recommended reverting to velocity-only because that is the minimal edit that makes both existing callers correct; the alternative (keep the move, skip humanTick.ts:1467 for the 'path' branch and drop hotelStay.ts:234-235) touches more code and needs a caller-visible flag.
3. `EntitySpatialGrid.insert` (161) returns early for non-finite x/y WITHOUT removing the entity's previous cell entry, while `update` (183) only removes on `!alive`; `clampToMapBounds` (mapBounds.ts:17-20) does not guard NaN, and `validateInvariant` cannot detect a stale-in-place cell. So a single NaN position would leave the entity queryable in its old cell (dSq NaN passes `dSq > radiusSq`) and unflagged by the invariant checker. I found no reachable NaN source today, so I did not raise it as a finding — but insert/update are the wrong place to swallow it.
4. `forEachInArrayRadius` (adaptiveSpatialQuery.ts:42-67) lacks the `Number.isFinite(radius) / radius < 0` guard that `forEachInRadius` has. A NaN radius routes to the naive path (the cost model compares NaN < x = false) and then `dSq > NaN` is false for every entity, so the callback runs for the entire fallback array. No caller passes a non-finite radius today (all radii are constants), so this is latent only.
5. Perf-only, out of group but caused by my group's options builder: humanRelationships.ts:154/1303/1396 call `socialAdaptiveOptions('social', n, width ?? 0, height ?? 0)`. With worldWidth/worldHeight = 0 the model computes totalCells=1 and always chooses 'naive', so those social scans silently bypass `humanSocialGrid` and do an O(population) array scan per settler per SOCIAL_STAGGER tick. Correctness is unaffected (the predicate is applied in both paths).
6. Diagnostics: `getSpatialQueryReport` (spatialQueryMetrics.ts:182) divides session totals by `measuredTicks`, which is incremented only for ticks that had activity (128-146), so the printed "queries/tick" is an average over active ticks, not over elapsed ticks. Its only consumer is scripts/perf-all.ts, and `formatSpatialQueryReport` (224) / `getCurrentTickMetrics` (178) are unused anywhere — diagnostics-only, not raised as a finding.
7. pathfinding's module-level `gridCache`/`pathCache` are keyed on `seed|wallSignature|WxH`; the terrain tiles and the map preset are not part of the key, so two worlds with the same seed/size but a different preset (or any future terraforming) would reuse a stale blocked grid until the wall signature or dimensions change. The UI never passes a seed (App.tsx:892 uses a random one), so this needs an explicit `initGame({seed})`, which is why I left it out of the findings.
8. hotelStay.ts:232 builds its path cache key from rounded pixel coordinates, so the key changes almost every tick: A* (up to 6000 nodes) is re-run per visitor per tick and `pathCache` is cleared every 200 inserts, evicting the stable settler commute paths too. Performance only, no correctness claim, so not reported.
9. I verified against git history that the latest commit 349f49e added the two position-integration lines to steerWithPath (finding 2) and changed the lineCrossesBlocked step formula (finding 3); the origin-seeking waypoint loop (finding 1) and the non-reconciling syncTreeGrid predate that commit, and neither is locked in by any existing test (no test anywhere imports or exercises steerWithPath).

UNRESOLVED / NEEDS A DESIGN DECISION
1. Youth-love floor: SIMULATION_AUTHORITY §5 (14–17), README.md:158 and CHANGELOG.md:223 say 14, but the owner uses humanRelationships.ts:441 `YOUTH_LOVE_MIN_AGE = 12`. That owner file is outside this group; if 14 is authoritative, humanRelationships needs the fix and my finding 4 (collector gap) should land with it. Note `getYouthConceptionMultiplier` already returns 0 below 14, so only the link itself is affected.
2. Big-news ids: the robust fix needs a save-format decision — either persist the allocator (add a key to WORLD_STATE_SAVE_KEYS plus worker prep/delta and the worker-side sync) or switch to tick-scoped ids. Because `dismissedBigNewsIds` is never pruned (unbounded growth; compared element-wise on every UI patch through gameLoop.ts:110 `idsPatchChanged`), an id-collision-free scheme is preferable to keeping a growing busy set.
3. reproductionCooldown: confirm whether a 0–100 tick first-conception cooldown for factory-made humans is intended design or the unscaled legacy value. If intended, SPECIES_CONFIG[Human].reproductionCooldown is effectively dead and should be removed or documented.
4. beautyGrid: the beautyGrid module documents a deliberate daily rebuild, so stale-for-one-day may be accepted; it is only a defect if the cache is expected to be dropped wherever the other derived grids are (the invalidate function's doc says so).
5. Who owns Big News creation: `frontierCombat.ts:371-381 pushNews` (`id: raid_${state.tick}_${state.bigNews.length}`) and `groupEvents.ts:37-47 pushNews` (`id: ge_${++newsSeq}_${state.tick}`) duplicate simEffects.addBigNews's id scheme, 50-cap and createdAt handling. Not anchored in my files, and I could not construct a guaranteed id collision (groupEvents can't collide because tick is monotonic and the id embeds it; frontierCombat's id can repeat only if two of its pushes fire in one tick while the list is already at the 50-item cap — not demonstrated). Worth a follow-up in whichever group owns those files.
6. `allLivingHumans` (simulationEntities.ts:99) is documented as 'Living player humans' but returns every alive Human including visitor/rival/trade-caravan entities; its only caller (humanLifecycle.ts:171 rebuildChildrenIds) is faction-agnostic, so I could not show a behavioural failure and did not report it.

METHOD / LIMITS: read-only audit, no files created or modified, no commands other than `read`/`grep`/`glob` and a read-only `git log`. I did not run the test suite (a behaviour asserted by tests/simulation.invariants.test.ts, tests/humanLifecycle.test.ts and tests/settlerTraits.test.ts was treated as intended). Checks performed that produced no finding (recorded so they are not re-litigated): (a) every daily relationship call site (tryDailyConception, tryDailyAffairEncounter, tryDailyAffairGossip, tryDailyAmicableDivorce, tryDailyHumanMortality, trySchoolyardGossip, tryFormSchoolyardBond, creditChildSchoolDay, syncHumanAgeFromCalendar, flushRelationshipDiagnostics) has exactly one caller — humanTick — so no second owner exists; (b) isNewCalendarDayTick is read before gameTick's markCalendarDayProcessed, so the daily block cannot fire twice or be skipped on a normal tick; (c) reproductionCooldown is decremented per real tick only here (Humans are absent from WILDLIFE_TICK_TYPES, tickLayerSystems.ts:72-79), so it is not double-decremented, and the per-tick decrement matches REPRODUCTION_COOLDOWN_TICKS = ticksForDays(150); (d) the realtime affair path never writes affairPartnerId and never rolls a scandal for an unestablished pair (it requires hasAffairPartner(...) && entity.affairPartnerId === paramour.id, humanTick.ts:1010-1015), matching tests/affair.cadence.test.ts; exposure requires intimate === true and spouse presence (humanRelationships.ts:1076-1082); (e) all positional calls (tickHumanHunting, commuteHumanToBuilding, tryExposeCaughtAffairForPair, findCourtshipPartner, findClosestAdaptiveInRadius, tryDailyAffairEncounter/Gossip) match their signatures argument-for-argument; (f) every candidate/partner list predicate re-checks entity.alive, so a settler killed earlier in the loop cannot be selected later in the same pass; (g) the offscreen throttle (state.tick + id) % 24 never suppresses the daily block, which sits above the `active` gate, so no daily decision is lost for off-screen settlers; (h) no division-by-zero / NaN path found in the movement and leisure math (all `Math.hypot(...) || 1`, fract() guards non-finite, energy/velocity writes are clamped or bounded); (i) per-entity Maps (workersByWorkplace, schoolReserved) are tick-local and do not grow across ticks.

Verified-OK (no finding raised): (1) Layer cadence law holds — gameTick calls realtime every tick, systems when tick%4===0, assign when tick%18===0 (4x/day, 18 = 6*TICKS_PER_HOUR), daily when tick%72===0; 72 is divisible by 4 and 18, so the day boundary always includes a systems and an assign pulse, and isProductionTick (dayCycleClock.ts:79-89) always lands on a systems tick. (2) Year/day/hour arithmetic is consistent between dayCycle.ts and dayCycleClock.ts: the `prevCalendarDay > 0` guard (gameTick.ts:78-79, dailyWorldEvents.ts:221-222) correctly suppresses a double year increment when a world is reloaded at a tick that is an exact TICKS_PER_DAY multiple, dayInYear stays 0 for the whole day-360 boundary day, and markCalendarDayProcessed/isNewCalendarDayTick agree because lastProcessedCalendarDay is only advanced at the end of the boundary tick. (3) tickLayerSystems' multi-tick scaling is correct: flash/combatTicks/reproductionCooldown/animFrame/energy and the wander+breeding probabilities are all scaled by `step = WILDLIFE_LAYER_INTERVAL`, and winterPenalty/config.energyLossPerTick are per-tick values that are only multiplied once (no double scaling); updateResearch's per-pulse `PER_TICK_RATE_SCALE` (1/3) gives the same per-day total as the legacy cadence (18 pulses/day x 1/3 = 6). (4) gameTick's paused early-return cannot desync humanPopulation/wildlifeCounts/workingSettlers/idleSettlers/entityByType: it returns before any mutation, and computePopulationCounts/countWorkingAndIdleSettlers re-filter `alive` from allAlive, so dead entities left in allAlive cannot inflate counters. (5) I checked the `deathsThisTick = aliveEntities.length - (allAlive.length - newEntities.length)` undercount (gameTick.ts:250) and concluded it is harmless: the guard at line 257 also ORs `newEntities.length > 0`, and when newEntities is empty the expression equals the true death count, so the stale-byType path is not reachable — deliberately not reported.

Deliberately not reported (redundant/dead guards, not behaviour): tickLayerDaily.ts:51 `if (state.tick > 0)` can never be false on the gameTick path (daily requires tick%TICKS_PER_DAY===0 and tick is incremented first); dailyWorldEvents.ts:84 `state.tick % TICKS_PER_DAY === 0` is likewise always true when reached from tickLayerDaily.ts:81; and tickElectionPromises is called twice in the same tick (tickLayerDaily.ts:62 and dailyWorldEvents.ts:131) but is idempotent through its `evaluated` story flag, so it is not a double effect.

Unresolved design question: OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE has two incompatible readings — simFocus.ts:25 documents it as 'every N wildlife-layer calls' (8 calls = 32 ticks) while the human analogue OFFSCREEN_HUMAN_THROTTLE is expressed in ticks and locked by tests/dayCycle.cadence.test.ts:95-99 ('~8 clock hours' = 24 ticks). The fix for finding 1 preserves the documented 'layer calls' reading; if the intended value is really 8 ticks, the constant and its comment should be restated and the stagger made id-preserving.

Unresolved / design questions raised while tracing invariant writers:

1. Collector coverage. collectSimulationInvariantErrors is invoked only by gameTick's dev-only daily pulse (gameTick.ts:277-286) and by tests/fullYear.integration.test.ts at 90-day checkpoints. No ordinary test asserts it after worker command results, although simulationInvariants.ts:31 claims it is safe to run there. The §5 table does not say, but the workforce owner excludes pregnancy from jobs and from auto-crewed sites, so the manual builder command looks like the odd path out; either the check belongs in addToConstructionCrew (one rule) or the exclusion is only meant for jobs.

Legacy save migrations look unreachable, which affects one candidate finding I dropped: migrateTickTimeline (saveLoad.ts:236-252) scales entity `pregnancyProgress` but neither scales nor backfills `pregnancyDueProgress` (compare humanLifecycle.ts:64-66, where both are compared in the same absolute-tick units), and the load path (saveLoad.ts:393-408 + migrateEntityPersistedFields) never repairs a pregnant entity that lacks `pregnancyDueProgress`. If the version gate is temporary (the file still carries applySaveMigration records), both the missing `scaleField(rec, 'pregnancyDueProgress')` and a load-time backfill (`entity.pregnancyDueProgress = Math.round(PREGNANCY_TICKS * (0.85 + Math.random() * 0.3))` when `pregnant && pregnancyDueProgress == null`) should be added before that gate is lifted, otherwise the §5 'pregnant has a valid pregnancyDueProgress' invariant is false from load until birth.

Both partners stay mutually consistent but stale, so I did not raise it as an invariant finding; flagging it because it is the same field family as finding 4 if the catalog is meant to mirror sim state.
